Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Skill: Ubiquitous Language\n7\t\n8\t## Purpose\n9\t\n10\tDDD requires a shared vocabulary between domain experts and developers. This skill extracts and maintains that vocabulary for StockForge's Vietnamese stock market domain.\n11\t\n12\t## When to Use\n13\t\n14\t- Starting a new bounded context (one of 9 BCs)\n15\t- Processing conversation with domain expert about stock investing\n16\t- Reviewing conversation for undocumented terms\n17\t- Checking code for term drift from glossary\n18\t- Onboarding new contributor\n19\t\n20\t## When NOT to Use\n21\t\n22\t- Technical infrastructure (not domain-specific)\n23\t- External API integration (use their terminology)\n24\t- UI framework concerns (not DDD-relevant)\n25\t\n26\t## Relationship to /drill-me\n27\t\n28\t`/drill-me` is interactive — asks user questions, extracts language live.\n29\tThis skill is passive — analyzes existing content to find terms.\n30\t\n31\tUse both: `/drill-me` for new domains, this skill for ongoing maintenance.\n32\t\n33\t## Extraction Process\n34\t\n35\t### 1. Identify Candidates\n36\t\n37\tScan source (conversation, spec, interview transcript) for:\n38\t- **Domain nouns** (\"thesis\", \"KOL recommendation\", \"pump detection\", \"calibration\")\n39\t- **Domain verbs** (\"submit thesis\", \"extract recommendation\", \"detect pump phase\")\n40\t- **State names** (\"active\", \"incubating\", \"distributing\", \"dumped\")\n41\t- **Relationships** (\"KOL owns Channel\", \"Thesis references Catalysts\")\n42\t- **Rules** (\"Thesis can only be submitted when bear case is substantive\")\n43\t\n44\t### 2. Candidate Vetting\n45\t\n46\tFor each candidate, ask:\n47\t- Is this domain-specific or generic?\n48\t- Does it have a precise business meaning?\n49\t- Could a domain expert (Vietnamese investor) define it clearly?\n50\t- Is it already in glossary under different name?\n51\t\n52\tSkip generic terms (user, item, data) unless they have specific domain meaning.\n53\t\n54\t### 3. Definition Structure\n55\t\n56\tFor each accepted term:\n57\t\n58\t```markdown\n59\t### [Term Name]\n60\t\n61\t**Bounded context**: [which of 9 BCs owns this term]\n62\t\n63\t**Definition**: [Clear, specific definition — what it is, what it's for]\n64\t\n65\t**Lifecycle**: [If applicable — state transitions]\n66\t\n67\t**Not to confuse with**: [List of similar-but-different terms]\n68\t\n69\t**Code**: [file path if implemented, or \"not yet built\"]\n70\t\n71\t**Introduced**: [date, source conversation/spec]\n72\t```\n73\t\n74\t### 4. Drift Detection\n75\t\n76\tFor each term, scan codebase:\n77\t```bash\n78\tgrep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"\n79\t```\n80\t\n81\tFlag if:\n82\t- Code uses different name for same concept\n83\t- Multiple names exist for what should be one term\n84\t- Term defined in glossary but not used in code\n85\t\n86\t### 5. Conflict Resolution\n87\t\n88\tWhen conflicts arise:\n89\t- **Rename code to match glossary**: Most common. Glossary is canonical.\n90\t- **Update glossary to match code**: If code name is better, update glossary + add to drift-log.\n91\t- **Recognize two distinct concepts**: Sometimes what seemed synonymous is actually different. Define both distinctly.\n92\t\n93\t## Writing Good Definitions\n94\t\n95\t### Bad definition\n96\t```markdown\n97\t### Thesis\n98\t**Definition**: An analysis of a stock.\n99\t```\n100\tToo vague. Could be anything.\n101\t\n102\t### Good definition\n103\t```markdown\n104\t### Thesis\n105\t**Bounded context**: BC-8 Analysis & Thesis\n106\t**Definition**: A structured multi-perspective investment analysis for a specific stock\n107\t(Ticker). Must include both BullAnalysis and BearAnalysis (adversarial by design).\n108\tLifecycle ends in either PostMortem (if acted on) or Abandoned (if not).\n109\t**Lifecycle**: Draft → Active → [Closed | Abandoned] → PostMortem (optional)\n110\t**Not to confuse with**: \n111\t- ExtractedClaim (a factual claim from a source, not a thesis)\n112\t- KolRecommendation (a KOL's recommendation, input to thesis, not thesis itself)\n113\t- Analysis (generic term; our canonical term is Thesis for investment analyses)\n114\t```\n115\t\n116\t## Common Pitfalls\n117\t\n118\t### Term Explosion\n119\tDon't add every noun mentioned. Reserve glossary for terms with precise meaning.\n120\t\n121\t### Synonym Tolerance\n122\tDon't allow \"Recommendation\" and \"KolRecommendation\" for same thing. Pick one. Enforce.\n123\t\n124\t### Over-Abstraction\n125\t\"Signal\" as a glossary term is usually too generic in this context. Be specific (ExtractedClaim, KolRecommendation, SentimentScore).\n126\t\n127\t### Missing Lifecycle\n128\tMost domain entities have states. Document them.\n129\t\n130\t### No \"Not to Confuse With\"\n131\tIf term is easy to confuse with another, document the distinction explicitly.\n132\t\n133\t## Updating Glossary\n134\t\n135\tChanges to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` always include:\n136\t\n137\t1. Update the term definition\n138\t2. Append entry to `drift-log.md`:\n139\t\n140\t```markdown\n141\t## YYYY-MM-DD — [Add | Rename | Deprecate | Clarify] — [term]\n142\t\n143\t**Session**: [reference]\n144\t**Change**: [what changed]\n145\t**Rationale**: [why]\n146\t**Impact**: [files affected, if any]\n147\t```\n148\t\n149\t3. If renaming, add to \"Stop List\" in glossary.md:\n150\t\n151\t```markdown\n152\t| Do NOT use | USE instead |\n153\t|---|---|\n154\t| Analysis | Thesis (for investment analyses) |\n155\t| Recommendation | KolRecommendation |\n156\t| Signal | ExtractedClaim | SentimentScore (be specific) |\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\t## Output Format\n160\t\n161\tWhen extracting language from source:\n162\t\n163\t```markdown\n164\t# Ubiquitous Language Extraction — [source]\n165\t\n166\t## Date\n167\tYYYY-MM-DD\n168\t\n169\t## Source\n170\t[conversation ID, spec path, or interview transcript]\n171\t\n172\t## Candidate Terms Found ([N])\n173\t\n174\t### Accepted ([M])\n175\t\n176\t#### [Term 1]\n177\t[Full definition as above]\n178\t\n179\t#### [Term 2]\n180\t[Full definition]\n181\t\n182\t### Deferred ([K])\n183\t- [Term] — need more context from domain expert\n184\t- [Term] — overlap with existing, need clarification\n185\t\n186\t### Rejected ([L])\n187\t- [Term] — too generic\n188\t- [Term] — technical infrastructure, not domain\n189\t\n190\t## Conflicts Detected\n191\t- [Existing term] vs [candidate] — [resolution needed]\n192\t\n193\t## Next Steps\n194\t1. Review accepted terms with domain expert\n195\t2. Update glossary.md with accepted definitions\n196\t3. Run /ul-audit to find code drift\n197\t4. For deferred terms, schedule /drill-me session\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\t## Integration\n201\t\n202\t- `/drill-me` — interactive interview, this skill processes results\n203\t- `/ul-audit` — scans code against glossary, this skill drives definitions\n204\t- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — output target\n205\t- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` — change log\n206\t\n207\t## Attribution\n208\t\n209\tAdapted from mattpocock/skills (`ubiquitous-language`), MIT licensed.\n210\tCustomized for StockForge DDD workflow with 9 bounded contexts and Vietnamese stock domain.\n211\t"}]},"uuid":"5e4e31ea-0624-458e-a29f-eb9753150a45","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:09:12.562Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\ubiquitous-language\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: ubiquitous-language\ndescription: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. This skill extracts and maintains that vocabulary for StockForge's Vietnamese stock market domain.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Starting a new bounded context (one of 9 BCs)\n- Processing conversation with domain expert about stock investing\n- Reviewing conversation for undocumented terms\n- Checking code for term drift from glossary\n- Onboarding new contributor\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Technical infrastructure (not domain-specific)\n- External API integration (use their terminology)\n- UI framework concerns (not DDD-relevant)\n\n## Relationship to /drill-me\n\n`/drill-me` is interactive — asks user questions, extracts language live.\nThis skill is passive — analyzes existing content to find terms.\n\nUse both: `/drill-me` for new domains, this skill for ongoing maintenance.\n\n## Extraction Process\n\n### 1. Identify Candidates\n\nScan source (conversation, spec, interview transcript) for:\n- **Domain nouns** (\"thesis\", \"KOL recommendation\", \"pump detection\", \"calibration\")\n- **Domain verbs** (\"submit thesis\", \"extract recommendation\", \"detect pump phase\")\n- **State names** (\"active\", \"incubating\", \"distributing\", \"dumped\")\n- **Relationships** (\"KOL owns Channel\", \"Thesis references Catalysts\")\n- **Rules** (\"Thesis can only be submitted when bear case is substantive\")\n\n### 2. Candidate Vetting\n\nFor each candidate, ask:\n- Is this domain-specific or generic?\n- Does it have a precise business meaning?\n- Could a domain expert (Vietnamese investor) define it clearly?\n- Is it already in glossary under different name?\n\nSkip generic terms (user, item, data) unless they have specific domain meaning.\n\n### 3. Definition Structure\n\nFor each accepted term:\n\n```markdown\n### [Term Name]\n\n**Bounded context**: [which of 9 BCs owns this term]\n\n**Definition**: [Clear, specific definition — what it is, what it's for]\n\n**Lifecycle**: [If applicable — state transitions]\n\n**Not to confuse with**: [List of similar-but-different terms]\n\n**Code**: [file path if implemented, or \"not yet built\"]\n\n**Introduced**: [date, source conversation/spec]\n```\n\n### 4. Drift Detection\n\nFor each term, scan codebase:\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"\n```\n\nFlag if:\n- Code uses different name for same concept\n- Multiple names exist for what should be one term\n- Term defined in glossary but not used in code\n\n### 5. Conflict Resolution\n\nWhen conflicts arise:\n- **Rename code to match glossary**: Most common. Glossary is canonical.\n- **Update glossary to match code**: If code name is better, update glossary + add to drift-log.\n- **Recognize two distinct concepts**: Sometimes what seemed synonymous is actually different. Define both distinctly.\n\n## Writing Good Definitions\n\n### Bad definition\n```markdown\n### Thesis\n**Definition**: An analysis of a stock.\n```\nToo vague. Could be anything.\n\n### Good definition\n```markdown\n### Thesis\n**Bounded context**: BC-8 Analysis & Thesis\n**Definition**: A structured multi-perspective investment analysis for a specific stock\n(Ticker). Must include both BullAnalysis and BearAnalysis (adversarial by design).\nLifecycle ends in either PostMortem (if acted on) or Abandoned (if not).\n**Lifecycle**: Draft → Active → [Closed | Abandoned] → PostMortem (optional)\n**Not to confuse with**: \n- ExtractedClaim (a factual claim from a source, not a thesis)\n- KolRecommendation (a KOL's recommendation, input to thesis, not thesis itself)\n- Analysis (generic term; our canonical term is Thesis for investment analyses)\n```\n\n## Common Pitfalls\n\n### Term Explosion\nDon't add every noun mentioned. Reserve glossary for terms with precise meaning.\n\n### Synonym Tolerance\nDon't allow \"Recommendation\" and \"KolRecommendation\" for same thing. Pick one. Enforce.\n\n### Over-Abstraction\n\"Signal\" as a glossary term is usually too generic in this context. Be specific (ExtractedClaim, KolRecommendation, SentimentScore).\n\n### Missing Lifecycle\nMost domain entities have states. Document them.\n\n### No \"Not to Confuse With\"\nIf term is easy to confuse with another, document the distinction explicitly.\n\n## Updating Glossary\n\nChanges to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` always include:\n\n1. Review accepted terms with domain expert\n2. Update glossary.md with accepted definitions\n3. Run /ul-audit to find code drift\n4. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n---\n\n# Skill: Spec to Wiki Conversion\n\n## Purpose\n\nTransform raw spec file into Obsidian-optimized wiki entry that enables graph navigation and cross-referencing.\n\n## Core Rule\n\n- `specs/` = source of truth (raw format, free to edit)\n- `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/` = derived view (Obsidian format)\n- Raw changes → regenerate wiki (preserving human additions where possible)\n- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`** (project-wide constraint, see CLAUDE.md hard rules)\n\n## When to Use\n\n- New spec lands in `specs/` and has no wiki entry yet\n- Existing spec edited → wiki view drifts\n- Periodic vault audit catches missing wikilinks / stale frontmatter\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Quick draft notes (use `obsidian-vault/wiki/scratch/` instead)\n- Non-spec docs (use `obsidian-vault` skill for general note creation)\n\n## Process (7 steps)\n\n1. **Read raw spec completely** — frontmatter (spec_id/tier/status), Part A/B/C structure, all mentioned terms.\n2. **Identify linkable items** — glossary terms (`[[term]]`), spec cross-refs (`[[SPEC-...]]`), bounded contexts (`[[bc/...]]`), entity mentions (companies, tickers, KOLs).\n3. **Generate wiki file** at `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md` — see `references/wiki-template.md` for full frontmatter + body schema.\n4. **Apply wikilinks** — first mention only per doc; never inside code blocks; see `references/wikilink-rules.md`.\n5. **Create missing stubs** — for entities/concepts mentioned but no page; see `references/stub-template.md`.\n6. **Update index + log** — append to `obsidian-vault/wiki/_index.md` + `_log.md`; see `references/index-log-templates.md`.\n7. **Regeneration** when raw changes — diff-based update preserves human additions; see `references/regeneration.md`.\n\n## Wikilink Boundaries (concise)\n\n- ✅ First mention of glossary/spec/entity term in this doc\n- ✅ Cross-references between specs and bounded contexts\n- ❌ Inside ` ```code``` ` blocks\n- ❌ Subsequent mentions in same doc (link spam)\n- ❌ Generic terms not in glossary\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Wikilink inside code blocks\n- Linking every single mention (link pollution)\n- Overwriting wiki without diff-preserving human additions\n- Creating wikilinks to non-existent pages without stub\n- Skipping `_index.md` / `_log.md` updates\n\n## Do\n\n- First-mention linking per doc\n- Aggressive stub creation (empty stub > missing link)\n- Diff-based update to preserve human curation\n- Frontmatter consistent with `references/wiki-template.md` schema\n\n## Related\n\n- `obsidian-vault` — base Obsidian interactions\n- `spec-dual-layer` — understanding spec structure being converted\n- `ubiquitous-language` — glossary drives link candidates\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":15558,"cache_read_input_tokens":97528,"output_tokens":1958,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":15558,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1958,"cache_read_input_tokens":97528,"cache_creation_input_tokens":15558,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":15558},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYS3Sxp26g3MmAzm9zvJ","type":"assistant","uuid":"49ac3232-ae1b-4ff4-a720-91dd1ed36807","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:09:42.622Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n---\n\n# Skill: Spec to Wiki Conversion\n\n## Purpose\n\nTransform raw spec file into Obsidian-optimized wiki entry that enables graph navigation and cross-referencing.\n\n## Core Rule\n\n- `specs/` = source of truth (raw format, free to edit)\n- `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/` = derived view (Obsidian format)\n- Raw changes → regenerate wiki (preserving human additions where possible)\n- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`** (project-wide constraint, see CLAUDE.md hard rules)\n\n## When to Use\n\n- New spec lands in `specs/` and has no wiki entry yet\n- Existing spec edited → wiki view drifts\n- Periodic vault audit catches missing wikilinks / stale frontmatter\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Quick draft notes (use `obsidian-vault/wiki/scratch/` instead)\n- Non-spec docs (use `obsidian-vault` skill for general note creation)\n\n## Process (7 steps)\n\n1. **Read raw spec completely** — frontmatter (spec_id/tier/status), Part A/B/C structure, all mentioned terms.\n2. **Identify linkable items** — glossary terms (`[[term]]`), spec cross-refs (`[[SPEC-...]]`), bounded contexts (`[[bc/...]]`), entity mentions (companies, tickers, KOLs).\n3. **Generate wiki file** at `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md` — see `references/wiki-template.md` for full frontmatter + body schema.\n4. **Apply wikilinks** — first mention only per doc; never inside code blocks; see `references/wikilink-rules.md`.\n5. **Create missing stubs** — for entities/concepts mentioned but no page; see `references/stub-template.md`.\n6. **Update index + log** — append to `obsidian-vault/wiki/_index.md` + `_log.md`; see `references/index-log-templates.md`.\n7. **Regeneration** when raw changes — diff-based update preserves human additions; see `references/regeneration.md`.\n\n## Wikilink Boundaries (concise)\n\n- ✅ First mention of glossary/spec/entity term in this doc\n- ✅ Cross-references between specs and bounded contexts\n- ❌ Inside ` ```code``` ` blocks\n- ❌ Subsequent mentions in same doc (link spam)\n- ❌ Generic terms not in glossary\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Wikilink inside code blocks\n- Linking every single mention (link pollution)\n- Overwriting wiki without diff-preserving human additions\n- Creating wikilinks to non-existent pages without stub\n- Skipping `_index.md` / `_log.md` updates\n\n## Do\n\n- First-mention linking per doc\n- Aggressive stub creation (empty stub > missing link)\n- Diff-based update to preserve human curation\n- Frontmatter consistent with `references/wiki-template.md` schema\n\n## Related\n\n- `obsidian-vault` — base Obsidian interactions\n- `spec-dual-layer` — understanding spec structure being converted\n- `ubiquitous-language` — glossary drives link candidates\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":211,"newStart":14,"newLines":51,"lines":[" - `specs/` = source of truth (raw format, free to edit)"," - `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/` = derived view (Obsidian format)"," - Raw changes → regenerate wiki (preserving human additions where possible)","+- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`** (project-wide constraint, see CLAUDE.md hard rules)"," ","-## Process","+## When to Use"," ","-### 1. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n---\n\n# Skill: Spec to Wiki Conversion\n\n## Purpose\n\nTransform raw spec file into Obsidian-optimized wiki entry that enables graph navigation and cross-referencing.\n\n## Core Rule\n\n- `specs/` = source of truth (raw format, free to edit)\n- `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/` = derived view (Obsidian format)\n- Raw changes → regenerate wiki (preserving human additions where possible)\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Read Raw Spec Completely\n\nParse:\n- Frontmatter (spec_id, tier, status)\n- Part A, B, C structure\n- All mentioned terms and entities\n\n### 2. Identify Linkable Items\n\nScan for:\n\n**Glossary terms** (from `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`):\n- Every mention becomes `[[term-name]]`\n- Create stub if page doesn't exist\n\n**Spec cross-references**:\n- `SPEC-2026-04-001` → `[[SPEC-2026-04-001]]`\n\n**Bounded contexts**:\n- \"BC-6 Influence Network\" → `[[bc/influence]]`\n\n**Entity mentions**:\n- Company names, tickers, KOLs\n- Create stub pages in `obsidian-vault/wiki/entities/`\n\n### 3. Generate Wiki File\n\nTarget: `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md`\n\nStructure:\n\n```markdown\n---\ntype: spec\ntier: 2\nspec_id: SPEC-2026-04-001\nspec_slug: validate-investment-thesis\nstatus: draft\nversion: 1.0\ncreated: 2026-04-20\nlast_reviewed: 2026-04-20\nbounded_contexts:\n  - \"[[bc/analysis]]\"\n  - \"[[bc/portfolio]]\"\nrelated_specs: []\nubiquitous_language_terms:\n  - \"[[Thesis]]\"\n  - \"[[BearAnalysis]]\"\n  - \"[[Catalyst]]\"\nsource_raw: \"[../../../specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md]\"\ntags:\n  - spec\n  - tier2\n  - feature\n  - analysis\n---\n\n# [[SPEC-2026-04-001]] — Validate Investment Thesis\n\n> Wiki view of [[SPEC-2026-04-001]]. \n> Raw source: [../../../specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md](../../../specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md)\n\n## Navigation\n\n- [[#Part A — Business Specification]]\n- [[#Part B — Agent Contract]]\n- [[#Part C — Provenance & Review]]\n\n## Related Nodes\n\n- **Depends on**: [[bc/market-data]]\n- **Enables**: [[bc/portfolio]]\n- **Bounded contexts**: [[bc/analysis]], [[bc/portfolio]]\n- **Key terms**: [[Thesis]], [[BearAnalysis]], [[BullAnalysis]], [[Catalyst]]\n\n---\n\n[Full content of raw spec, with wikilinks applied]\n```\n\n### 4. Wikilink Application Rules\n\n**First mention of term in wiki doc**: add wikilink\n```markdown\nA [[Thesis]] is the structured investment analysis produced...\n```\n\n**Subsequent mentions in same doc**: plain text OK (avoid link spam)\n```markdown\nWhen thesis is submitted, the system emits ThesisSubmittedEvent...\n```\n\n**Code references**: don't wikilink inside code blocks\n```python\n# This is plain code — no wikilinks\nthesis = Thesis.create(ticker, bull, bear)\n```\n\n### 5. Create Missing Stubs\n\nFor mentioned entities/concepts without wiki page:\n\nStub at `obsidian-vault/wiki/entities/<slug>.md`:\n\n```markdown\n---\ntype: entity\nstatus: stub\nsource_mentions:\n  - \"[[SPEC-2026-04-001]]\"\ncreated: 2026-04-20\ntags:\n  - stub\n  - entity\n---\n\n# [[Entity Name]]\n\n> Stub page. Created because mentioned in [[SPEC-2026-04-001]]. \n> Please expand with context and connections.\n\n## Context\nFirst mentioned in context of: [brief description from where]\n\n## Properties\n- [Add structured info as known]\n\n## Relationships\n- Connected to: [list]\n\n## Backlinks\n*(Obsidian auto-populates)*\n```\n\n### 6. Update Index\n\nRead `obsidian-vault/wiki/_index.md`, append new entry:\n\n```markdown\n## Specs\n\n### Tier 2 (Feature)\n\n- [[specs/tier2-feature/SPEC-2026-04-001-validate-investment-thesis]]\n  - Status: draft\n  - BCs: [[bc/analysis]], [[bc/portfolio]]\n  - Created: 2026-04-20\n```\n\n### 7. Append to Log\n\n`obsidian-vault/wiki/_log.md`:\n\n```markdown\n## [2026-04-20] ingest | SPEC-2026-04-001\n\n**Type**: spec (tier 2)\n**Title**: Validate Investment Thesis\n**Raw source**: `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md`\n**Wiki entry**: `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier2-feature/SPEC-2026-04-001-validate-investment-thesis.md`\n**Stubs created**:\n- `wiki/entities/vcb.md`\n- `wiki/concepts/adversarial-analysis.md`\n**Existing links to**: [[Thesis]], [[BearAnalysis]], [[BullAnalysis]] (x6)\n```\n\n## Regeneration (Updating Existing Wiki)\n\nWhen raw spec changes and wiki already exists:\n\n### Diff-Based Update\n\n1. Read current wiki file\n2. Extract human additions:\n   - Extra wikilinks added manually\n   - Cross-references beyond what auto-extracted\n   - Comments / notes in wiki frontmatter\n3. Regenerate from raw\n4. Preserve human additions\n5. Update \"last_reviewed\" in frontmatter\n\n### Full Regeneration\n\nIf spec changes fundamentally:\n1. Move old wiki to `obsidian-vault/wiki/archive/<date>/`\n2. Generate fresh\n3. Note in _log.md: full regen + reason\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Wikilink inside code blocks\n- Link every single mention (link pollution)\n- Overwrite wiki without diff-preserving human additions\n- Create wikilinks to non-existent pages (always create stubs)\n- Skip index/log updates\n\n**Do**:\n- First-mention linking in each doc\n- Aggressive stub creation (easier to have empty stub than missing link)\n- Diff-based update to preserve human curation\n- Keep frontmatter consistent with schema\n\n## Related\n\n- `obsidian-vault` — base Obsidian interactions\n- `spec-dual-layer` — understanding spec structure being converted\n- `ubiquitous-language` — glossary drives link candidates\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"49ac3232-ae1b-4ff4-a720-91dd1ed36807","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"46fa66c7-653f-4b0f-9b8d-f106002c6075","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"e279392e-e863-4c7f-80f9-f55c4f2e7fe6","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:26:17.185Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"68669f80-d939-4074-9a40-f7b7d14f6d5a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_012gt5r3nrAmS75yBq9YhQhm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01DUbC8ejXL6TodH1yzULosx","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\PC\\.ccs\\instances\\nathanleewindy\\projects\\C--htdocs-stockforge\\memory\\bash_permission_pattern.md","content":"---\nname: Bash permission pattern requires explicit cmd:* form\ndescription: Claude Code's permission matcher does not treat Bash(*) as a wildcard for all commands; each command needs explicit Bash(<cmd>:*) entry. When user reports stuck permission prompts, add specific entries to .claude/settings.local.json instead of relying on Bash(*).\ntype: feedback\n---\n\nWhen the user is stuck on a permission prompt — especially via mobile remote control where accept-from-mobile may not propagate cleanly — proactively add the specific `Bash(<command>:*)` permission to `.claude/settings.local.json` (project-gitignored). Do NOT rely on `Bash(*)` as a catch-all; the matcher does not expand it that way.\n\n**Why:** 2026-04-30 user reported \"grant permission từ mobile qua remote control, accept, nhưng có vẻ không được. bị stuck. làm cho nó accept đi\" while running `mkdir -p .claude/skills/spec-to-wiki/references`. Existing `Bash(*)` entry did not match. Adding `Bash(mkdir:*)` resolved it immediately.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- When a routine shell tool (`mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `echo`, `test`, `touch`, `diff`, `awk`, `sed`, `head`, `tail`, `sort`, `uniq`, `tr`, `printf`, `for`, `if`, `while`, `bash`, `sh`) hits a stuck permission, add `Bash(<cmd>:*)` to `settings.local.json` allow list and retry — don't ask the user.\n- Keep `Bash(*)` in the list for legacy / fallback but treat it as decorative; the explicit `Bash(<cmd>:*)` entries are what actually pass.\n- Project-level `.claude/settings.json` deny rules still take precedence, so this does not bypass charter immutability protections.\n- Memory `wildcard_permissions_preference.md` already covers the high-level approach; this entry is the specific tactical pattern.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":264,"cache_read_input_tokens":123744,"output_tokens":1849,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":264,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1849,"cache_read_input_tokens":123744,"cache_creation_input_tokens":264,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":264},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYTYqv7RfLzBcbhfxJP9","type":"assistant","uuid":"43db65af-596f-4822-afd0-69c173eb29a7","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:29:28.348Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"71708cc7-41cc-4148-b54f-d6443eca2365","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_015GHSrC61no27eGnAdK2Xiz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SuLNqH6kxEKVxfdKhZzN7y","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\Users\\PC\\.ccs\\instances\\nathanleewindy\\projects\\C--htdocs-stockforge\\memory\\bash_permission_pattern.md","old_string":"**How to apply:**\n- When a routine shell tool (`mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `echo`, `test`, `touch`, `diff`, `awk`, `sed`, `head`, `tail`, `sort`, `uniq`, `tr`, `printf`, `for`, `if`, `while`, `bash`, `sh`) hits a stuck permission, add `Bash(<cmd>:*)` to `settings.local.json` allow list and retry — don't ask the user.\n- Keep `Bash(*)` in the list for legacy / fallback but treat it as decorative; the explicit `Bash(<cmd>:*)` entries are what actually pass.\n- Project-level `.claude/settings.json` deny rules still take precedence, so this does not bypass charter immutability protections.\n- Memory `wildcard_permissions_preference.md` already covers the high-level approach; this entry is the specific tactical pattern.","new_string":"**How to apply:**\n- When a routine shell tool (`mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `echo`, `test`, `touch`, `diff`, `awk`, `sed`, `head`, `tail`, `sort`, `uniq`, `tr`, `printf`, `for`, `if`, `while`, `bash`, `sh`) hits a stuck permission, add `Bash(<cmd>:*)` to `settings.local.json` allow list and retry — don't ask the user.\n- **Compound commands chained with `&&` / `;` / `|`** are matched as ONE full string, NOT per sub-command. So `Bash(mkdir:*)` does NOT cover `mkdir -p X && ls X && echo OK`. Either: (a) tách thành nhiều single Bash calls, hoặc (b) set `defaultMode: \"bypassPermissions\"` ở `.claude/settings.local.json`. Default to (a) — single-command calls are clearer and align with allowlist semantics; (b) is a sledgehammer reserved for stuck-on-mobile-remote moments.\n- Keep `Bash(*)` in the list for legacy / fallback but treat it as decorative; the explicit `Bash(<cmd>:*)` entries are what actually pass.\n- Project-level `.claude/settings.json` deny rules still take precedence, so this does not bypass charter immutability protections.\n- Memory `wildcard_permissions_preference.md` already covers the high-level approach; this entry is the specific tactical pattern."},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1228,"cache_read_input_tokens":127628,"output_tokens":1688,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1228,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1688,"cache_read_input_tokens":127628,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1228,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1228},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYTcut6GS4HSijQjxb2u","type":"assistant","uuid":"dfa97546-2980-43fc-a7ec-3e8810b3b3da","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:30:09.718Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

When user reports stuck permission prompts, add specific entries to .claude/settings.local.json instead of relying on Bash(*).\ntype: feedback\noriginSessionId: 302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd\n---\nWhen the user is stuck on a permission prompt — especially via mobile remote control where accept-from-mobile may not propagate cleanly — proactively add the specific `Bash(<command>:*)` permission to `.claude/settings.local.json` (project-gitignored). Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n---\n\n# Skill: Spec to Wiki Conversion\n\n## Purpose\n\nTransform raw spec file into Obsidian-optimized wiki entry that enables graph navigation and cross-referencing.\n\n## Core Rule\n\n- `specs/` = source of truth (raw format, free to edit)\n- `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/` = derived view (Obsidian format)\n- Raw changes → regenerate wiki (preserving human additions where possible)\n- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`** (project-wide constraint, see CLAUDE.md hard rules)\n\n## When to Use\n\n- New spec lands in `specs/` and has no wiki entry yet\n- Existing spec edited → wiki view drifts\n- Periodic vault audit catches missing wikilinks / stale frontmatter\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Quick draft notes (use `obsidian-vault/wiki/scratch/` instead)\n- Non-spec docs (use `obsidian-vault` skill for general note creation)\n\n## Process (7 steps)\n\n1. **Read raw spec completely** — frontmatter (spec_id/tier/status), Part A/B/C structure, all mentioned terms.\n2. **Identify linkable items** — glossary terms (`[[term]]`), spec cross-refs (`[[SPEC-...]]`), bounded contexts (`[[bc/...]]`), entity mentions (companies, tickers, KOLs).\n3. **Generate wiki file** at `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md` — see `references/wiki-template.md` for full frontmatter + body schema.\n4. **Apply wikilinks** — first mention only per doc; never inside code blocks; see `references/wikilink-rules.md`.\n5. **Create missing stubs** — for entities/concepts mentioned but no page; see `references/stub-template.md`.\n6. **Update index + log** — append to `obsidian-vault/wiki/_index.md` + `_log.md`; see `references/index-log-templates.md`.\n7. **Regeneration** when raw changes — diff-based update preserves human additions; see `references/regeneration.md`.\n\n## Wikilink Boundaries (concise)\n\n- ✅ First mention of glossary/spec/entity term in this doc\n- ✅ Cross-references between specs and bounded contexts\n- ❌ Inside ` ```code``` ` blocks\n- ❌ Subsequent mentions in same doc (link spam)\n- ❌ Generic terms not in glossary\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Wikilink inside code blocks\n- Linking every single mention (link pollution)\n- Overwriting wiki without diff-preserving human additions\n- Creating wikilinks to non-existent pages without stub\n- Skipping `_index.md` / `_log.md` updates\n\n## Do\n\n- First-mention linking per doc\n- Aggressive stub creation (empty stub > missing link)\n- Diff-based update to preserve human curation\n- Frontmatter consistent with `references/wiki-template.md` schema\n\n## Related\n\n- `obsidian-vault` — base Obsidian interactions\n- `spec-dual-layer` — understanding spec structure being converted\n- `ubiquitous-language` — glossary drives link candidates\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":31,"oldLines":11,"newStart":31,"newLines":11,"lines":[" "," 1. **Read raw spec completely** — frontmatter (spec_id/tier/status), Part A/B/C structure, all mentioned terms."," 2. **Identify linkable items** — glossary terms (`[[term]]`), spec cross-refs (`[[SPEC-...]]`), bounded contexts (`[[bc/...]]`), entity mentions (companies, tickers, KOLs).","-3. **Generate wiki file** at `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md` — see `references/wiki-template.md` for full frontmatter + body schema.","-4. **Apply wikilinks** — first mention only per doc; see `references/index-log-templates.md`.","-7. **Regeneration** when raw changes — diff-based update preserves human additions; see `references/regeneration.md`.","+3. **Generate wiki file** at `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier<N>-<type>/<spec_id>-<slug>.md` — see `references/templates.md` § Wiki File for full frontmatter + body schema.","+4. **Apply wikilinks** — first mention only per doc; see `references/templates.md` § Index & Log.","+7. **Regeneration** when raw changes — diff-based update preserves human additions; see `references/templates.md` § Regeneration."," "," ## Wikilink Boundaries (concise)"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6501a293-f77b-4e8e-aa8f-7f5ad4f9ed5d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

spec\n  - tier2\n  - feature\n  - analysis\n---\n\n# [[SPEC-2026-04-001]] — Validate Investment Thesis\n\n> Wiki view of [[SPEC-2026-04-001]].\n> Raw source: [../../../specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md](../../../specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md)\n\n## Navigation\n\n- [[#Part A — Business Specification]]\n- [[#Part B — Agent Contract]]\n- [[#Part C — Provenance & Review]]\n\n## Related Nodes\n\n- **Depends on**: [[bc/market-data]]\n- **Enables**: [[bc/portfolio]]\n- **Bounded contexts**: [[bc/analysis]], [[bc/portfolio]]\n- **Key terms**: [[Thesis]], [[BearAnalysis]], [[BullAnalysis]], [[Catalyst]]\n\n---\n\n[Full content of raw spec, with wikilinks applied]\n```\n\n## Wikilink Rules\n\n**First mention of term in wiki doc**: add wikilink\n\n```markdown\nA [[Thesis]] is the structured investment analysis produced...\n```\n\n**Subsequent mentions in same doc**: plain text OK (avoid link spam)\n\n```markdown\nWhen thesis is submitted, the system emits ThesisSubmittedEvent...\n```\n\n**Code references**: don't wikilink inside code blocks\n\n```python\n# This is plain code — no wikilinks\nthesis = Thesis.create(ticker, bull, bear)\n```\n\n## Stub Template\n\nFor mentioned entities/concepts without wiki page, create at `obsidian-vault/wiki/entities/<slug>.md`:\n\n```markdown\n---\ntype: entity\nstatus: stub\nsource_mentions:\n  - \"[[SPEC-2026-04-001]]\"\ncreated: 2026-04-20\ntags:\n  - stub\n  - entity\n---\n\n# [[Entity Name]]\n\n> Stub page. Created because mentioned in [[SPEC-2026-04-001]].\n> Please expand with context and connections.\n\n## Context\nFirst mentioned in context of: [brief description from where]\n\n## Properties\n- [Add structured info as known]\n\n## Relationships\n- Connected to: [list]\n\n## Backlinks\n*(Obsidian auto-populates)*\n```\n\n## Index & Log\n\nAppend to `obsidian-vault/wiki/_index.md`:\n\n```markdown\n## Specs\n\n### Tier 2 (Feature)\n\n- [[specs/tier2-feature/SPEC-2026-04-001-validate-investment-thesis]]\n  - Status: draft\n  - BCs: [[bc/analysis]], [[bc/portfolio]]\n  - Created: 2026-04-20\n```\n\nAppend to `obsidian-vault/wiki/_log.md`:\n\n```markdown\n## [2026-04-20] ingest | SPEC-2026-04-001\n\n**Type**: spec (tier 2)\n**Title**: Validate Investment Thesis\n**Raw source**: `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md`\n**Wiki entry**: `obsidian-vault/wiki/specs/tier2-feature/SPEC-2026-04-001-validate-investment-thesis.md`\n**Stubs created**:\n- `wiki/entities/vcb.md`\n- `wiki/concepts/adversarial-analysis.md`\n**Existing links to**: [[Thesis]], [[BearAnalysis]], [[BullAnalysis]] (x6)\n```\n\n## Regeneration\n\nWhen raw spec changes and wiki already exists:\n\n### Diff-based update\n\n1. Read current wiki file\n2. Extract human additions:\n   - Extra wikilinks added manually\n   - Cross-references beyond what auto-extracted\n   - Comments / notes in wiki frontmatter\n3. Regenerate from raw\n4. Preserve human additions\n5. Update `last_reviewed` in frontmatter\n\n### Full regeneration\n\nIf spec changes fundamentally:\n1. Move old wiki to `obsidian-vault/wiki/archive/<date>/`\n2. Generate fresh\n3. {"parentUuid":"4385e651-edb9-4240-8bdc-d800f6cf3edf","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"7ea3ae10-5720-48a4-9af4-c134b5744368","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:31:56.269Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"a10c958b-56cd-4024-83f7-302c10784975","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01792Cja36CSr33dprzzjrJJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Huh5eW54A12tWAVZnxNwML","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\crawler-reliability\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: crawler-reliability\ndescription: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n---\n\n# Skill: Crawler Reliability\n\n## Purpose\n\nWeb scrapers have silent-break failure mode: selector looks right, passes tests, breaks in production when site updates. This skill minimizes that risk.\n\n## Core Principles\n\n1. **Verify selector against live DOM before committing** (VBW for scrapers)\n2. **Retry with exponential backoff, but with budget cap**\n3. **Monitor for silent break** (output shape changes session-over-session)\n4. **Respect rate limits and robots.txt**\n5. **Cache aggressively** — fetch once, parse many\n\n## Stack\n\n| Concern | Tool |\n|---|---|\n| Dynamic sites | Playwright (headless Chromium) |\n| Static APIs | httpx / aiohttp |\n| Retry logic | tenacity |\n| Cache | Redis |\n| YouTube transcript | yt-dlp |\n| Raw content store | Cloudflare R2 |\n\n## Selector Robustness\n\n**Prefer (in order):** `data-testid` / `aria-label` / `itemprop` > nearby-text + relationship locator > class selector > nth-child positional. Positional selectors break on DOM reshuffle — never use them as primary.\n\n**Fallback chain pattern**: try multiple strategies, return first non-empty result, log warning if all fail and return None. Don't raise — partial output beats whole-pipeline halt.\n\n## VBW for Scrapers\n\nBefore writing any selector:\n\n1. Fetch live HTML once: `curl URL > sample.html`\n2. Open in browser, inspect actual DOM\n3. Identify stable selectors (testid / aria / itemprop)\n4. Write selector based on actual DOM, not assumed structure\n\nThis is VBW Protocol applied to scrapers. Critical — selectors written from memory are top failure mode.\n\n## Retry & Backoff\n\nUse `tenacity`: `stop_after_attempt(5)` + `wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30)` + `retry_if_exception_type((HTTPError, TimeoutException))`. Treat `429 Too Many Requests` as retryable; `4xx` other than 429 is NOT retryable (won't fix itself). Always cap total retry budget.\n\n## Rate Limiting\n\nPer-domain token bucket via `asyncio.Semaphore`. Default: 10 calls/min/domain. Adjust per site terms — CafeF is more lenient than VietnamBiz. Always sleep at least `60 / cpm` between calls. Wrap fetch in `polite_fetch(url)` that acquires semaphore first.\n\n## Monitoring for Silent Break\n\nEvery crawler emits shape metrics per run:\n\n- `article_count` (alert if 0 — likely DOM change)\n- `with_title`, `with_url`, `with_published_at` (per-field success rate)\n- Field success rate < 50% triggers warning log\n\nPersist to `agent-workspace/calibration/crawler-shape/<source>.tsv` for session-over-session comparison.\n\n## Caching Pattern\n\nKey: `crawl:<sha256(url)>`. Use Redis `SETEX` with TTL:\n\n| Content | TTL |\n|---|---|\n| News listings | 1-6 hours |\n| Article detail | 24-72 hours |\n| Static (about pages) | 7 days |\n| Market data | 5-15 min OR don't cache |\n\n## Storage\n\nRaw HTML → Cloudflare R2 at `raw-crawl/<domain>/<date>/<sha256(url)>.html` with metadata: `url`, `fetched_at`, `status_code`. Parsed structure → Postgres. Raw preserved for reprocessing when extraction logic improves.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Writing selectors from memory (\"all CafeF pages have `.article-content`\")\n- Skipping retry (\"it'll work, we tested it\")\n- Fetching in tight loops without rate limiting (gets IP banned)\n- Ignoring status codes (500 != 200)\n- Committing scraped data without `source_url` (violates I-S2 citation rule)\n\n## Do\n\n- Verify against live DOM via VBW\n- Retry with exponential backoff + budget cap\n- Rate limit per domain\n- Monitor shape metrics over time\n- Cache aggressively with reasonable TTL\n- Preserve raw content in R2 for reprocessing\n\n## Related\n\n- `evidence-extraction` — parsing crawled content into claims\n- `prompt-engineering` — LLM extraction from raw HTML\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/financial-data-protocol.md` — citation rules (I-S2)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10031,"cache_read_input_tokens":131466,"output_tokens":3327,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":10031,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":3327,"cache_read_input_tokens":131466,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10031,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":10031},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYTmyJE5WptXfEbUdsrH","type":"assistant","uuid":"4c2404c4-5795-451d-a984-6670a84fa9c4","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:32:49.273Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n---\n\n# Skill: Crawler Reliability\n\n## Purpose\n\nWeb scrapers have silent-break failure mode. Selector looks right, passes tests, breaks in production when site updates. This skill minimizes that risk.\n\n## Core Principles\n\n1. **Verify selector against live DOM before committing**\n2. **Retry with backoff, but with budget cap**\n3. **Monitor for silent break (output shape changes)**\n4. **Respect rate limits and robots.txt**\n5. **Cache aggressively — fetch once, parse many**\n\n## Stack\n\n- **Playwright** (headless Chromium) for dynamic sites\n- **httpx** or **aiohttp** for static APIs\n- **tenacity** for retry logic\n- **Redis** for caching fetched pages\n- **yt-dlp** for YouTube transcripts\n- **Cloudflare R2** for raw content storage\n\n## Selector Robustness\n\n### Bad (fragile)\n```python\nprice = await page.text_content('.product-card > div:nth-child(2) > span.price')\n# Breaks when site reshuffles DOM\n```\n\n### Good (robust)\n```python\n# Prefer stable attributes\nprice = await page.text_content('[data-testid=\"stock-price\"]')\n\n# Or aria-label\nprice = await page.text_content('[aria-label=\"Stock price\"]')\n\n# Or nearby text + relationship\nprice_el = await page.locator('text=\"Giá:\"').locator('+ span').text_content()\n```\n\n### Fallback chain\n```python\nasync def extract_price(page) -> str | None:\n    strategies = [\n        lambda: page.text_content('[data-testid=\"price\"]'),\n        lambda: page.text_content('[itemprop=\"price\"]'),\n        lambda: page.locator('text=/[\\\\d,]+đ/').first().text_content(),\n    ]\n    \n    for strategy in strategies:\n        try:\n            result = await strategy()\n            if result:\n                return result\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n    \n    # All failed — log and return None\n    logger.warning('All price selectors failed', url=page.url)\n    return None\n```\n\n## VBW for Scrapers\n\n**Before** writing scraper selector:\n1. Fetch live HTML: `curl URL > sample.html`\n2. Open in browser\n3. Inspect actual DOM\n4. Identify stable selectors\n5. Write selector based on ACTUAL DOM, not assumed structure\n\nThis is VBW Protocol applied to scrapers. Critical.\n\n## Retry & Backoff (tenacity)\n\n```python\nfrom tenacity import retry, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential, retry_if_exception_type\nimport httpx\n\n@retry(\n    stop=stop_after_attempt(5),\n    wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=1, max=30),\n    retry=retry_if_exception_type((httpx.HTTPError, httpx.TimeoutException)),\n)\nasync def fetch_with_retry(url: str) -> str:\n    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:\n        response = await client.get(url, timeout=30)\n        \n        if response.status_code == 429:\n            raise httpx.HTTPStatusError(\"Rate limited\", request=response.request, response=response)\n        \n        response.raise_for_status()\n        return response.text\n```\n\n## Rate Limiting\n\nRespect the site. Use token bucket per domain:\n\n```python\nimport asyncio\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nclass RateLimiter:\n    def __init__(self, calls_per_minute: int = 10):\n        self._semaphores: dict[str, asyncio.Semaphore] = defaultdict(\n            lambda: asyncio.Semaphore(calls_per_minute)\n        )\n    \n    async def acquire(self, domain: str) -> None:\n        async with self._semaphores[domain]:\n            await asyncio.sleep(60 / 10)  # simple approach\n\nrate_limiter = RateLimiter(calls_per_minute=10)\n\nasync def polite_fetch(url: str) -> str:\n    from urllib.parse import urlparse\n    domain = urlparse(url).netloc\n    await rate_limiter.acquire(domain)\n    return await fetch_with_retry(url)\n```\n\n## Monitoring for Silent Break\n\nEvery crawler should emit shape metrics:\n\n```python\nasync def crawl_news_listing(query: str) -> list[dict]:\n    articles = await extract_articles(page)\n    \n    # Emit shape metrics\n    logger.info(\"Crawl shape\", \n        query=query,\n        article_count=len(articles),\n        with_title=sum(1 for a in articles if a.get(\"title\")),\n        with_url=sum(1 for a in articles if a.get(\"url\")),\n        with_published_at=sum(1 for a in articles if a.get(\"published_at\")),\n    )\n    \n    # Alert if anomalous\n    if len(articles) == 0:\n        logger.error(\"Crawler returned zero articles\", query=query)\n    \n    if sum(1 for a in articles if a.get(\"url\")) / max(len(articles), 1) < 0.5:\n        logger.warning(\"URL extraction rate dropped below 50%\", query=query)\n    \n    return articles\n```\n\n## Caching Pattern\n\n```python\nimport hashlib\nimport redis.asyncio as redis\n\nasync def fetch_cached(url: str, ttl_sec: int = 3600) -> str:\n    key = f\"crawl:{hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).hexdigest()}\"\n    \n    cached = await redis_client.get(key)\n    if cached:\n        logger.debug(\"Cache hit\", url=url)\n        return cached.decode()\n    \n    content = await polite_fetch(url)\n    await redis_client.setex(key, ttl_sec, content)\n    return content\n```\n\nTTL guidance:\n- News listings: 1-6 hours\n- Article detail: 24-72 hours\n- Static content (about pages): 7 days\n- Market data: don't cache or very short TTL (5-15 min)\n\n## Storage\n\nRaw crawled pages → Cloudflare R2:\n```python\nimport boto3\n\ns3 = boto3.client(\"s3\", endpoint_url=R2_ENDPOINT)\n\ns3.put_object(\n    Bucket=\"stockforge-raw\",\n    Key=f\"raw-crawl/{domain}/{date}/{url_hash}.html\",\n    Body=content.encode(),\n    Metadata={\n        \"url\": url,\n        \"fetched_at\": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),\n        \"status_code\": str(response.status_code),\n    },\n)\n```\n\nParsed structure → Postgres. Raw preserved for reprocessing.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Write selectors from memory (\"all CafeF pages have `.article-content`\")\n- Skip retry (\"it'll work, we tested it\")\n- Fetch in tight loops without rate limiting (get IP banned)\n- Ignore status codes (500 != 200)\n- Commit scraped data without source_url (violates I-1)\n\n**Do**:\n- Verify against live DOM\n- Retry with exponential backoff + budget cap\n- Rate limit per domain\n- Monitor shape metrics over time\n- Cache aggressively with reasonable TTL\n- Preserve raw content in R2 for reprocessing\n\n## Related\n\n- `evidence-extraction` — parsing crawled content into claims\n- `prompt-engineering` — LLM extraction from raw HTML\n- `constitution/invariants.md` — I-1 (source_url required)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4c2404c4-5795-451d-a984-6670a84fa9c4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
