{"parentUuid":"fbb33de1-b244-4dc2-b2c6-9af4f11b5041","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"545f3404-4b54-44f6-aace-cc088a2584fa","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:32:50.281Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"e7f574e7-d161-4c9c-90fa-bc4978b7b9f5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_013tzrynNKF49t4zSGouKQiq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017tc588ww4KCXXcCUfMLUT8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\fastapi-module\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: fastapi-module\ndescription: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n---\n\n# Skill: FastAPI Module\n\n## Purpose\n\nConsistent FastAPI router structure across StockForge's HTTP gateway (Phase 2+).\n\n> Phase 1 uses Streamlit for the personal dashboard. FastAPI is for Phase 2+ public API or when a proper HTTP interface is needed for workers.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Creating a new HTTP endpoint or adding routes\n- Wiring dependency injection / Pydantic DTOs\n- Setting up router-level test scaffolding\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Phase 1 work (use Streamlit directly)\n- Domain layer logic (use `ddd-tactical-patterns` skill — domain has zero framework dependency)\n\n## Module Layout\n\n```\napps/api/<bc_name>/\n├── routers/<resource>_router.py    # one router per resource\n└── dto/<resource>_dto.py            # Pydantic Request/Response + Mapper\npackages/application/<bc_name>/use_cases/<verb>_<resource>_use_case.py\npackages/domain/<bc_name>/repositories/<resource>_repository.py     # Protocol port\npackages/infrastructure/<bc_name>/persistence/<resource>_postgres_repository.py  # adapter\n```\n\n## Naming Conventions\n\n| Type | Pattern | Example |\n|---|---|---|\n| Router | `<resource>_router.py` | `theses_router.py` |\n| DTO request | `<Action><Resource>Request` | `CreateThesisRequest` |\n| DTO response | `<Resource>Response` | `ThesisResponse` |\n| Use case | `<Verb><Resource>UseCase` | `ValidateThesisUseCase` |\n| Mapper | `<Resource>Mapper` | `ThesisMapper` |\n\n## Router Template (skeleton)\n\n```python\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/theses\", tags=[\"analysis\"])\n\ndef get_validate_thesis_use_case(\n    db: Annotated[DatabaseClient, Depends(get_db)],\n    event_bus: Annotated[EventBus, Depends(get_event_bus)],\n) -> ValidateThesisUseCase:\n    return ValidateThesisUseCase(\n        thesis_repo=ThesisPostgresRepository(db),\n        event_bus=event_bus,\n    )\n\n@router.post(\"/\", response_model=ThesisResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)\nasync def create_thesis(\n    request: CreateThesisRequest,\n    use_case: Annotated[ValidateThesisUseCase, Depends(get_validate_thesis_use_case)],\n) -> ThesisResponse:\n    result = await use_case.execute(\n        ticker=request.ticker,\n        bull_case_text=request.bull_case,\n        bear_case_text=request.bear_case,\n    )\n    return ThesisMapper.to_response(result)\n```\n\n## DTO + Mapper Rules (Pydantic v2 — interfaces layer ONLY)\n\n- **Request**: `BaseModel` + `@field_validator` for normalization (`ticker.strip().upper()`) and substantive-content checks (e.g., bear case ≥50 chars per I-S10).\n- **Response**: `BaseModel` with primitive types (`str`, `int`, `datetime` → ISO string). No domain objects exposed.\n- **Mapper**: static `to_response(domain_obj) -> ResponseDTO`. Mapping happens at boundary, not in use case.\n\n## Port + Adapter\n\n- **Port** (`Protocol` in `packages/domain/<bc>/repositories/`): defines async interface (`save`, `find_by_id`).\n- **Adapter** (in `packages/infrastructure/<bc>/persistence/`): concrete implementation injected at router DI.\n\nNever skip the Protocol indirection — it's what enables fakes in tests + swap of persistence later.\n\n## App Factory\n\n`apps/api/main.py`: `create_app()` returns `FastAPI` configured with title/version, then `app.include_router(<bc>_router, prefix=\"/api/v1\")` per BC.\n\n## Testing Setup\n\nUse `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` + `app.dependency_overrides[get_<x>_use_case] = lambda: mock_use_case` for per-test injection. Mock `AsyncMock(spec=UseCase)`. Assert HTTP status + that `mock_use_case.execute.assert_called_once()`.\n\n## Router Boundary Rules\n\n- **Never import** another BC's router module directly\n- **Never import** `packages/domain/<otherBc>/` from this router\n- Cross-BC integration goes via: domain events (publish/subscribe), HTTP calls if service boundary required, or shared kernel (`packages/contracts/`)\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Business logic in routers (use cases own it)\n- Importing repositories directly in routers (use case mediates)\n- Pydantic models in domain layer (domain uses dataclasses)\n- Mixing use cases from multiple BCs in one router\n- Skipping Protocol/port for \"simple\" repos\n\n## Do\n\n- One router per BC resource\n- Thin routers, thick use cases\n- Protocol/adapter everywhere for testability\n- Pydantic DTOs at HTTP boundary only\n- Validate inputs at DTO level\n\n## Related\n\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — domain models this router consumes\n- `postgres-pgvector` — repository implementation patterns\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":44,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8145,"cache_read_input_tokens":141497,"output_tokens":2599,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8145,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":44,"output_tokens":2599,"cache_read_input_tokens":141497,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8145,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8145},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYTqwrmanJzcwmZ1jPV1","type":"assistant","uuid":"c9203e5e-1707-4fe7-9db7-9b3edb371ea7","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:33:24.740Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Thin routers, thick use cases"," - Protocol/adapter everywhere for testability"," - Pydantic DTOs at HTTP boundary only"]},{"oldStart":221,"oldLines":5,"newStart":118,"newLines":5,"lines":[" "," ## Related"," ","-- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — for domain models this router uses","-- `postgres-pgvector` — for repository implementations","+- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — domain models this router consumes","+- `postgres-pgvector` — repository implementation patterns"]}],"originalFile":"---\nname: fastapi-module\ndescription: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n---\n\n# Skill: FastAPI Module\n\n## Purpose\n\nConsistent FastAPI router structure across StockForge's HTTP gateway (Phase 2+).\n\nNote: Phase 1 uses Streamlit for the personal dashboard. FastAPI is for Phase 2+ public API or when a proper HTTP interface is needed for workers.\n\n## Router Template\n\n```python\n# apps/api/<bc_name>/routers/<resource>_router.py\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nfrom apps.api.shared.dependencies import get_db, get_event_bus\nfrom packages.application.analysis.use_cases.validate_thesis_use_case import ValidateThesisUseCase\nfrom apps.api.analysis.dto.thesis_dto import CreateThesisRequest, ThesisResponse\nfrom apps.api.analysis.dto.thesis_dto import ThesisMapper\nfrom packages.infrastructure.analysis.persistence.thesis_postgres_repository import ThesisPostgresRepository\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/theses\", tags=[\"analysis\"])\n\n\ndef get_validate_thesis_use_case(\n    db: Annotated[DatabaseClient, Depends(get_db)],\n    event_bus: Annotated[EventBus, Depends(get_event_bus)],\n) -> ValidateThesisUseCase:\n    return ValidateThesisUseCase(\n        thesis_repo=ThesisPostgresRepository(db),\n        event_bus=event_bus,\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/\", response_model=ThesisResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)\nasync def create_thesis(\n    request: CreateThesisRequest,\n    use_case: Annotated[ValidateThesisUseCase, Depends(get_validate_thesis_use_case)],\n) -> ThesisResponse:\n    result = await use_case.execute(\n        ticker=request.ticker,\n        bull_case_text=request.bull_case,\n        bear_case_text=request.bear_case,\n    )\n    return ThesisMapper.to_response(result)\n```\n\n## Naming Conventions\n\n| Type | Pattern | Example |\n|---|---|---|\n| Router | `<resource>_router.py` | `theses_router.py` |\n| DTO (request) | `<Action><Resource>Request` | `CreateThesisRequest` |\n| DTO (response) | `<Resource>Response` | `ThesisResponse` |\n| Use case | `<Verb><Resource>UseCase` | `ValidateThesisUseCase` |\n| Mapper | `<Resource>Mapper` | `ThesisMapper` |\n\n## DTO Pattern (Pydantic v2 — interfaces layer only)\n\n```python\n# apps/api/analysis/dto/thesis_dto.py\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.models.thesis import Thesis\n\nclass CreateThesisRequest(BaseModel):\n    ticker: str\n    bull_case: str\n    bear_case: str\n\n    @field_validator(\"ticker\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_ticker(cls, v: str) -> str:\n        return v.strip().upper()\n\n    @field_validator(\"bear_case\")\n    @classmethod\n    def bear_case_must_be_substantive(cls, v: str) -> str:\n        if len(v.strip()) < 50:\n            raise ValueError(\"Bear case must be substantive (>50 chars)\")\n        return v\n\n\nclass ThesisResponse(BaseModel):\n    id: str\n    ticker: str\n    status: str\n    bull_case_summary: str\n    bear_case_summary: str\n    created_at: str\n\n\nclass ThesisMapper:\n    @staticmethod\n    def to_response(thesis: Thesis) -> ThesisResponse:\n        return ThesisResponse(\n            id=str(thesis.id),\n            ticker=str(thesis.ticker),\n            status=thesis.status.value,\n            bull_case_summary=thesis.bull_case.summary,\n            bear_case_summary=thesis.bear_case.summary,\n            created_at=thesis.created_at.isoformat(),\n        )\n```\n\n## Port + Adapter Pattern (Domain → Infrastructure)\n\nPort (Protocol) in domain:\n```python\n# packages/domain/analysis/repositories/thesis_repository.py\nfrom typing import Protocol\n\nclass ThesisRepository(Protocol):\n    async def save(self, thesis: Thesis) -> None: ...\n    async def find_by_id(self, id: ThesisId) -> Thesis | None: ...\n```\n\nAdapter (implementation) in infrastructure:\n```python\n# packages/infrastructure/analysis/persistence/thesis_postgres_repository.py\nclass ThesisPostgresRepository:\n    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient) -> None:\n        self._db = db\n    \n    async def save(self, thesis: Thesis) -> None: ...\n    async def find_by_id(self, id: ThesisId) -> Thesis | None: ...\n```\n\nWire at router dependency injection (shown above).\n\n## App Factory\n\n```python\n# apps/api/main.py\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI\nfrom apps.api.analysis.routers.theses_router import router as theses_router\nfrom apps.api.influence.routers.kols_router import router as kols_router\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(\n        title=\"StockForge API\",\n        description=\"AI-first investment research — Vietnamese stock market\",\n        version=\"0.1.0\",\n    )\n    \n    app.include_router(theses_router, prefix=\"/api/v1\")\n    app.include_router(kols_router, prefix=\"/api/v1\")\n    \n    return app\n\napp = create_app()\n```\n\n## Testing Setup\n\n```python\n# apps/api/tests/test_theses_router.py\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\nfrom unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock\n\nfrom apps.api.main import create_app\nfrom apps.api.analysis.routers.theses_router import get_validate_thesis_use_case\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef mock_use_case() -> AsyncMock:\n    return AsyncMock(spec=ValidateThesisUseCase)\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(mock_use_case: AsyncMock) -> TestClient:\n    app = create_app()\n    app.dependency_overrides[get_validate_thesis_use_case] = lambda: mock_use_case\n    return TestClient(app)\n\ndef test_create_thesis_dispatches_to_use_case(\n    client: TestClient,\n    mock_use_case: AsyncMock,\n) -> None:\n    mock_use_case.execute.return_value = make_thesis_fixture()\n    \n    response = client.post(\"/api/v1/theses/\", json={\n        \"ticker\": \"VCB\",\n        \"bull_case\": \"Strong earnings growth driven by retail expansion...\",\n        \"bear_case\": \"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins and trigger provision surge...\",\n    })\n    \n    assert response.status_code == 201\n    mock_use_case.execute.assert_called_once()\n```\n\n## Router Boundary Rules\n\n- **Never import** another BC's router module directly\n- **Never import** from `packages/domain/<otherBc>/` in this router\n- Cross-BC integration via:\n  - Domain events (published, subscribed via contracts)\n  - HTTP calls if service boundary strictly required\n  - Shared kernel (contracts package)\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Put business logic in routers (use cases own it)\n- Import repositories directly in routers (use case mediates)\n- Use Pydantic models in domain layer (domain uses dataclasses)\n- Mix use cases from multiple BCs in one router\n- Skip the port/Protocol indirection for \"simple\" repos\n\n**Do**:\n- One router per bounded context resource\n- Thin routers, thick use cases\n- Protocol/adapter everywhere for testability\n- Pydantic DTOs at HTTP boundary only\n- Validate inputs at DTO level\n\n## Related\n\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — for domain models this router uses\n- `postgres-pgvector` — for repository implementations\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c9203e5e-1707-4fe7-9db7-9b3edb371ea7","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0045105b-ab8a-4767-85b0-fc1abfd579a5","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. {"parentUuid":"8dbb8944-5a39-4235-92aa-cea9c4bf4a0d","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. {"parentUuid":"7345574a-0ded-406f-b9a3-67f149f41716","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01FYx9MfyxAunBsUbq6NajqK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SFD2oFnviqhCT27iwXHKmm","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\Users\\PC\\.ccs\\instances\\nathanleewindy\\projects\\C--htdocs-stockforge\\memory\\bash_permission_pattern.md","old_string":"**How to apply:**\n- When a routine shell tool (`mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `echo`, `test`, `touch`, `diff`, `awk`, `sed`, `head`, `tail`, `sort`, `uniq`, `tr`, `printf`, `for`, `if`, `while`, `bash`, `sh`) hits a stuck permission, add `Bash(<cmd>:*)` to `settings.local.json` allow list and retry — don't ask the user.\n- **Compound commands chained with `&&` / `;` / `|`** are matched as ONE full string, NOT per sub-command. So `Bash(mkdir:*)` does NOT cover `mkdir -p X && ls X && echo OK`. Either: (a) tách thành nhiều single Bash calls, hoặc (b) set `defaultMode: \"bypassPermissions\"` ở `.claude/settings.local.json`. Default to (a) — single-command calls are clearer and align with allowlist semantics; (b) is a sledgehammer reserved for stuck-on-mobile-remote moments.\n- Keep `Bash(*)` in the list for legacy / fallback but treat it as decorative; the explicit `Bash(<cmd>:*)` entries are what actually pass.\n- Project-level `.claude/settings.json` deny rules still take precedence, so this does not bypass charter immutability protections.\n- Memory `wildcard_permissions_preference.md` already covers the high-level approach; this entry is the specific tactical pattern.","new_string":"**How to apply:**\n- The current `.claude/settings.local.json` already covers a comprehensive `Bash(<cmd>:*)` allowlist for ~150 routine commands across these families: file-ops (mkdir/rm/mv/cp/touch/ln/chmod/stat/find/ls/du/df), text-processing (cat/head/tail/grep/awk/sed/tr/sort/uniq/wc/cut/paste/diff/jq/yq/xargs), compression (tar/gzip/zip), process control (ps/kill/sleep/timeout/nohup), hashing (md5sum/sha256sum), network (curl/wget/ssh/rsync), VCS (git/gh), build (make/npm/yarn/pnpm/cargo/go/mvn/gradle/python/pytest/ruff/mypy), DBs (psql/mysql/redis-cli/sqlite3), shell control (if/for/while/case/source/eval/export/exec), and stockforge-specific tools (yt-dlp/ffmpeg/whisper). Plus `defaultMode: \"bypassPermissions\"`. Together these mean routine ops should not prompt at all.\n- If a NEW tool category surfaces (rare — nginx, jenkins, pulumi, bicep, etc.), add `Bash(<cmd>:*)` to `.claude/settings.local.json` allow list. {"parentUuid":"f8484928-8b08-4da6-8a31-b1b43da2bc60","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01Wzuf36LRE2Ff1RHNkoeMiD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QcBacbHdUqNvSMEQgqna14","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\ubiquitous-language\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: ubiquitous-language\ndescription: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n---\n\n# Skill: Ubiquitous Language\n\n## Purpose\n\nDDD requires a shared vocabulary between domain experts and developers. This skill extracts and maintains that vocabulary for StockForge's Vietnamese stock market domain (9 BCs).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Starting a new bounded context\n- Processing conversation with domain expert about stock investing\n- Reviewing conversation for undocumented terms\n- Checking code for term drift from glossary\n- Onboarding new contributor\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Technical infrastructure (not domain-specific)\n- External API integration (use their terminology)\n- UI framework concerns (not DDD-relevant)\n\n## Relationship to /drill-me\n\n`/drill-me` is interactive — asks user questions, extracts language live. This skill is passive — analyzes existing content. Use both: `/drill-me` for new domains, this skill for ongoing maintenance.\n\n## Extraction Process\n\n1. **Identify candidates** — scan source for: domain nouns (`thesis`, `KOL recommendation`, `pump detection`), domain verbs (`submit thesis`, `extract recommendation`), state names (`active`, `incubating`, `dumped`), relationships (`KOL owns Channel`), rules (`Thesis can only be submitted when bear case is substantive`).\n\n2. **Vet each candidate** — is it domain-specific or generic? Does it have precise business meaning? Could a Vietnamese investor define it clearly? Already in glossary under different name? Skip generic terms (`user`, `item`, `data`) unless they have specific domain meaning.\n\n3. **Define accepted terms** with this 6-field schema (see `references/templates.md` for full example):\n   - `Bounded context` (which of 9 BCs owns it)\n   - `Definition` (clear, specific — what it is, what it's for)\n   - `Lifecycle` (state transitions, if applicable)\n   - `Not to confuse with` (similar-but-different terms)\n   - `Code` (file path if implemented, or \"not yet built\")\n   - `Introduced` (date, source conversation/spec)\n\n4. **Drift detection** — for each term, `grep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"`. Flag if: code uses different name for same concept; multiple names exist for one term; term defined but unused in code.\n\n5. **Resolve conflicts**:\n   - **Rename code to match glossary** (most common; glossary is canonical)\n   - **Update glossary to match code** (if code name is better; log to drift-log)\n   - **Recognize two distinct concepts** (sometimes synonymous candidates are actually different — define both)\n\n## Writing Good Definitions\n\n**Bad**: `Thesis: An analysis of a stock.` (too vague)\n\n**Good** (see `references/templates.md` § Term Definition Example for `Thesis`): includes BC, precise definition with adversarial-by-design constraint, lifecycle Draft → Active → [Closed | Abandoned] → PostMortem, and explicit \"Not to confuse with\" entries (ExtractedClaim, KolRecommendation, generic \"Analysis\").\n\n## Common Pitfalls\n\n- **Term explosion** — don't add every noun mentioned; reserve glossary for terms with precise meaning\n- **Synonym tolerance** — never allow \"Recommendation\" + \"KolRecommendation\" for same thing; pick one, enforce\n- **Over-abstraction** — \"Signal\" is too generic; be specific (`ExtractedClaim`, `KolRecommendation`, `SentimentScore`)\n- **Missing lifecycle** — most domain entities have states; document them\n- **No \"Not to Confuse With\"** — if term is easy to confuse with another, document the distinction explicitly\n\n## Updating the Glossary\n\nEvery change to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` must:\n\n1. Update or add the term definition\n2. Append entry to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` (date, change type, rationale, impact files)\n3. If renaming, add entry to glossary \"Stop List\" (`Do NOT use` ↔ `USE instead`)\n\nSee `references/templates.md` § Drift Log + Stop List for entry templates.\n\n## Output Format (extraction run)\n\nWhen extracting language from a source, produce:\n\n- Header (date, source ID/path)\n- `Accepted [M]` — full definitions\n- `Deferred [K]` — terms needing more domain-expert context\n- `Rejected [L]` — too generic / technical infra / not domain\n- `Conflicts Detected` — existing term vs candidate, resolution needed\n- `Next Steps` — review with expert / update glossary / run /ul-audit / schedule /drill-me\n\nFull template: `references/templates.md` § Extraction Output.\n\n## Integration\n\n- `/drill-me` — interactive interview (this skill processes results)\n- `/ul-audit` — scans code against glossary (this skill drives definitions)\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — output target\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` — change log\n\n## Attribution\n\nAdapted from mattpocock/skills (`ubiquitous-language`), MIT licensed. Customized for StockForge DDD workflow with 9 bounded contexts and Vietnamese stock domain.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5753,"cache_read_input_tokens":164205,"output_tokens":3750,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5753,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":3750,"cache_read_input_tokens":164205,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5753,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5753},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYU13jjWZF1CJ9KtcUwz","type":"assistant","uuid":"88ad7855-db00-4df6-b8c5-ea36bdab96d5","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:35:35.019Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Customized for StockForge DDD workflow with 9 bounded contexts and Vietnamese stock domain."]}],"originalFile":"---\nname: ubiquitous-language\ndescription: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n---\n\n# Skill: Ubiquitous Language\n\n## Purpose\n\nDDD requires a shared vocabulary between domain experts and developers. This skill extracts and maintains that vocabulary for StockForge's Vietnamese stock market domain.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Starting a new bounded context (one of 9 BCs)\n- Processing conversation with domain expert about stock investing\n- Reviewing conversation for undocumented terms\n- Checking code for term drift from glossary\n- Onboarding new contributor\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Technical infrastructure (not domain-specific)\n- External API integration (use their terminology)\n- UI framework concerns (not DDD-relevant)\n\n## Relationship to /drill-me\n\n`/drill-me` is interactive — asks user questions, extracts language live.\nThis skill is passive — analyzes existing content to find terms.\n\nUse both: `/drill-me` for new domains, this skill for ongoing maintenance.\n\n## Extraction Process\n\n### 1. Identify Candidates\n\nScan source (conversation, spec, interview transcript) for:\n- **Domain nouns** (\"thesis\", \"KOL recommendation\", \"pump detection\", \"calibration\")\n- **Domain verbs** (\"submit thesis\", \"extract recommendation\", \"detect pump phase\")\n- **State names** (\"active\", \"incubating\", \"distributing\", \"dumped\")\n- **Relationships** (\"KOL owns Channel\", \"Thesis references Catalysts\")\n- **Rules** (\"Thesis can only be submitted when bear case is substantive\")\n\n### 2. Candidate Vetting\n\nFor each candidate, ask:\n- Is this domain-specific or generic?\n- Does it have a precise business meaning?\n- Could a domain expert (Vietnamese investor) define it clearly?\n- Is it already in glossary under different name?\n\nSkip generic terms (user, item, data) unless they have specific domain meaning.\n\n### 3. Definition Structure\n\nFor each accepted term:\n\n```markdown\n### [Term Name]\n\n**Bounded context**: [which of 9 BCs owns this term]\n\n**Definition**: [Clear, specific definition — what it is, what it's for]\n\n**Lifecycle**: [If applicable — state transitions]\n\n**Not to confuse with**: [List of similar-but-different terms]\n\n**Code**: [file path if implemented, or \"not yet built\"]\n\n**Introduced**: [date, source conversation/spec]\n```\n\n### 4. Drift Detection\n\nFor each term, scan codebase:\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"\n```\n\nFlag if:\n- Code uses different name for same concept\n- Multiple names exist for what should be one term\n- Term defined in glossary but not used in code\n\n### 5. Conflict Resolution\n\nWhen conflicts arise:\n- **Rename code to match glossary**: Most common. Glossary is canonical.\n- **Update glossary to match code**: If code name is better, update glossary + add to drift-log.\n- **Recognize two distinct concepts**: Sometimes what seemed synonymous is actually different. Define both distinctly.\n\n## Writing Good Definitions\n\n### Bad definition\n```markdown\n### Thesis\n**Definition**: An analysis of a stock.\n```\nToo vague. Could be anything.\n\n### Good definition\n```markdown\n### Thesis\n**Bounded context**: BC-8 Analysis & Thesis\n**Definition**: A structured multi-perspective investment analysis for a specific stock\n(Ticker). Must include both BullAnalysis and BearAnalysis (adversarial by design).\nLifecycle ends in either PostMortem (if acted on) or Abandoned (if not).\n**Lifecycle**: Draft → Active → [Closed | Abandoned] → PostMortem (optional)\n**Not to confuse with**: \n- ExtractedClaim (a factual claim from a source, not a thesis)\n- KolRecommendation (a KOL's recommendation, input to thesis, not thesis itself)\n- Analysis (generic term; our canonical term is Thesis for investment analyses)\n```\n\n## Common Pitfalls\n\n### Term Explosion\nDon't add every noun mentioned. Reserve glossary for terms with precise meaning.\n\n### Synonym Tolerance\nDon't allow \"Recommendation\" and \"KolRecommendation\" for same thing. Pick one. Enforce.\n\n### Over-Abstraction\n\"Signal\" as a glossary term is usually too generic in this context. Be specific (ExtractedClaim, KolRecommendation, SentimentScore).\n\n### Missing Lifecycle\nMost domain entities have states. Document them.\n\n### No \"Not to Confuse With\"\nIf term is easy to confuse with another, document the distinction explicitly.\n\n## Updating Glossary\n\nChanges to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` always include:\n\n1. Update the term definition\n2. Append entry to `drift-log.md`:\n\n```markdown\n## YYYY-MM-DD — [Add | Rename | Deprecate | Clarify] — [term]\n\n**Session**: [reference]\n**Change**: [what changed]\n**Rationale**: [why]\n**Impact**: [files affected, if any]\n```\n\n3. If renaming, add to \"Stop List\" in glossary.md:\n\n```markdown\n| Do NOT use | USE instead |\n|---|---|\n| Analysis | Thesis (for investment analyses) |\n| Recommendation | KolRecommendation |\n| Signal | ExtractedClaim | SentimentScore (be specific) |\n```\n\n## Output Format\n\nWhen extracting language from source:\n\n```markdown\n# Ubiquitous Language Extraction — [source]\n\n## Date\nYYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Source\n[conversation ID, spec path, or interview transcript]\n\n## Candidate Terms Found ([N])\n\n### Accepted ([M])\n\n#### [Term 1]\n[Full definition as above]\n\n#### [Term 2]\n[Full definition]\n\n### Deferred ([K])\n- [Term] — need more context from domain expert\n- [Term] — overlap with existing, need clarification\n\n### Rejected ([L])\n- [Term] — too generic\n- [Term] — technical infrastructure, not domain\n\n## Conflicts Detected\n- [Existing term] vs [candidate] — [resolution needed]\n\n## Next Steps\n1. Review accepted terms with domain expert\n2. Update glossary.md with accepted definitions\n3. Run /ul-audit to find code drift\n4. For deferred terms, schedule /drill-me session\n```\n\n## Integration\n\n- `/drill-me` — interactive interview, this skill processes results\n- `/ul-audit` — scans code against glossary, this skill drives definitions\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — output target\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` — change log\n\n## Attribution\n\nAdapted from mattpocock/skills (`ubiquitous-language`), MIT licensed.\nCustomized for StockForge DDD workflow with 9 bounded contexts and Vietnamese stock domain.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"88ad7855-db00-4df6-b8c5-ea36bdab96d5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Review accepted terms with domain expert\n2. Update glossary.md with accepted definitions\n3. Run /ul-audit to find code drift\n4. {"parentUuid":"f3ef3813-204c-441e-9da8-10561689b917","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"24c406e9-3097-4922-adc6-450b532742b4","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:35:51.687Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"6216836a-093f-4cba-84d9-ab000f08cbec","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01SzemhVtYxbspTe7M92tsS2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WFaHp1hKLbNBxBhC1ntMGX","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\write-a-skill\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: write-a-skill\ndescription: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n---\n\n# Skill: Write a Skill\n\n## Purpose\n\nTurn an observed pattern into a reusable skill that Claude Code auto-discovers and applies.\n\n## When to Create a Skill\n\n- Same pattern applied in 3+ sessions → skill candidate\n- User explains the same technique repeatedly → formalize it\n- Post-mortem reveals a rule that would help future sessions → skill\n- New tool/library adopted with non-obvious correct usage → skill\n\n## When NOT to Create a Skill\n\n- One-off patterns (not reusable)\n- Framework documentation (link to docs instead)\n- Obvious patterns (experienced dev would know)\n- Duplicates of existing skills\n\n## Anatomy\n\n```\n.claude/skills/<skill-name>/\n├── SKILL.md          # required (≤150 LOC per drift-signals D1)\n├── examples/         # optional concrete examples\n└── references/       # optional companion docs (no LOC ceiling)\n```\n\n## SKILL.md Structure\n\nTemplate + section breakdown: see `references/best-practices.md` § \"Structure\" and `references/templates.md` § \"SKILL.md skeleton\".\n\nCore sections every skill needs: frontmatter (`name` + `description`), Purpose, When to Use, When NOT to Use, Process / Content, Anti-Patterns, Related.\n\n## Critical: The Description Field\n\nClaude Code auto-discovers skills by matching `description` to current context. A vague description means the skill never fires.\n\n### Description writing rules\n\n1. **Lead with the core action** — \"Extract X\", \"Implement Y\", \"Design Z\"\n2. **Include domain keywords** — terms the user might mention (`thesis`, `KOL`, `pump`)\n3. **\"Use when\" clause** — explicit trigger conditions\n4. **Optional**: what's avoided / ensured\n5. **StockForge-specific**: mention any invariants this skill enforces (e.g., I-S1 no-LLM-math)\n\nBad/good examples + StockForge-specific examples: `references/templates.md` § \"Description examples\".\n\n## Progressive Disclosure (L-S14-1)\n\nFirst-draft target: **20% under the ceiling** (skill ≤120 LOC, command ≤96 LOC, agent ≤160 LOC). Reserve 20-40 LOC for amendments. A skill drafted AT the ceiling violates D1 within 2-3 amendments. See `references/best-practices.md` § L-S14-1.\n\nWhen content grows past compression reserve: extract topical sub-sections to `references/<topic>.md` (no D1 ceiling) and replace inline content with a one-line pointer. Don't compress at the cost of clarity.\n\n## Quality Checklist for New Skill\n\n- [ ] `description` is specific enough to trigger appropriately\n- [ ] `description` contains keywords user would likely use\n- [ ] \"When to use\" + \"When NOT to use\" both concrete\n- [ ] At least one example included\n- [ ] Anti-patterns section has 3+ concrete bad examples\n- [ ] Cross-references to related skills\n- [ ] SKILL.md ≤120 LOC (first-draft target per L-S14-1)\n- [ ] If skill touches financial output: I-S1 no-LLM-math constraint noted\n- [ ] Tested: manually trigger with matching keywords, verify activation\n\n## Skill Bloat — Pruning\n\nEvery skill loaded consumes context tokens. Quarterly: any skill not triggered in 3 months — evaluate (still relevant? description need fixing? deprecate?).\n\n## Migration from mattpocock Skills\n\nIf adopting from upstream:\n\n1. Copy SKILL.md\n2. Review description for StockForge-specific context\n3. Adjust examples to StockForge domain (thesis, KOL, VN stocks) if relevant\n4. Keep MIT attribution note\n5. Add stock-domain invariants (I-S1 no-LLM-math, I-S2 citation) where applicable\n6.
