Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n---\n\n# Skill: Write a Skill\n\n## Purpose\n\nTurn an observed pattern into a reusable skill that Claude Code auto-discovers and applies.\n\n## When to Create a Skill\n\n- Same pattern applied in 3+ sessions → skill candidate\n- User explains the same technique repeatedly → formalize it\n- Post-mortem reveals a rule that would help future sessions → skill\n- New tool/library adopted with non-obvious correct usage → skill\n\n## When NOT to Create a Skill\n\n- One-off patterns (not reusable)\n- Framework documentation (link to docs instead)\n- Obvious patterns (experienced dev would know)\n- Duplicates of existing skills\n\n## Anatomy\n\n```\n.claude/skills/<skill-name>/\n├── SKILL.md          # required (≤150 LOC per drift-signals D1)\n├── examples/         # optional concrete examples\n└── references/       # optional companion docs (no LOC ceiling)\n```\n\n## SKILL.md Structure\n\nTemplate + section breakdown: see `references/best-practices.md` § \"Structure\" and `references/templates.md` § \"SKILL.md skeleton\".\n\nCore sections every skill needs: frontmatter (`name` + `description`), Purpose, When to Use, When NOT to Use, Process / Content, Anti-Patterns, Related.\n\n## Critical: The Description Field\n\nClaude Code auto-discovers skills by matching `description` to current context. A vague description means the skill never fires.\n\n### Description writing rules\n\n1. **Lead with the core action** — \"Extract X\", \"Implement Y\", \"Design Z\"\n2. **Include domain keywords** — terms the user might mention (`thesis`, `KOL`, `pump`)\n3. **\"Use when\" clause** — explicit trigger conditions\n4. **Optional**: what's avoided / ensured\n5. **StockForge-specific**: mention any invariants this skill enforces (e.g., I-S1 no-LLM-math)\n\nBad/good examples + StockForge-specific examples: `references/templates.md` § \"Description examples\".\n\n## Progressive Disclosure (L-S14-1)\n\nFirst-draft target: **20% under the ceiling** (skill ≤120 LOC, command ≤96 LOC, agent ≤160 LOC). Reserve 20-40 LOC for amendments. A skill drafted AT the ceiling violates D1 within 2-3 amendments. See `references/best-practices.md` § L-S14-1.\n\nWhen content grows past compression reserve: extract topical sub-sections to `references/<topic>.md` (no D1 ceiling) and replace inline content with a one-line pointer. Don't compress at the cost of clarity.\n\n## Quality Checklist for New Skill\n\n- [ ] `description` is specific enough to trigger appropriately\n- [ ] `description` contains keywords user would likely use\n- [ ] \"When to use\" + \"When NOT to use\" both concrete\n- [ ] At least one example included\n- [ ] Anti-patterns section has 3+ concrete bad examples\n- [ ] Cross-references to related skills\n- [ ] SKILL.md ≤120 LOC (first-draft target per L-S14-1)\n- [ ] If skill touches financial output: I-S1 no-LLM-math constraint noted\n- [ ] Tested: manually trigger with matching keywords, verify activation\n\n## Skill Bloat — Pruning\n\nEvery skill loaded consumes context tokens. Quarterly: any skill not triggered in 3 months — evaluate (still relevant? description need fixing? deprecate?).\n\n## Migration from mattpocock Skills\n\nIf adopting from upstream:\n\n1. Copy SKILL.md\n2. Review description for StockForge-specific context\n3. Adjust examples to StockForge domain (thesis, KOL, VN stocks) if relevant\n4. Keep MIT attribution note\n5. Add stock-domain invariants (I-S1 no-LLM-math, I-S2 citation) where applicable\n6. Link to upstream in \"Related\" section\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Vague description (won't trigger reliably)\n- SKILL.md drafted AT ceiling (violates D1 after first amendment)\n- Code dumps in SKILL.md (push to `examples/` or `references/`)\n- Duplicating procedure between `<name>` skill and `/<name>` command (L-S14-2 — see `references/best-practices.md`)\n- No \"Not to confuse with\" / no anti-patterns section\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `ubiquitous-language` — when skill involves domain terms\n- `obsidian-vault` — when skill involves knowledge management\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":148,"newStart":14,"newLines":84,"lines":[" - Same pattern applied in 3+ sessions → skill candidate"," - User explains the same technique repeatedly → formalize it"," - Post-mortem reveals a rule that would help future sessions → skill","-- New tool/library adopted that has non-obvious correct usage → skill","+- New tool/library adopted with non-obvious correct usage → skill"," ","-## Anatomy of a Skill","+## When NOT to Create a Skill"," ","+- One-off patterns (not reusable)","+- Framework documentation (link to docs instead)","+- Obvious patterns (experienced dev would know)","+- Duplicates of existing skills","+","+## Anatomy","+"," ```"," .claude/skills/<skill-name>/","-├── SKILL.md          # Main skill file (required)","-├── examples/         # Concrete examples (optional)","-└── references/       # Linked resources (optional)","+├── SKILL.md          # required (≤150 LOC per drift-signals D1)","+├── examples/         # optional concrete examples","+└── references/       # optional companion docs (no LOC ceiling)"," ```"," "," ## SKILL.md Structure"," ","-```markdown","----","-name: skill-name-kebab-case","-description: One sentence. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n---\n\n# Skill: Write a Skill\n\n## Purpose\n\nTurn an observed pattern into a reusable skill that Claude Code auto-discovers and applies.\n\n## When to Create a Skill\n\n- Same pattern applied in 3+ sessions → skill candidate\n- User explains the same technique repeatedly → formalize it\n- Post-mortem reveals a rule that would help future sessions → skill\n- New tool/library adopted that has non-obvious correct usage → skill\n\n## Anatomy of a Skill\n\n```\n.claude/skills/<skill-name>/\n├── SKILL.md          # Main skill file (required)\n├── examples/         # Concrete examples (optional)\n└── references/       # Linked resources (optional)\n```\n\n## SKILL.md Structure\n\n```markdown\n---\nname: skill-name-kebab-case\ndescription: One sentence. Specific keywords. When to use. Why it matters.\n---\n\n# Skill: Human-Readable Name\n\n## Purpose\nWhat this skill does. Why it exists. One paragraph.\n\n## When to Use\n- Specific trigger 1\n- Specific trigger 2\n\n## When NOT to Use\n- Wrong context 1\n- Wrong context 2\n\n## Process / Content\nStep-by-step or structured explanation of the skill.\n\n## Examples\nGood examples. Bad examples. Correct patterns.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\nCommon mistakes to avoid.\n\n## Related Skills\nCross-references to other skills.\n```\n\n## Critical: The Description Field\n\nClaude Code auto-discovers skills by matching the `description` to current context.\n\n### Bad description\n```yaml\ndescription: Helps with stuff\n```\nToo vague. Won't trigger reliably.\n\n### Good description\n```yaml\ndescription: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation \n  integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL \n  transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim \n  has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution.\n  Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n```\nSpecific keywords. Clear \"use when\". Mentions what's ensured. StockForge-specific.\n\n### Description writing rules\n\n1. **Lead with the core action** — \"Extract X\", \"Implement Y\", \"Design Z\"\n2. **Include domain keywords** — terms user might mention (thesis, KOL, pump)\n3. **\"Use when\" clause** — trigger conditions\n4. **Optional**: what's avoided / ensured\n5. **StockForge-specific**: mention any invariants this skill enforces\n\n## Progressive Disclosure\n\nDon't dump everything in SKILL.md. Progressive disclosure:\n\n### Main file: SKILL.md\n- Purpose, when to use, core content\n- Enough to apply the skill at basic level\n- Should fit under 400 lines (ideally 100-300)\n\n### examples/ directory\n- Concrete code examples\n- Before/after transformations\n- Referenced from SKILL.md\n\n### references/ directory\n- Detailed technical specs\n- Relevant external documentation\n- Referenced on-demand\n\nAgent loads SKILL.md first. Only loads examples/references if deep-diving.\n\n## Quality Checklist for New Skill\n\nBefore committing a new skill:\n\n- [ ] `description` is specific enough to trigger appropriately\n- [ ] `description` contains keywords user would likely use\n- [ ] \"When to use\" is concrete, not vague\n- [ ] \"When NOT to use\" is included\n- [ ] At least one example included\n- [ ] Anti-patterns section has 3+ concrete bad examples\n- [ ] Cross-references to related skills\n- [ ] Under 400 lines (split if longer)\n- [ ] Tested: manually trigger with matching keywords, verify activation\n- [ ] If skill touches financial output: no-LLM-math constraint noted\n\n## Avoiding Skill Bloat\n\n### Every skill has a cost\nSkills loaded into context consume tokens. Every skill.\n\n### Don't create skills for\n- One-off patterns (not reusable)\n- Framework documentation (link to docs instead)\n- Obvious patterns (experienced dev would know)\n- Duplicates of existing skills\n\n### Prune periodically\nQuarterly: any skill that hasn't been triggered in 3 months — evaluate:\n- Still relevant?\n- Description need fixing?\n- Or deprecate?\n\n## Migration from mattpocock Skills\n\nIf adopting a mattpocock/skills skill:\n1. Copy SKILL.md\n2. Review description for StockForge-specific context\n3. Adjust examples to StockForge domain if needed (thesis, KOL, VN stocks)\n4. Keep MIT attribution note\n5. Add any stock-domain invariants that apply (no-LLM-math, citation)\n6. Concrete templates referenced from each section.\n\n## SKILL.md Skeleton\n\n```markdown\n---\nname: skill-name-kebab-case\ndescription: One sentence. Specific keywords. When to use. Why it matters.\n---\n\n# Skill: Human-Readable Name\n\n## Purpose\nWhat this skill does. Why it exists. One paragraph.\n\n## When to Use\n- Specific trigger 1\n- Specific trigger 2\n\n## When NOT to Use\n- Wrong context 1\n- Wrong context 2\n\n## Process / Content\nStep-by-step or structured explanation of the skill.\n\n## Examples\nGood examples. Bad examples. Correct patterns.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\nCommon mistakes to avoid.\n\n## Related Skills\nCross-references to other skills.\n```\n\n## Description Examples\n\n### Bad\n\n```yaml\ndescription: Helps with stuff\n```\n\nToo vague. Won't trigger reliably.\n\n### Good\n\n```yaml\ndescription: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation\n  integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL\n  transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim\n  has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution.\n  Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n```\n\nSpecific keywords. Clear \"use when\". Mentions what's ensured. StockForge-specific.\n\n### StockForge-specific patterns\n\nLead phrases that match user vocabulary:\n\n- \"Extract structured claims...\" → matches \"extract claims from KOL\"\n- \"Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions...\" → matches \"build new endpoint\"\n- \"Design Postgres schemas with pgvector...\" → matches \"add migration\"\n- \"Build reliable web crawlers...\" → matches \"scrape CafeF\"\n\nAlways end with the invariant: \"Enforces no-LLM-math (I-S1)\" / \"Every claim cites source + as_of (I-S2)\" / etc.\n\n## Frontmatter Fields (full reference)\n\n| Field | Required | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `name` | yes | kebab-case; matches folder name |\n| `description` | yes | 1-2 sentences; auto-discovery driver |\n| `allowed-tools` | optional | restrict to specific tools (e.g. `[Read, Glob, Grep]` for analysis-only) |\n\n`allowed-tools` is the only optional field — when set, the skill cannot use other tools even if invoked.\n\n## Common Failure Modes (when writing a skill)\n\n1. **Drafting at the ceiling** — D1 violation within 2-3 amendments. Use 20% reserve.\n2. **Code-dumping into SKILL.md** — push code to `examples/<name>.py` or `references/templates.md` instead.\n3. **Skipping \"When NOT to use\"** — leads to mis-triggering on adjacent contexts.\n4. **No anti-patterns section** — useful negative examples often clarify the positive case.\n5. **Duplicating with sibling command** — `/<name>` and `<name>` skill must not have overlapping bodies (L-S14-2).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":44,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8635,"cache_read_input_tokens":169958,"output_tokens":3502,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8635,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":44,"output_tokens":3502,"cache_read_input_tokens":169958,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8635,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8635},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYU5KV8uu2kj1CjkCbTq","type":"assistant","uuid":"1507e278-7a92-4476-8cdb-3663cac7fdfa","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:36:41.547Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Mentions what's ensured. StockForge-specific.\n\n### StockForge-specific patterns\n\nLead phrases that match user vocabulary:\n\n- \"Extract structured claims...\" → matches \"extract claims from KOL\"\n- \"Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions...\" → matches \"build new endpoint\"\n- \"Design Postgres schemas with pgvector...\" → matches \"add migration\"\n- \"Build reliable web crawlers...\" → matches \"scrape CafeF\"\n\nAlways end with the invariant: \"Enforces no-LLM-math (I-S1)\" / \"Every claim cites source + as_of (I-S2)\" / etc.\n\n## Frontmatter Fields (full reference)\n\n| Field | Required | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `name` | yes | kebab-case; matches folder name |\n| `description` | yes | 1-2 sentences; auto-discovery driver |\n| `allowed-tools` | optional | restrict to specific tools (e.g. `[Read, Glob, Grep]` for analysis-only) |\n\n`allowed-tools` is the only optional field — when set, the skill cannot use other tools even if invoked.\n\n## Common Failure Modes (when writing a skill)\n\n1. **Drafting at the ceiling** — D1 violation within 2-3 amendments. Opening Question\n34\t\n35\tAsk:\n36\t> \"Let's drill down on [domain area]. I'll ask structured questions to build out the ubiquitous language. Name them in the language a domain expert would use.\"\n47\t- For each thing: \"What does a [thing] always have? What can it do?\"\n48\t- \"What differentiates [thing A] from [thing B] — what's the critical distinction?\"\n49\t\n50\t**Phase B: Verbs (what happens)**\n51\t\n52\t- \"What are the key actions/operations in this domain?\"\n53\t- For each action: \"What triggers this? What's the expected outcome?\"\n54\t- \"Are there actions that look similar but are actually different? Which are forbidden?\"\n60\t- \"What invariants must hold at each state?\"\n61\t\n62\t**Phase D: Relationships**\n63\t\n64\t- \"How does [thing A] relate to [thing B]?\"\n65\t- \"Is the relationship one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many?\"\n66\t- \"Is the relationship owned (one thing exists only as part of another) or referenced (both can exist independently)?\"\n67\t\n68\t**Phase E: Conflict Check**\n69\t\n70\t- Compare new terms with existing glossary\n71\t- \"I notice you used 'Signal' — we already have 'ExtractedClaim' in the glossary for what sounds similar. Real-Time Glossary Updates\n80\t\n81\tAs user answers, build draft entries:\n82\t\n83\t```markdown\n84\t### [Term]\n85\t**Bounded context**: [from Phase F]\n86\t**Definition**: [from Phase A answers]\n87\t**Lifecycle**: [from Phase C if applicable]\n88\t**Not to confuse with**: [from Phase E]\n89\t**Code**: [to be determined when implementing]\n90\t**Introduced**: [today's date] (via /drill-me session)\n91\t```\n92\t\n93\tShow draft to user: \"Does this capture it accurately?\"\n94\t\n95\t### 5. {"parentUuid":"0be3f1ad-a6ae-4690-986c-48577788b4be","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"1875c1b1-489c-4ec8-a1fa-118a1fa76ff7","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:36:43.016Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"1ae165ee-d299-4a36-acf0-3b9c18a6d1d9","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_018hmsP8SPX1EATCxMd8KeEV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GDLneRv8U1AtDrGeH6E7e5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\drill-me.md","content":"# /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n\n> Interrogate the user about a domain area to build/refine the ubiquitous language glossary.\n> Inspired by mattpocock/grill-me, customized for DDD purposes. Body delegates to `ubiquitous-language` skill for term-definition substance.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Before implementing a new feature area (extracts domain terms first)\n- When new domain vocabulary emerges in conversation\n- When glossary and code are drifting (run periodically)\n- At the start of a new bounded context\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — domain area to drill on (e.g., `KOL influence tracking`, `pump detection signals`, `thesis lifecycle`).\n\nIf no argument, ask user what domain area they want to explore.\n\n## Process (8 steps)\n\n1. **Load current state** — read `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` + `domain-mapping.md` + any existing specs in the domain. Identify already-defined terms, undefined concepts, potential synonyms.\n\n2. **Opening question** — frame: \"Let's drill down on [domain area]. I'll ask structured questions to build out the ubiquitous language. Your answers become the canonical domain vocabulary — both human and agent will use these exact terms going forward.\"\n\n3. **Structured question sequence** — ONE question at a time; adapt next question on response. Six phases:\n   - **A. Nouns** — main \"things\" in domain; what each \"always has\"; critical distinctions between similar things\n   - **B. Verbs** — key actions/operations; triggers + expected outcomes; actions that look similar but differ\n   - **C. Lifecycle** — states for key entities; allowed/forbidden transitions; invariants per state\n   - **D. Relationships** — A-to-B cardinality (1:1 / 1:N / N:M); ownership vs reference\n   - **E. Conflict check** — compare new terms with existing glossary; force explicit resolution of every potential synonym\n   - **F. Boundary check** — which of 9 BCs owns each term\n\n4. **Real-time draft entries** — as user answers, build draft per `ubiquitous-language` skill schema (BC / Definition / Lifecycle / Not to confuse with / Code / Introduced). Show draft, ask \"does this capture it accurately?\".\n\n5. **Drift check** — for each proposed term, grep existing code (`grep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"`). If matches: surface contradictions for resolution.\n\n6. **Write to glossary** — append new terms to `glossary.md` (Core Domain or BC-specific section). Renames go to \"Stop List\". Append entry to `drift-log.md`.\n\n7. **Suggest code audit** — if existing code uses terms inconsistently with new glossary, list specifically what needs to change; recommend `/ul-audit` follow-up.\n\n8. **Output summary** — Domain Explored / Terms Added / Terms Refined / Terms Deprecated / Conflicts Resolved / Files Updated / Recommended Follow-up.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Asking all questions at once (overwhelming, loses quality)\n- Accepting vague definitions (\"it's like X but different\") — push for specifics\n- Letting user use same term for two concepts (force differentiation)\n- Skipping conflict check with existing glossary\n- Writing to glossary without user confirmation of drafts\n\n## Do\n\n- Go slowly, one concept at a time\n- Insist on clear distinctions\n- Surface conflicts proactively\n- Use real examples from user's domain\n- Connect new terms to existing terms\n\n## Related\n\n- `ubiquitous-language` skill — passive analysis variant; this command is the interactive variant\n- `/ul-audit` command — code-vs-glossary drift detector; runs after this session\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — output target\n\nFull term-definition schema, drift-log entry template, and extraction output format: `.claude/skills/ubiquitous-language/references/templates.md`.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":11522,"cache_read_input_tokens":178593,"output_tokens":1931,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":11522,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1931,"cache_read_input_tokens":178593,"cache_creation_input_tokens":11522,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":11522},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYU96xvihiz9EavQBNdF","type":"assistant","uuid":"321c4b30-258a-4a07-9de0-44d0aa64a45e","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:37:15.130Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

If matches: surface contradictions for resolution.\n\n6. **Write to glossary** — append new terms to `glossary.md` (Core Domain or BC-specific section). Renames go to \"Stop List\". Append entry to `drift-log.md`.\n\n7. **Suggest code audit** — if existing code uses terms inconsistently with new glossary, list specifically what needs to change; recommend `/ul-audit` follow-up.\n\n8. **Output summary** — Domain Explored / Terms Added / Terms Refined / Terms Deprecated / Conflicts Resolved / Files Updated / Recommended Follow-up.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Asking all questions at once (overwhelming, loses quality)\n- Accepting vague definitions (\"it's like X but different\") — push for specifics\n- Letting user use same term for two concepts (force differentiation)\n- Skipping conflict check with existing glossary\n- Writing to glossary without user confirmation of drafts\n\n## Do\n\n- Go slowly, one concept at a time\n- Insist on clear distinctions\n- Surface conflicts proactively\n- Use real examples from user's domain\n- Connect new terms to existing terms\n\n## Related\n\n- `ubiquitous-language` skill — passive analysis variant; this command is the interactive variant\n- `/ul-audit` command — code-vs-glossary drift detector; runs after this session\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — output target\n\nFull term-definition schema, drift-log entry template, and extraction output format: `.claude/skills/ubiquitous-language/references/templates.md`.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":7,"newStart":1,"newLines":7,"lines":[" # /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction"," "," > Interrogate the user about a domain area to build/refine the ubiquitous language glossary.","-> Inspired by mattpocock/grill-me, customized for DDD purposes.","+> Inspired by mattpocock/grill-me, customized for DDD purposes. Load Current State\n\nRead:\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/domain-mapping.md`\n- Any existing specs in the domain area\n\nIdentify:\n- Terms already in glossary for this area\n- Concepts mentioned but not formally defined\n- Potential synonyms or inconsistencies\n\n### 2. Opening Question\n\nAsk:\n> \"Let's drill down on [domain area]. I'll ask structured questions to build out the ubiquitous language. Your answers become the canonical domain vocabulary — both human and agent will use these exact terms going forward.\n>\n> Ready? First question...\"\n\n### 3. Structured Question Sequence\n\nAsk ONE question at a time. Wait for answer. Adapt next question based on response.\n\n**Phase A: Nouns (what exists in this domain)**\n\n- \"What are the main 'things' in this domain? Name them in the language a domain expert would use.\"\n- For each thing: \"What does a [thing] always have? What can it do?\"\n- \"What differentiates [thing A] from [thing B] — what's the critical distinction?\"\n\n**Phase B: Verbs (what happens)**\n\n- \"What are the key actions/operations in this domain?\"\n- For each action: \"What triggers this? What's the expected outcome?\"\n- \"Are there actions that look similar but are actually different? What distinguishes them?\"\n\n**Phase C: Lifecycle**\n\n- \"Does [key entity] have a lifecycle? What states does it go through?\"\n- \"What transitions between states are allowed? Which are forbidden?\"\n- \"What invariants must hold at each state?\"\n\n**Phase D: Relationships**\n\n- \"How does [thing A] relate to [thing B]?\"\n- \"Is the relationship one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many?\"\n- \"Is the relationship owned (one thing exists only as part of another) or referenced (both can exist independently)?\"\n\n**Phase E: Conflict Check**\n\n- Compare new terms with existing glossary\n- \"I notice you used 'Signal' — we already have 'ExtractedClaim' in the glossary for what sounds similar. Are they the same thing, different, or should we rename?\"\n- Force explicit resolution of every potential synonym\n\n**Phase F: Boundary Check**\n\n- \"Which bounded context does [term] belong in?\"\n- \"If it could be in two BCs, which one owns it and which just references?\"\n\n### 4. Real-Time Glossary Updates\n\nAs user answers, build draft entries:\n\n```markdown\n### [Term]\n**Bounded context**: [from Phase F]\n**Definition**: [from Phase A answers]\n**Lifecycle**: [from Phase C if applicable]\n**Not to confuse with**: [from Phase E]\n**Code**: [to be determined when implementing]\n**Introduced**: [today's date] (via /drill-me session)\n```\n\nShow draft to user: \"Does this capture it accurately?\"\n\n### 5. Check for Drift\n\nFor each term proposed, grep existing code:\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"TermName\\|term_name\\|termName\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"\n```\n\nIf matches found:\n- \"I see this term is already used in code at [locations]. Does your definition match how it's currently used?\"\n- Flag any contradictions for resolution\n\n### 6. Write to Glossary\n\nAfter session ends, append to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`:\n- New terms in appropriate section (Core Domain or BC-specific)\n- If renaming existing term, add to \"Stop List\" old → new mapping\n\nUpdate `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md`:\n```markdown\n## YYYY-MM-DD — Add/Rename/Refine — [terms affected]\n\n**Session**: /drill-me on \"[domain area]\"\n**Terms added**: [list]\n**Terms refined**: [list]  \n**Terms deprecated**: [list]\n**Decisions made**: [any important clarifications]\n```\n\n### 7. Suggest Code Audit\n\nIf any existing code uses terms inconsistently with new glossary:\n- Report specifically what needs to change\n- Suggest running `/ul-audit` after to verify\n\n### 8. Output Summary\n\n```markdown\n# /drill-me Session Complete\n\n## Domain Explored\n[domain area]\n\n## Terms Added ([N])\n- [term] — [one-line definition]\n- ...\n\n## Terms Refined ([N])\n- [term] — [what changed]\n\n## Terms Deprecated ([N])\n- [old term] → use [new term] instead\n\n## Conflicts Resolved\n- [A vs B] → [resolution]\n\n## Files Updated\n- `glossary.md` — N new entries, M edits\n- `drift-log.md` — entry added\n- `domain-mapping.md` — placeholders for new terms\n\n## Recommended Follow-up\n- [ ] Run `/ul-audit` to check existing code alignment\n- [ ] Update specs that use old terms (list: [...])\n- [ ] [Other actions specific to this session]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Ask all questions at once (overwhelming, loses quality)\n- Accept vague definitions (\"it's like X but different\") — push for specifics\n- Let user use same term for two concepts (force differentiation)\n- Skip conflict check with existing glossary\n- Write to glossary without user confirmation of drafts\n\n**Do**:\n- Go slowly, one concept at a time\n- Insist on clear distinctions\n- Surface conflicts proactively\n- Use real examples from user's domain\n- Connect new terms to existing terms\n\n---\n\n## Example Flow\n\n```\nUser: /drill-me KOL influence tracking\n\nAgent: Let's drill down on KOL influence tracking. I'll ask structured questions.\n\nFirst: What are the main \"things\" in this domain? In your language.\n\nUser: KOL, channel, recommendation, calibration record...\n\nAgent: Good. Let's start with KOL. What does a KOL always have?\n\nUser: Name, platform, follower count, track record...\n\nAgent: Does KOL have a lifecycle? Can a KOL become \"inactive\" or \"discredited\"?\n\nUser: Yes — Active, Inactive, Blacklisted\n\nAgent: What triggers Blacklisted? And can a Blacklisted KOL return to Active?\n\nUser: Blacklisted if caught pump-and-dump. No return.\n\nAgent: Important invariant. Let me draft:\n\n### Kol\n**Bounded context**: BC-6 Influence Network\n**Definition**: Named influencer who makes stock recommendations on a public channel.\nHas measurable track record tracked via CredibilityScore.\n**Lifecycle**: Active → Inactive (dormant) → Blacklisted (caught manipulation).\nBlacklisted is terminal — no return.\n**Not to confuse with**: Channel (the platform account a KOL operates)\n\nAccurate so far?\n\n[... continues ...]\n```\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"321c4b30-258a-4a07-9de0-44d0aa64a45e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"e8d80e70-08a9-448b-94b0-84508608b1ae","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0c07ec5e-f80a-4b57-8f42-9e5efe182b9e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GbvJxxuP3bbZwBTrNaiAuK","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n2\t\n3\t> Scan codebase for architectural decay using numbered drift signals.\n4\t\n5\t## When to Use\n6\t\n7\t- End of each session (recommended)\n8\t- Before PR merge (required)\n9\t- When investigating architectural issues\n10\t- Periodically (weekly minimum)\n11\t\n12\t## Input\n13\t\n14\t`$ARGUMENTS` — optional:\n15\t- No arg → run all signals\n16\t- `high` → run HIGH severity only\n17\t- `DR<N>` → run specific signal\n18\t- Example: `/drift-check DR1`\n19\t\n20\t## Process\n21\t\n22\t### 1. Run Each Signal\n27\t\n28\tFor each signal in scope:\n29\t\n30\t**DR1: Domain layer imports framework**\n31\t```bash\n32\tgrep -rn \"from fastapi\\|import fastapi\\|from pydantic\\|import pydantic\\|from sqlalchemy\\|import sqlalchemy\\|from dramatiq\\|import dramatiq\" \\\n33\t  packages/domain/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n34\t```\n35\t\n36\t**DR2: Evidence without citation**\n37\t```bash\n38\t# If DB accessible:\n39\tpsql -c \"SELECT id, text FROM claims WHERE source_url IS NULL OR source_url = '' LIMIT 10;\"\n40\t# If not, skip with note\n41\t```\n42\t\n43\t**DR3: LLM call without retry/budget**\n44\t```bash\n45\tgrep -rn \"anthropic\\.Anthropic\\(\\|client\\.messages\\.create\\|openai\\.OpenAI\\(\" \\\n46\t  packages/infrastructure/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null \\\n47\t  | grep -v \"with_budget\\|with_retry\"\n48\t```\n49\t\n50\t**DR4: Hardcoded prompt outside prompts/**\n51\t```bash\n52\t# Heuristic: long triple-quoted strings in Python files outside prompts/\n53\tgrep -rEn '\"\"\"[^\"]{500,}\"\"\"' packages/application/ apps/ \\\n54\t  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"prompts/\"\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\t**DR5: Claim stored without required metadata**\n58\t```sql\n59\tSELECT id FROM claims \n60\tWHERE source_url IS NULL \n61\t   OR extracted_at IS NULL \n62\t   OR confidence IS NULL LIMIT 10;\n63\t```\n64\t\n65\t**DR6: `Any` type in domain package**\n66\t```bash\n67\tgrep -rn \": Any\\|-> Any\\| Any,\" packages/domain/ \\\n68\t  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n69\t```\n70\t\n71\t**DR7: UL term drift**\n72\t```\n73\tRun /ul-audit for semantic check (handled separately).\n74\t```\n75\t\n76\t**DR8: Cross-BC direct import**\n77\t```bash\n78\tfor BC in market_data fundamental company_intelligence macro news influence crowd analysis portfolio; Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Body delegates execution to the deterministic hook + the `drift-detector` agent (semantic signals).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- End of each session (recommended)\n- Before PR merge (required)\n- When investigating architectural issues\n- Periodically (weekly minimum)\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — optional:\n\n- No arg → run all signals\n- `high` → run HIGH severity only\n- `DR<N>` → run specific signal (e.g., `/drift-check DR1`)\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Load definitions** — read `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` for current signal definitions, severity, and remediation guidance.\n\n2. **Run deterministic signals (DR1-DR9)** — invoke `bash scripts/hooks/drift-signals-D1-D9.sh`. The script handles all regex/grep/sql signals (LOC ceilings, framework imports, citation completeness, hardcoded prompts, claim metadata, `Any` types, cross-BC imports, thesis-without-verifier, learning-data path leaks). Output emits to drift-logs and stdout in the report schema below.\n\n3. **Run semantic signals (DR7 UL drift, DR12 anti-patterns)** — these need LLM inspection. Dispatch the `drift-detector` agent (fresh context, run_in_background) with current artifact set. Agent returns observations file under `agent-workspace/memory/observations/`.\n\n4. **Spec-existence check (DR10)** — extract `SPEC-YYYY-MM-DD-NNN` references via `grep -rhoE` and verify each lives under `specs/`. Report missing.\n\n5. **Stale-handoff check (DR11)** — compare `mtime` of `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` + `current-execution.md` vs latest session log under `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/`. Project.md older than latest session = likely stale.\n\n6. **Aggregate** into the report schema (see \"Report Format\" below). Severity breakdown: HIGH violations block commit; MEDIUM warns; LOW logs.\n\n7. **Write report** to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm.md`.\n\n8. **Exit code** for CI integration: `0` all-PASS / `1` MEDIUM violations only / `2` HIGH violations (blocks CI).\n\n## Report Format\n\n```markdown\n# Drift Check Report — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Summary\n- Scope: [all | high | DR<N>]\n- Total signals run: N\n- Passed: X / Warnings: Y (MEDIUM/LOW) / Violations: Z (HIGH — blocks)\n\n## Results\n| Signal | Severity | Status | Violations | Details |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| DR1 | HIGH | PASS | 0 | LOC ceilings clean |\n| DR2 | HIGH | CHECK | - | DB unavailable, skipped |\n| DR3 | MEDIUM | FAIL | 2 | See below |\n...\n\n## Violations Detail\n### DRn (severity) — title\n- File:line — issue + suggested fix\n\n## Recommendations\n- Blocking (must fix before commit): [HIGH list]\n- Should fix this session: [MEDIUM list]\n- Tracked for later: [LOW list]\n```\n\n## Auto-Fix (offered, not applied)\n\nFor some signals, suggest fixes without applying:\n\n- DR6 (`Any` types) → suggest concrete types (mypy --strict will catch these)\n- DR3 (unwrapped LLM calls) → show wrapper pattern from `packages/infrastructure/llm/` shared budget+retry helper\n\nUser explicitly approves before any fix is applied.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Skipping drift check because \"it takes too long\" (the hook runs in <2s)\n- Ignoring HIGH violations with TODO comments\n- Running only some signals regularly — do all periodically\n\n## Do\n\n- Run before every commit\n- Fix HIGH immediately\n- Track MEDIUM for next session\n- Add new signals to `drift-signals.md` + hook when new patterns emerge\n\n## Related\n\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` — signal specialized Load Definitions\n\nRead `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` for current definitions.\n\n### 2. Run Each Signal\n\nFor each signal in scope:\n\n**DR1: Domain layer imports framework**\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"from fastapi\\|import fastapi\\|from pydantic\\|import pydantic\\|from sqlalchemy\\|import sqlalchemy\\|from dramatiq\\|import dramatiq\" \\\n  packages/domain/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n```\n\n**DR2: Evidence without citation**\n```bash\n# If DB accessible:\npsql -c \"SELECT id, text FROM claims WHERE source_url IS NULL OR source_url = '' LIMIT 10;\"\n# If not, skip with note\n```\n\n**DR3: LLM call without retry/budget**\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"anthropic\\.Anthropic\\(\\|client\\.messages\\.create\\|openai\\.OpenAI\\(\" \\\n  packages/infrastructure/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null \\\n  | grep -v \"with_budget\\|with_retry\"\n```\n\n**DR4: Hardcoded prompt outside prompts/**\n```bash\n# Heuristic: long triple-quoted strings in Python files outside prompts/\ngrep -rEn '\"\"\"[^\"]{500,}\"\"\"' packages/application/ apps/ \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"prompts/\"\n```\n\n**DR5: Claim stored without required metadata**\n```sql\nSELECT id FROM claims \nWHERE source_url IS NULL \n   OR extracted_at IS NULL \n   OR confidence IS NULL LIMIT 10;\n```\n\n**DR6: `Any` type in domain package**\n```bash\ngrep -rn \": Any\\|-> Any\\| Any,\" packages/domain/ \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n```\n\n**DR7: UL term drift**\n```\nRun /ul-audit for semantic check (handled separately).\n```\n\n**DR8: Cross-BC direct import**\n```bash\nfor BC in market_data fundamental company_intelligence macro news influence crowd analysis portfolio; do\n  echo \"Checking $BC...\"\n  grep -rn \"from packages.domain\\.\" packages/domain/$BC/ \\\n    --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"packages.domain.$BC\\.\"\ndone\n```\n\n**DR9: Thesis output without verifier step**\n```sql\nSELECT t.id FROM theses t\nLEFT JOIN verifier_runs vr ON vr.thesis_id = t.id\nWHERE vr.id IS NULL AND t.status = 'active' LIMIT 10;\n```\n\n**DR10: Spec referenced doesn't exist**\n```bash\n# Extract all SPEC-YYYY-MM-DD-NNN references\ngrep -rhoE \"SPEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{3}\" . \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" --include=\"*.md\" 2>/dev/null | sort -u \\\n  | while read spec_id; do\n      if ! find specs -name \"*${spec_id}*\" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then\n        echo \"Missing: $spec_id\"\n      fi\n    done\n```\n\n**DR11: Stale session-handoff**\n```bash\n# Last modified time of state files\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/project.md 2>/dev/null\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md 2>/dev/null\n# Latest session log\nls -t agent-workspace/memory/sessions/ 2>/dev/null | head -1\n# Compare — if project.md older than latest session, likely stale\n```\n\n**DR12: Anti-pattern from agent-notes.md**\n```\nSemantic check — read agent-notes.md, look for documented anti-patterns, \nsearch codebase for their patterns. Requires LLM inspection.\n```\n\n### 3. Aggregate Results\n\nBuild summary table:\n\n```markdown\n# Drift Check Report — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Summary\n- **Scope**: [all | high | DR<N>]\n- **Total signals run**: N\n- **Passed**: X\n- **Warnings**: Y (MEDIUM/LOW)\n- **Violations**: Z (HIGH — blocks commit)\n\n## Results\n\n| Signal | Severity | Status | Violations | Details |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| DR1 | HIGH | PASS | 0 | Domain layer clean |\n| DR2 | HIGH | CHECK | - | DB unavailable, skipped |\n| DR3 | MEDIUM | FAIL | 2 | See below |\n| DR4 | MEDIUM | PASS | 0 | No large inline prompts |\n| ... | | | | |\n\n## Violations Detail\n\n### DR3 (MEDIUM) — LLM call without retry/budget\n\n**Violations found**: 2\n\n1. `packages/infrastructure/analysis/bear_agent.py:45`\n   - Direct `client.messages.create` call\n   - Fix: wrap with `with_budget()` and `with_retry()`\n\n2. `apps/workers/kol_extractor.py:23`\n   - Direct anthropic API call\n   - Fix: use shared budget wrapper\n\n## Recommendations\n\n### Blocking (must fix before commit)\n- [HIGH violations if any]\n\n### Should fix this session\n- [MEDIUM violations]\n\n### Tracked for later\n- [LOW violations]\n```\n\n### 4. Write Report\n\nSave report to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm.md`.\n\n### 5. Block or Allow\n\n- If ANY HIGH violations → block commit, require fix\n- If MEDIUM violations → warn, allow with awareness\n- If LOW only → log and continue\n\n### 6. Auto-Fix When Possible\n\nFor some signals, offer fixes:\n- DR6 (Any types): suggest proper types (mypy --strict will catch these)\n- DR3 (unwrapped LLM calls): show wrapper pattern\n\nDon't auto-apply — suggest, let user approve.\n\n---\n\n## Exit Codes (for CI integration)\n\n- 0: all PASS\n- 1: MEDIUM violations only\n- 2: HIGH violations (blocks CI)\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Skip drift check because \"it takes too long\"\n- Ignore HIGH violations with TODO comments\n- Run only some signals regularly (do all periodically)\n\n**Do**:\n- Run before every commit\n- Fix HIGH immediately\n- Track MEDIUM for next session\n- Add new signals when new patterns emerge\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"cc20ab82-d8f1-4c37-b93d-29e8a138f661","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Pre-flight\n\nBefore invoking subagent:\n- Identify scope: is this a phase-level goal or feature-level?\n- Check existing session-plans/pending/ for overlap\n- Ensure spec exists for what's being planned (or planning will produce spec)\n\n### 2. Invoke master-planner Subagent\n\nSpawn subagent via Task tool with:\n\n**Persona**: Senior technical lead who thinks in sessions, budgets, and verifiable success criteria.\n\n**Input context**:\n- Goal description\n- PROJECT_CHARTER.md\n- AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md (sections on phases, sandwich pattern, budgets)\n- Relevant constitution files\n- current-execution.md (for phase alignment)\n- Recent session logs (for pace calibration)\n\n**Task**: Produce structured session plan.\n\n**Budget**: 20-30K for subagent context, 10-15K for output.\n\n### 3. Subagent Process\n\nThe subagent:\n\n**Step 1**: Break down goal into logical units\n- Identify dependencies\n- Group related work\n- Separate PLAN work from IMPL work (sandwich pattern)\n- Identify THESIS sessions separately from implementation sessions\n\n**Step 2**: Estimate each unit\n- Context budget per unit (using session-budgets.md formula)\n- Session type for each unit (PLAN/FOCUSED_IMPL/MULTI_TASK_IMPL/VERIFY/THESIS/INGEST/POST-MORTEM)\n- Critical files to load\n\n**Step 3**: Check against 250K hard cap\n- If any session > 250K → split\n- Verify no session mixes PLAN + IMPL\n\n**Step 4**: Identify verification points\n- After which sessions to run VERIFY (sandwich)\n- Where human gates apply\n- Where drift-check needed\n\n**Step 5**: Write session plans to `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/NNN-name.md`\n\n### 4. Subagent Output Format\n\nPer session plan:\n\n```markdown\n# Session Plan: [N. Title]\n\n## Meta\n- **Spec/feature**: [reference]\n- **Session type**: [PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n- **Prerequisites**: [previous sessions/work that must complete first]\n- **Agent to use**: [main | sandwich-architect | sandwich-dev | sandwich-verifier]\n\n## Goal (Success Criteria)\n[Verifiable outcome — what's done when this is done?]\n\n## Context Budget\n- Fixed overhead: X K\n- Variable specific to this: Y K\n- Working space: Z K\n- **Total estimate**: Total K (of 250K cap)\n- **Status**: [within budget | split recommended]\n\n## Context to Load\n### Constitution (always)\n- CLAUDE.md\n- architecture.md, invariants.md, vbw-protocol.md\n\n### Specific to this session\n- Glossary sections: [BC names]\n- Spec: [paths]\n- Code files: [paths]\n- Skills: [which skills to activate]\n\n## Task Breakdown\n1. [Task with verification check]\n2. [Task with verification check]\n3. [Task with verification check]\n\n## Verification\n- [ ] All tasks complete\n- [ ] Deterministic gates pass (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- [ ] [Specific checks for this session]\n\n## Handoff to Next Session\n- Expected output of this session\n- What next session needs\n- What must be in agent-notes.md if learned\n\n## Risks\n- [Risk] → mitigation\n```\n\n### 5. Output Master Plan Summary\n\n```markdown\n# Master Plan — [Goal]\n\n## Overview\n**Goal**: [stated goal]\n**Estimated duration**: N sessions, ~M hours\n**Phase**: [X]\n\n## Session Sequence\n\n| # | Title | Type | Budget | Depends on |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | [title] | PLAN | 60K | - |\n| 2 | [title] | FOCUSED_IMPL | 120K | 1 |\n| 3 | [title] | VERIFY | 40K | 2 |\n| 4 | [title] | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | 200K | 3 |\n| ... | | | | |\n\n**Total estimated**: ~X tokens across Y sessions\n\n## Critical Path\n1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → ...\n\n## Parallel Opportunities\nSessions 5 and 6 are independent, could be done out of order.\n\n## Sandwich Structure\n- Architect sessions: 1, 4, 7\n- Dev sessions: 2, 5, 8\n- Verifier sessions: 3, 6, 9\n\n## Risks / Contingencies\n- [Risk]: if it materializes, add recovery session N.5\n\n## Files Written\nSession plans stored at:\n- `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/001-[title].md`\n- `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/002-[title].md`\n- ...\n\n## Next Action\nReview session plans. When ready:\n1. Pick up session 1 via `/session-start \"session 1 from master plan\"`\n2. Or adjust any plans that look wrong\n```\n\n### 6. Review with User\n\nUser reviews:\n- Are session boundaries logical?\n- Budgets realistic?\n- Any missing work?\n- Sequence makes sense?\n\nAdjustments as needed.\n\n### 7. Update Current Execution\n\nWhen plan approved, update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md`:\n- Add to active work items\n- Set session 1 as next to pick up\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Plan more than one phase at a time (too speculative)\n- Mix PLAN + IMPL in one session (catastrophic failure mode)\n- Assume sessions can exceed 250K \"if careful\" (quality cliff is real)\n- Skip verification sessions (cumulative drift)\n- Mix THESIS sessions with IMPL sessions (THESIS is read-only on code)\n\n**Do**:\n- Right-size sessions (not too big, not too many small)\n- Plan recovery sessions for risky work\n- Identify parallelizable sessions for flexibility\n- Keep session plans in git (review-able, diff-able)\n","numLines":202,"startLine":1,"totalLines":202}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a8a000e9-b0dc-4e73-87d8-769b70417569","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"e5ba63f7-6bca-4611-9f9e-33e52f9b2e7e","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. {"parentUuid":"f95adecc-aaab-419e-9d58-cd8eb0143a69","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01GcofqxFYzsCpjRCZynt2xx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UTyAPErdJPSs3x6oTh9yM9","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\master-plan.md","content":"# /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n\n> Invoke `master-planner` subagent (fresh context, run_in_background) to decompose a goal into phased, budgeted sessions following the sandwich pattern.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Start of new phase\n- When a large goal needs breakdown\n- When plan has >10 tasks and needs splitting\n- When approaching unfamiliar territory\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — goal or objective to decompose (e.g., `implement Phase 1 thin slice`, `build KOL channel monitoring pipeline`).\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Pre-flight** — identify scope (phase-level vs feature-level). Check `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for overlap. Ensure spec exists for what's being planned (or planning will produce one).\n\n2. **Dispatch `master-planner` subagent** with: goal description, `PROJECT_CHARTER.md`, `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` (phases / sandwich / budgets), relevant `agent-workspace/constitution/` files, `current-execution.md` (phase alignment), recent session logs (pace calibration). Subagent budget: 20-30K context + 10-15K output.\n\n3. **Subagent decomposes** — break into logical units with dependencies; group related work; separate PLAN from IMPL (sandwich pattern); identify THESIS sessions separately. Per-unit: estimate context budget via `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` formula; pick session type (PLAN / FOCUSED_IMPL / MULTI_TASK_IMPL / VERIFY / RECOVERY / THESIS / INGEST / POST-MORTEM); list critical files. Verify no session > 250K hard cap, no session mixes PLAN+IMPL.\n\n4. **Identify verification points** — where to insert VERIFY sessions (sandwich), human gates, drift-check runs.\n\n5. **Subagent writes** per-session plans to `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/NNN-name.md` using SPEC_TEMPLATE-style schema: Meta (spec/feature, session_type, prerequisites, agent) / Goal (verifiable success criteria) / Context Budget (fixed + variable + working = total) / Context to Load (constitution + specific) / Task Breakdown (numbered with verification check per task) / Verification (deterministic gates + specific checks) / Handoff to Next Session / Risks.\n\n6. **Master-plan summary** — overview row showing Goal / Estimated duration / Phase / Session sequence table (`# | Title | Type | Budget | Depends on`) / Critical Path / Parallel Opportunities / Sandwich Structure (Architect-Dev-Verifier rotation) / Risks-Contingencies / Files Written.\n\n7. **Review with user** — session boundaries logical? Budgets realistic? Missing work? Sequence makes sense? Adjustments before commit.\n\n8. **Update `current-execution.md`** — append to active work items; set session 1 as next pickup.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Planning more than one phase at a time (too speculative)\n- Mixing PLAN + IMPL in one session (catastrophic — Session 4 failure mode)\n- Assuming sessions can exceed 250K \"if careful\" (quality cliff is real)\n- Skipping verification sessions (cumulative drift)\n- Mixing THESIS with IMPL (THESIS is read-only on code per CLAUDE.md)\n\n## Do\n\n- Right-size sessions (not too big, not too many small)\n- Plan recovery sessions for risky work\n- Identify parallelizable sessions for flexibility\n- Keep session plans in git (review-able, diff-able)\n\n## Related\n\n- `master-planner` agent — does the actual decomposition\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` — budget formulas (fixed + variable + working)\n- `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` — session plan schema source\n- `/session-start` — picks up the produced plans\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10217,"cache_read_input_tokens":199864,"output_tokens":1851,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":10217,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1851,"cache_read_input_tokens":199864,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10217,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":10217},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUEhPWuqzvwQVwv69m8","type":"assistant","uuid":"1868f8bc-0c35-4f8c-8704-a065f78144fe","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:38:31.807Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Pre-flight\n\nBefore invoking subagent:\n- Identify scope: is this a phase-level goal or feature-level?\n- Check existing session-plans/pending/ for overlap\n- Ensure spec exists for what's being planned (or planning will produce spec)\n\n### 2. Invoke master-planner Subagent\n\nSpawn subagent via Task tool with:\n\n**Persona**: Senior technical lead who thinks in sessions, budgets, and verifiable success criteria.\n\n**Input context**:\n- Goal description\n- PROJECT_CHARTER.md\n- AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md (sections on phases, sandwich pattern, budgets)\n- Relevant constitution files\n- current-execution.md (for phase alignment)\n- Recent session logs (for pace calibration)\n\n**Task**: Produce structured session plan.\n\n**Budget**: 20-30K for subagent context, 10-15K for output.\n\n### 3. Subagent Process\n\nThe subagent:\n\n**Step 1**: Break down goal into logical units\n- Identify dependencies\n- Group related work\n- Separate PLAN work from IMPL work (sandwich pattern)\n- Identify THESIS sessions separately from implementation sessions\n\n**Step 2**: Estimate each unit\n- Context budget per unit (using session-budgets.md formula)\n- Session type for each unit (PLAN/FOCUSED_IMPL/MULTI_TASK_IMPL/VERIFY/THESIS/INGEST/POST-MORTEM)\n- Critical files to load\n\n**Step 3**: Check against 250K hard cap\n- If any session > 250K → split\n- Verify no session mixes PLAN + IMPL\n\n**Step 4**: Identify verification points\n- After which sessions to run VERIFY (sandwich)\n- Where human gates apply\n- Where drift-check needed\n\n**Step 5**: Write session plans to `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/NNN-name.md`\n\n### 4. Subagent Output Format\n\nPer session plan:\n\n```markdown\n# Session Plan: [N. Title]\n\n## Meta\n- **Spec/feature**: [reference]\n- **Session type**: [PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n- **Prerequisites**: [previous sessions/work that must complete first]\n- **Agent to use**: [main | sandwich-architect | sandwich-dev | sandwich-verifier]\n\n## Goal (Success Criteria)\n[Verifiable outcome — what's done when this is done?]\n\n## Context Budget\n- Fixed overhead: X K\n- Variable specific to this: Y K\n- Working space: Z K\n- **Total estimate**: Total K (of 250K cap)\n- **Status**: [within budget | split recommended]\n\n## Context to Load\n### Constitution (always)\n- CLAUDE.md\n- architecture.md, invariants.md, vbw-protocol.md\n\n### Specific to this session\n- Glossary sections: [BC names]\n- Spec: [paths]\n- Code files: [paths]\n- Skills: [which skills to activate]\n\n## Task Breakdown\n1. [Task with verification check]\n2. [Task with verification check]\n3. [Task with verification check]\n\n## Verification\n- [ ] All tasks complete\n- [ ] Deterministic gates pass (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- [ ] [Specific checks for this session]\n\n## Handoff to Next Session\n- Expected output of this session\n- What next session needs\n- What must be in agent-notes.md if learned\n\n## Risks\n- [Risk] → mitigation\n```\n\n### 5. Output Master Plan Summary\n\n```markdown\n# Master Plan — [Goal]\n\n## Overview\n**Goal**: [stated goal]\n**Estimated duration**: N sessions, ~M hours\n**Phase**: [X]\n\n## Session Sequence\n\n| # | Title | Type | Budget | Depends on |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | [title] | PLAN | 60K | - |\n| 2 | [title] | FOCUSED_IMPL | 120K | 1 |\n| 3 | [title] | VERIFY | 40K | 2 |\n| 4 | [title] | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | 200K | 3 |\n| ... | | | | |\n\n**Total estimated**: ~X tokens across Y sessions\n\n## Critical Path\n1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → ...\n\n## Parallel Opportunities\nSessions 5 and 6 are independent, could be done out of order.\n\n## Sandwich Structure\n- Architect sessions: 1, 4, 7\n- Dev sessions: 2, 5, 8\n- Verifier sessions: 3, 6, 9\n\n## Risks / Contingencies\n- [Risk]: if it materializes, add recovery session N.5\n\n## Files Written\nSession plans stored at:\n- `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/001-[title].md`\n- `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/002-[title].md`\n- ...\n\n## Next Action\nReview session plans. When ready:\n1. Pick up session 1 via `/session-start \"session 1 from master plan\"`\n2. Or adjust any plans that look wrong\n```\n\n### 6. Review with User\n\nUser reviews:\n- Are session boundaries logical?\n- Budgets realistic?\n- Any missing work?\n- Sequence makes sense?\n\nAdjustments as needed.\n\n### 7. Update Current Execution\n\nWhen plan approved, update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md`:\n- Add to active work items\n- Set session 1 as next to pick up\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Plan more than one phase at a time (too speculative)\n- Mix PLAN + IMPL in one session (catastrophic failure mode)\n- Assume sessions can exceed 250K \"if careful\" (quality cliff is real)\n- Skip verification sessions (cumulative drift)\n- Mix THESIS sessions with IMPL sessions (THESIS is read-only on code)\n\n**Do**:\n- Right-size sessions (not too big, not too many small)\n- Plan recovery sessions for risky work\n- Identify parallelizable sessions for flexibility\n- Keep session plans in git (review-able, diff-able)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1868f8bc-0c35-4f8c-8704-a065f78144fe","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
