{"parentUuid":"012e4c8b-cfc8-409d-adf4-3b0ca5dabe63","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"c7423aa4-2255-4df4-abf7-4a382016ee46","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:38:33.154Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"6f1e7e4b-40d8-4791-9943-8142813a4eb2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_013D8xvkdJVtv5uqANsDdpng","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01RE1CqJsXuvGXzn6MJno8F8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\ul-audit.md","content":"# /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n\n> Check that code identifiers match canonical terms in `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`. Body delegates substance to the `ul-auditor` agent (semantic synonym detection) + grep-based deterministic checks.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- After new terms added via `/drill-me`\n- Monthly maintenance\n- When suspicion of term drift\n- Before phase boundary\n- After significant refactoring\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — depth selector: `quick` (~2 min — HIGH severity stop-list only; pre-commit / end-of-session) or `full` (~10-15 min — all terms, all files, specs, synonym detection; default).\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Load canonical terms** — read `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`. Extract every defined term, canonical spelling, and the \"Stop List\" (terms we explicitly do NOT use).\n\n2. **Scan code for term usage** — for each canonical term, `grep -rn \"TermName\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\"` plus case-insensitive variant patterns to catch snake_case / camelCase / PascalCase variants. Map term → variants found → status (OK / DRIFT).\n\n3. **Stop-list check** — for each entry in Stop List (e.g., `Recommendation` when canonical is `KolRecommendation`), grep code identifiers (`class X`, `def x`, `: X`). For each hit, determine if it refers to the canonical concept.\n\n4. **Domain mapping accuracy** — read `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/domain-mapping.md`. For each term with code location listed, verify file exists and class/dataclass uses canonical name.\n\n5. **Synonym detection (semantic)** — dispatch `ul-auditor` agent (fresh context, run_in_background) to find concept-level synonyms grep cannot catch (e.g., `Analysis` and `Report` both used for the `Thesis` concept). Agent reads candidate clusters and returns observations.\n\n6. **Spec consistency cross-check** — for each spec in `specs/`: terms used exist in glossary? Same term used consistently within spec? Match terms used in implementing code?\n\n7. **Output audit report** with sections: Summary (canonical terms / files scanned / specs scanned / violations) / Status (`CLEAN` | `DRIFT DETECTED` | `MAJOR DRIFT`) / Term Usage Coverage table / Violations Detail (each numbered V-N with term, canonical, found-at file:line, suggested fix) / Domain Mapping Gaps / Spec Consistency / Recommendations split into Must-Fix (DRIFT), Suggested (consistency), Maintenance.\n\n8. **Suggest fixes — DON'T auto-apply** — propose specific renames and updates per violation. User explicitly approves before any apply.\n\n9. **Log audit** — write report to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/ul-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Append entry to `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` with date, violations summary, fix status.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Skipping audit because \"code works anyway\"\n- Only fixing HIGH violations (MEDIUM accumulates)\n- Auto-renaming without user review (breaks intentional distinctions)\n\n## Do\n\n- Run periodically even without complaints\n- Fix drift as it emerges (cheap to fix early)\n- Update glossary if new terminology is genuinely better — don't silently rename code without glossary update\n\n## Related\n\n- `ul-auditor` agent — semantic synonym detector (step 5)\n- `ubiquitous-language` skill — passive analysis (term-definition substance)\n- `/drill-me` — interactive extraction (input source for new terms)\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` — canonical terms\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/domain-mapping.md` — term → code location\n- `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md` — change log\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9476,"cache_read_input_tokens":210081,"output_tokens":1803,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9476,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1803,"cache_read_input_tokens":210081,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9476,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9476},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUHE43ZPj6b8jmZsJmZ","type":"assistant","uuid":"f2fc2d2a-d7d1-42bd-a608-2b4a07ab3770","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:39:02.065Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Load Canonical Terms\n\nRead `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`:\n- Extract every defined term\n- Note canonical spelling\n- Note \"Stop List\" (terms we do NOT use)\n\n### 2. Scan Codebase for Term Usage\n\nFor each canonical term, grep codebase:\n\n```bash\n# Exact match (Python)\ngrep -rn \"TermName\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null\n\n# Case variations (snake_case for vars, PascalCase for classes)\ngrep -rniE \"term.{0,1}name\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null\n```\n\n### 3. Check for Stop-List Terms\n\nFor each term in \"Stop List\" (e.g., \"Report\" when we use \"Thesis\"):\n\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"class Report\\|def report\\|: Report\" packages/ apps/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null\n# For each hit, determine if it's referring to Thesis concept\n```\n\n### 4. Check Domain Mapping Accuracy\n\nRead `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/domain-mapping.md`:\n- For each term with code location listed, verify file exists\n- Verify class/dataclass at location uses canonical name\n- Flag mismatches\n\n### 5. Detect Synonyms in Use\n\nLook for multiple terms referring to same concept:\n\nExamples:\n- `Analysis` class AND `Report` class (suspicious)\n- `Kol` class AND `Influencer` class used interchangeably\n- `Claim` AND `Fact` AND `Datapoint` (canonical: Claim)\n- `Thesis` AND `Report` AND `Signal` (canonical: Thesis)\n\nUse semantic inspection — not just grep — to identify likely synonyms.\n\n### 6. Rename Recommendation → KolRecommendation across files\n2. Rename Signal → ExtractedClaim (news context)\n\n### Suggested (for consistency)\n1. Update spec #002 to use canonical terms\n2. Log Audit\n\nAppend to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/ul-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`.\n\nUpdate `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/drift-log.md`:\n```markdown\n## YYYY-MM-DD — Audit — [N violations found]\n\n**Session**: /ul-audit\n**Violations**: [brief summary]\n**Fix status**: [fixed | pending | documented]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Depth Levels\n\n### Quick Scan\n- Just check HIGH severity violations\n- Stop-list term usage\n- Time: ~2 minutes\n- Use when: pre-commit, end of session\n\n### Full Audit\n- All terms, all files, all specs\n- Synonym detection\n- Mapping accuracy\n- Time: ~10-15 minutes\n- Use when: monthly, before phase boundary, after refactoring\n\nSpecify depth with `/ul-audit quick` or `/ul-audit full` (default: full).\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Skip audit because \"code works anyway\"\n- Only fix HIGH violations (MEDIUM accumulates)\n- Auto-rename without user review (breaks intentional distinctions)\n\n**Do**:\n- Run periodically even without complaints\n- Fix drift as it emerges (cheap to fix early)\n- Update glossary if new terminology is better (don't silently rename)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f2fc2d2a-d7d1-42bd-a608-2b4a07ab3770","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Determine session type\n\nUsing `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` decision tree:\n\n```\nQ1: Detailed plan already exists for this goal?\n  NO → Type: PLAN (use sandwich-architect subagent)\n  YES → Q2\n\nQ2: How many tasks in plan?\n  1-3 small → Type: FOCUSED_IMPL\n  4-10 → Type: MULTI_TASK_IMPL\n  >10 → SPLIT recommendation\n\nQ3: Previous session failed or left broken state?\n  YES → Type: RECOVERY (prepend to planned type)\n\nQ4: Need to verify previous session's output?\n  YES → Schedule VERIFY after main work\n\nQ5: Goal is investment thesis analysis on a stock?\n  YES → Type: THESIS (read-only on code, outputs to thesis-log/)\n\nQ6: Goal is ingesting new data sources or KOL channels?\n  YES → Type: INGEST\n\nQ7: Goal is reviewing past thesis outcomes?\n  YES → Type: POST-MORTEM\n```\n\n### 4. Estimate context budget\n\nPer `session-budgets.md` estimation:\n```\nFixed overhead: ~12K\n+ Bounded contexts needed: 5K each\n+ Specs needed: 3-4K each\n+ Files to read: 2K each\n+ Skills loaded: 1.5K each\n+ Working space: ~30% of total\n= Estimated budget\n```\n\nIf > 250K → flag and recommend split.\n\n### 5. Check for matching session plan\n\nLook in `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for file matching goal.\nIf found, load and use as execution guide.\nIf not, note need to create one via `/master-plan`.\n\n### 6. Output session brief\n\nFormat:\n\n```markdown\n# Session Brief — [DATE] Session N\n\n## Goal\n[One sentence description]\n\n## Session Type\n[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n\n## Context Budget Estimate\n- Fixed overhead: X K\n- Variable (specific to this session): Y K\n- Output working space: Z K\n- **Total estimate**: Total K (of 250K hard cap)\n\n## Status Check\n- Active phase: [from current-execution.md]\n- Recent sessions (last 3 summary):\n  - Session N-1: [one line]\n  - Session N-2: [one line]\n  - Session N-3: [one line]\n- Pending from last: [if any]\n\n## Files Loaded\n[List of files read]\n\n## Skills/Agents Relevant\n[List of skills that may be invoked]\n\n## Constraints Active (from constitution)\n[Key invariants relevant to this session]\n[For THESIS sessions: adversarial-by-default, no-LLM-math, bear-case-required]\n[For code sessions: mypy --strict, no Pydantic in domain, cross-BC via contracts only]\n\n## Proposed Next Actions\n1. [Action 1]\n2. [Action 2]\n3. [Action 3]\n\n---\n\nReady to proceed? Confirm or adjust.\n```\n\n### 7. Wait for user confirmation\n\nDo NOT begin substantive work until user confirms or adjusts the brief.\n\n---\n\n## First Session Handling\n\nIf this is the first session ever (Phase 0, Session 1):\n\nOutput:\n\n```markdown\n# Welcome to StockForge\n\nI see this is the first session. Let me guide you through setup.\n\n## Project State\nPhase: 0 (Project Setup)\nStatus: Starter kit just downloaded / initialized\n\n## What I See\n- CLAUDE.md loaded\n- Constitution files present\n- Ubiquitous language seeded\n- No session logs yet\n- No code written yet\n\n## Recommended First Steps (Day 1 Checklist)\n\nBefore building anything:\n\n1. Read `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (30 min, not skippable — 10 principles + signal architecture)\n2. Skim `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` Sections 1-5 (30 min)\n3. Customize `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` if your stack differs\n4. Run `/drill-me \"KOL influence tracking\"` to start refining the stock domain glossary\n5. Identify 3-5 VN stocks you want to cover first (eval set for thesis validation)\n\nFull checklist: `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md`\n\n## Options\n\nA. Run the Day 1 checklist step by step\nB. Jump straight to first spec review\nC. Just explore the codebase first\n\nWhat would you like to do?\n```\n\nWait for user choice before proceeding.\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- If any memory file is missing/corrupted → report specifically, don't guess\n- If constitution file missing → CRITICAL, don't proceed\n- If current-execution.md contradicts project.md → flag for human resolution\n- If budget estimate > 250K → recommend split before starting\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n- Don't skip reading memory files \"to save time\" — costs more later\n- Don't load entire codebase upfront — use just-in-time in execution\n- Don't guess session type — follow decision tree\n- Don't proceed without user confirming brief — ensures alignment\n- Don't start THESIS session and write code (THESIS is read-only on code)\n","numLines":200,"startLine":1,"totalLines":200}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9d84eaac-fabe-4f54-a923-4846087d5402","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0476e2eb-e93b-4e7f-8277-a7d6350bde7c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01BHKBhpNVf5JxjPkpf6oqhD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MDSkpNZUzY2rNZiXRxPNZ9","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\session-start.md","content":"# /session-start — Begin Work Session\n\n> Loads project context, identifies session type, outputs session brief. Body delegates loading discipline to `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` § Reading Priority + `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` § decision tree.\n\n## When to Use\n\nAt the start of every meaningful work session with Claude Code.\n\n## Input\n\nOptional: `$ARGUMENTS` — session goal (e.g., `implement KOL channel crawler`, `thesis on VCB`). If no goal, infer from `current-execution.md` or ask.\n\n## Steps\n\n1. **First-session check** — if `current-execution.md` shows Phase 0 + Session N=1, jump to \"First Session Handling\" (delegate to `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md`).\n\n2. **Load project state** in priority order (per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` § Reading Priority):\n   - `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` (active track)\n   - `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` (project state)\n   - `agent-workspace/memory/checkpoints/latest.md` if recent (within 24h)\n   - `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` (learned rules)\n   - `agent-workspace/memory/mistake-log.md` (failure catalog)\n   - Last 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/`\n   - Pattern files in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/` matching goal keywords\n\n3. **Determine session type** via `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` decision tree:\n   - No detailed plan exists → **PLAN** (sandwich-architect subagent)\n   - Plan exists, 1-3 small tasks → **FOCUSED_IMPL**; 4-10 → **MULTI_TASK_IMPL**; >10 → recommend split\n   - Previous session failed/broken → prepend **RECOVERY**\n   - Need to verify previous session output → schedule **VERIFY** after main work\n   - Goal is investment thesis on a stock → **THESIS** (read-only on code; outputs to `thesis-log/`)\n   - Goal is data ingest / KOL channels → **INGEST**\n   - Goal is reviewing past thesis outcomes → **POST-MORTEM**\n\n4. **Estimate context budget** per `session-budgets.md` formula: `fixed (~12K)` + `BCs needed × 5K` + `specs × 3-4K` + `files × 2K` + `skills × 1.5K` + `working space (~30%)`. If > 250K → flag, recommend split.\n\n5. **Match session plan** — look in `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for goal match. Load if found; otherwise note need to run `/master-plan`.\n\n6. **Output session brief** (see \"Brief Schema\" below).\n\n7. **Wait for user confirmation** — do NOT begin substantive work until user confirms or adjusts.\n\n## Brief Schema\n\n```markdown\n# Session Brief — [DATE] Session N\n\n## Goal\n[One sentence]\n\n## Session Type\n[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n\n## Context Budget Estimate\n- Fixed overhead: X K / Variable: Y K / Working: Z K → Total: T K (of 250K cap)\n\n## Status Check\n- Active phase: [from current-execution.md]\n- Recent sessions (last 3, one-line each)\n- Pending from last session (if any)\n\n## Files Loaded / Skills Relevant / Constraints Active\n[Lists; THESIS sessions cite adversarial-by-default + I-S1 no-LLM-math + I-S10 bear-case-required]\n\n## Proposed Next Actions\n1. ... 2. ... 3. ...\n\nReady to proceed? Confirm or adjust.\n```\n\n## First Session Handling\n\nIf Phase 0 + Session 1: output a welcome that frames Day 1 as a checklist and delegates to `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md` (read charter, skim AOM, customize architecture, run `/drill-me` to seed glossary, identify 3-5 VN stocks for eval set). Offer 3 choices: (A) walk Day 1 checklist, (B) jump to first spec review, (C) explore codebase first. Confirm or adjust.\n```\n\n## First Session Handling\n\nIf Phase 0 + Session 1: output a welcome that frames Day 1 as a checklist and delegates to `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md` (read charter, skim AOM, customize architecture, run `/drill-me` to seed glossary, identify 3-5 VN stocks for eval set). sessions"]}],"originalFile":"# /session-start — Begin Work Session\n\n> Loads project context, identifies session type, outputs session brief.\n\n## When to Use\n\nAt the start of every meaningful work session with Claude Code.\n\n## Input\n\nOptional: `$ARGUMENTS` — session goal (e.g., \"implement KOL channel crawler\", \"thesis on VCB\")\n\nIf no goal provided, infer from `current-execution.md` or ask.\n\n## Steps\n\n### 1. Check if first session ever\n\nRead `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md`:\n- If Phase = 0 and Session N = 1 → this is **first session**\n- Skip to \"First Session Handling\" below\n- Otherwise proceed to step 2\n\n### 2. Load project state\n\nRead in order (small to large):\n1. `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` → active track\n2. `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` → project state  \n3. Last 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/` → recent context\n4. Relevant pattern files in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/` (based on goal keywords)\n\n### 3. Determine session type\n\nUsing `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` decision tree:\n\n```\nQ1: Detailed plan already exists for this goal?\n  NO → Type: PLAN (use sandwich-architect subagent)\n  YES → Q2\n\nQ2: How many tasks in plan?\n  1-3 small → Type: FOCUSED_IMPL\n  4-10 → Type: MULTI_TASK_IMPL\n  >10 → SPLIT recommendation\n\nQ3: Previous session failed or left broken state?\n  YES → Type: RECOVERY (prepend to planned type)\n\nQ4: Need to verify previous session's output?\n  YES → Schedule VERIFY after main work\n\nQ5: Goal is investment thesis analysis on a stock?\n  YES → Type: THESIS (read-only on code, outputs to thesis-log/)\n\nQ6: Goal is ingesting new data sources or KOL channels?\n  YES → Type: INGEST\n\nQ7: Goal is reviewing past thesis outcomes?\n  YES → Type: POST-MORTEM\n```\n\n### 4. Estimate context budget\n\nPer `session-budgets.md` estimation:\n```\nFixed overhead: ~12K\n+ Bounded contexts needed: 5K each\n+ Specs needed: 3-4K each\n+ Files to read: 2K each\n+ Skills loaded: 1.5K each\n+ Working space: ~30% of total\n= Estimated budget\n```\n\nIf > 250K → flag and recommend split.\n\n### 5. Check for matching session plan\n\nLook in `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for file matching goal.\nIf found, load and use as execution guide.\nIf not, note need to create one via `/master-plan`.\n\n### 6. Output session brief\n\nFormat:\n\n```markdown\n# Session Brief — [DATE] Session N\n\n## Goal\n[One sentence description]\n\n## Session Type\n[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n\n## Context Budget Estimate\n- Fixed overhead: X K\n- Variable (specific to this session): Y K\n- Output working space: Z K\n- **Total estimate**: Total K (of 250K hard cap)\n\n## Status Check\n- Active phase: [from current-execution.md]\n- Recent sessions (last 3 summary):\n  - Session N-1: [one line]\n  - Session N-2: [one line]\n  - Session N-3: [one line]\n- Pending from last: [if any]\n\n## Files Loaded\n[List of files read]\n\n## Skills/Agents Relevant\n[List of skills that may be invoked]\n\n## Constraints Active (from constitution)\n[Key invariants relevant to this session]\n[For THESIS sessions: adversarial-by-default, no-LLM-math, bear-case-required]\n[For code sessions: mypy --strict, no Pydantic in domain, cross-BC via contracts only]\n\n## Proposed Next Actions\n1. [Action 1]\n2. [Action 2]\n3. [Action 3]\n\n---\n\nReady to proceed? Confirm or adjust.\n```\n\n### 7. Wait for user confirmation\n\nDo NOT begin substantive work until user confirms or adjusts the brief.\n\n---\n\n## First Session Handling\n\nIf this is the first session ever (Phase 0, Session 1):\n\nOutput:\n\n```markdown\n# Welcome to StockForge\n\nI see this is the first session. Let me guide you through setup.\n\n## Project State\nPhase: 0 (Project Setup)\nStatus: Starter kit just downloaded / initialized\n\n## What I See\n- CLAUDE.md loaded\n- Constitution files present\n- Ubiquitous language seeded\n- No session logs yet\n- No code written yet\n\n## Recommended First Steps (Day 1 Checklist)\n\nBefore building anything:\n\n1. Read `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (30 min, not skippable — 10 principles + signal architecture)\n2. Skim `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` Sections 1-5 (30 min)\n3. Customize `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` if your stack differs\n4. Run `/drill-me \"KOL influence tracking\"` to start refining the stock domain glossary\n5. Identify 3-5 VN stocks you want to cover first (eval set for thesis validation)\n\nFull checklist: `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md`\n\n## Options\n\nA. Run the Day 1 checklist step by step\nB. Jump straight to first spec review\nC. Just explore the codebase first\n\nWhat would you like to do?\n```\n\nWait for user choice before proceeding.\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- If any memory file is missing/corrupted → report specifically, don't guess\n- If constitution file missing → CRITICAL, don't proceed\n- If current-execution.md contradicts project.md → flag for human resolution\n- If budget estimate > 250K → recommend split before starting\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n- Don't skip reading memory files \"to save time\" — costs more later\n- Don't load entire codebase upfront — use just-in-time in execution\n- Don't guess session type — follow decision tree\n- Don't proceed without user confirming brief — ensures alignment\n- Don't start THESIS session and write code (THESIS is read-only on code)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5b3418c5-7cef-4d9d-a8d8-43c69b5c6cac","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Different targets.\n19\t\n20\t## Process\n21\t\n22\t### 1. Ask User What's Being Grilled\n23\t\n24\t\"What plan or design do you want to grill?\"\n25\t\n26\tCan be:\n27\t- A feature idea\n28\t- An architectural decision\n29\t- A spec draft\n30\t- An implementation approach\n31\t\n32\t### 2. Identify Decision Tree\n33\t\n34\tScan the plan/design for:\n35\t- Stated decisions (explicit)\n36\t- Implicit decisions (assumed, not articulated)\n37\t- Open branches (noted as \"TBD\")\n38\t- Edge cases not addressed\n39\t- Failure modes not planned for\n40\t\n41\t### 3. Ask Structured Questions\n42\t\n43\tOne at a time. Based on domain. Examples:\n44\t\n45\t**Architecture questions**:\n46\t- \"Where does [component] live — which bounded context?\"\n47\t- \"If [component A] fails, what happens to [component B]?\"\n48\t- \"What's the single source of truth for [data]?\"\n49\t- \"Who owns writes to [state]? Who reads?\"\n50\t\n51\t**Interface questions**:\n52\t- \"When [edge case] happens, what does the system return?\"\n53\t- \"If [input is invalid], how does user know what's wrong?\"\n54\t- \"What's the retry policy when [external call fails]?\"\n55\t- \"What happens to partial results on failure?\"\n56\t\n57\t**Data questions**:\n58\t- \"What's the primary key? Why that one?\"\n59\t- \"When [field] is null, what does it mean?\"\n60\t- \"Can [record] be deleted or soft-deleted only?\"\n61\t- \"What about timezone for [timestamp]?\"\n62\t\n63\t**Failure mode questions**:\n64\t- \"What's the worst case failure? Blast radius?\"\n65\t- \"How do we detect this failed?\"\n66\t- \"How do we recover? Manual or automatic?\"\n67\t- \"Is there a stuck state it could reach?\"\n68\t\n69\t**Scale questions**:\n70\t- \"At 10 concurrent stocks, does this work?\"\n71\t- \"At 100K news articles per day, does this query still return quickly?\"\n72\t- \"Growth plan: at what scale do we rethink?\"\n73\t\n74\t**Testing questions**:\n75\t- \"What's the happy path test?\"\n76\t- \"What's the hardest edge case to test?\"\n77\t- \"How do we test this without hitting live market data APIs?\"\n78\t\n79\t**StockForge-specific questions**:\n80\t- \"Does this output include a bear case? What's the bear thesis?\"\n81\t- \"Is any number in this output computed by LLM? If so, that's a charter violation.\"\n82\t- \"What's the source + as-of-date for every claim this produces?\"\n83\t- \"If LLM hallucinates here, what's the blast radius on a real money decision?\"\n84\t\n85\t### 4. Don't Accept Vague Answers\n86\t\n87\tIf user says \"we'll handle it later\" → \"OK, handle how? When?\"\n88\tIf user says \"it should be fine\" → \"What makes you confident?\"\n89\tIf user says \"standard approach\" → \"Point me to where we've done this before\"\n90\t\n91\tPush back until concrete decisions emerge.\n92\t\n93\t### 5. {"parentUuid":"e523e8a1-b093-4df2-9128-969a24822f82","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"be91a46b-0f42-4301-92a8-3dff31cbc063","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:39:43.739Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"e7de2606-7a99-4488-a45b-f328150c9755","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01HJ6cBUdSEiRrzPRKEogq2m","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QWURhaZ1CzUUnWWmRVvh9e","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\grill-me.md","content":"# /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n\n> Interrogates user about a plan/design until every decision branch is resolved. Body delegates question-bank substance to the `grill-maximization` skill (multi-batch + AskUserQuestion 4-question max).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Before starting implementation of non-trivial feature\n- When plan feels vague (\"we'll figure it out\")\n- When multiple paths exist and you haven't chosen\n- Before `/spec-author` for complex features\n\n## Contrast with `/drill-me`\n\n- `/drill-me` — domain language extraction (DDD focus, builds glossary)\n- `/grill-me` — design interrogation (makes implicit decisions explicit)\n\nBoth are interactive interviews. Different targets.\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Ask user what's being grilled** — feature idea / architectural decision / spec draft / implementation approach.\n\n2. **Identify decision tree** — scan for stated decisions, implicit decisions (assumed not articulated), open branches (\"TBD\"), unaddressed edge cases, unplanned failure modes.\n\n3. **Ask structured questions** — ONE at a time, wait for answer, adapt next. Categories (with stockforge tilt): Architecture (BC ownership, failure cascade, source of truth, write/read responsibility) / Interface (edge case returns, invalid input, retry policy, partial results) / Data (primary key, null semantics, soft-delete, timezone) / Failure modes (worst-case blast radius, detection, recovery — manual/auto, stuck states) / Scale (10 concurrent stocks? 100K news/day query latency? rethink threshold) / Testing (happy path, hardest edge, no-live-API approach) / **StockForge-specific** (bear case present per I-S10? any LLM-computed numbers — charter violation per I-S1? source + as_of-date for every claim per I-S2? hallucination blast radius on real-money decision?). Full question bank: `.claude/skills/grill-maximization/SKILL.md` § \"Question categories\".\n\n4. **Don't accept vague answers** — `\"we'll handle it later\"` → \"handle how? when?\"; `\"should be fine\"` → \"what makes you confident?\"; `\"standard approach\"` → \"point me to where we've done this before\".\n\n5. **Surface tradeoffs** — for each decision: \"Going with [A] gets [benefit] but pays [cost] — aware of that?\" / \"What's the alternative?\" / \"Who else tried [A]; what happened?\"\n\n6. **Catalog decisions** as they emerge — D-N entries with: question asked / options considered / decision / rationale / tradeoff. Decisions deferred → DD-N entries with revisit condition + working assumption. Unanswered → Q-N entries needing external input + action needed.\n\n7. **Done when** — every edge case has decision or explicit deferral; no \"we'll see\" answers remain unless deferred; tradeoffs surfaced and accepted; user visibly more confident in plan.\n\n8. **Output summary** — Grilled item / duration / Decisions Made (N) / Decisions Deferred (M) / Open Questions (P) / Confidence Level (1-5) / Suggested Next Steps (5: proceed to `/spec-author` or `/master-plan`; 3-4: address top Q-N; 1-2: grill more, different angle) / Artifacts path (`agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/grill-YYYY-MM-DD-[plan].md`).\n\n## Mindset\n\nThe griller's job is NOT to suggest answers — it's to surface hidden assumptions and force explicit choices. `\"I don't know\"` is a valid answer; it just means deferral or external input, not avoidance. Be skeptical. Be thorough. Be kind — this is productive, not adversarial.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Asking questions you already know the answer to (waste)\n- Accepting vague answers politely (defeats purpose)\n- Grilling when user just wants to ship (wrong timing)\n- Asking 10 questions at once (overwhelming — use 4-question batches per `grill-maximization` skill)\n- Skipping the stockforge-specific question family (finance domain has real stakes)\n\n## Do\n\n- One question, wait, follow up\n- Push on vague answers\n- Flag when you can't progress further\n- End with concrete artifact (decisions list)\n\n## Related\n\n- `grill-maximization` skill — bundling discipline (15-20 questions per touchpoint, max 25); full question bank\n- `/drill-me` — paired-purpose for domain language extraction\n- `/spec-author` — natural follow-up when grilling concludes with high confidence\n- `qa-escalation` skill — file-based Q&A protocol when grilling needs async human input\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2656,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7165,"cache_read_input_tokens":228852,"output_tokens":2164,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7165,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2656,"output_tokens":2164,"cache_read_input_tokens":228852,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7165,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7165},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUNRs6L8PKpZdptLaC5","type":"assistant","uuid":"a538eeda-aebe-4555-986f-dffed49e5fa6","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:40:14.704Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

full question bank","+- `/drill-me` — paired-purpose for domain language extraction","+- `/spec-author` — natural follow-up when grilling concludes with high confidence","+- `qa-escalation` skill — file-based Q&A protocol when grilling needs async human input"]}],"originalFile":"# /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n\n> Adopted from mattpocock/skills — adapted for StockForge context.\n> Interrogates user about a plan or design until every decision branch is resolved.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Before starting implementation of non-trivial feature\n- When plan feels vague (\"we'll figure it out\")\n- When multiple paths exist and you haven't chosen\n- Before `/spec-author` for complex features\n\n## Contrast with `/drill-me`\n\n- `/drill-me`: domain language extraction (DDD focus, builds glossary)\n- `/grill-me`: design interrogation (makes implicit decisions explicit)\n\nBoth are interactive interviews. Different targets.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Ask User What's Being Grilled\n\n\"What plan or design do you want to grill?\"\n\nCan be:\n- A feature idea\n- An architectural decision\n- A spec draft\n- An implementation approach\n\n### 2. Identify Decision Tree\n\nScan the plan/design for:\n- Stated decisions (explicit)\n- Implicit decisions (assumed, not articulated)\n- Open branches (noted as \"TBD\")\n- Edge cases not addressed\n- Failure modes not planned for\n\n### 3. Ask Structured Questions\n\nOne at a time. Based on domain. Examples:\n\n**Architecture questions**:\n- \"Where does [component] live — which bounded context?\"\n- \"If [component A] fails, what happens to [component B]?\"\n- \"What's the single source of truth for [data]?\"\n- \"Who owns writes to [state]? Who reads?\"\n\n**Interface questions**:\n- \"When [edge case] happens, what does the system return?\"\n- \"If [input is invalid], how does user know what's wrong?\"\n- \"What's the retry policy when [external call fails]?\"\n- \"What happens to partial results on failure?\"\n\n**Data questions**:\n- \"What's the primary key? Why that one?\"\n- \"When [field] is null, what does it mean?\"\n- \"Can [record] be deleted or soft-deleted only?\"\n- \"What about timezone for [timestamp]?\"\n\n**Failure mode questions**:\n- \"What's the worst case failure? Blast radius?\"\n- \"How do we detect this failed?\"\n- \"How do we recover? Manual or automatic?\"\n- \"Is there a stuck state it could reach?\"\n\n**Scale questions**:\n- \"At 10 concurrent stocks, does this work?\"\n- \"At 100K news articles per day, does this query still return quickly?\"\n- \"Growth plan: at what scale do we rethink?\"\n\n**Testing questions**:\n- \"What's the happy path test?\"\n- \"What's the hardest edge case to test?\"\n- \"How do we test this without hitting live market data APIs?\"\n\n**StockForge-specific questions**:\n- \"Does this output include a bear case? What's the bear thesis?\"\n- \"Is any number in this output computed by LLM? If so, that's a charter violation.\"\n- \"What's the source + as-of-date for every claim this produces?\"\n- \"If LLM hallucinates here, what's the blast radius on a real money decision?\"\n\n### 4. Don't Accept Vague Answers\n\nIf user says \"we'll handle it later\" → \"OK, handle how? When?\"\nIf user says \"it should be fine\" → \"What makes you confident?\"\nIf user says \"standard approach\" → \"Point me to where we've done this before\"\n\nPush back until concrete decisions emerge.\n\n### 5. Surface Tradeoffs\n\nFor decisions, help user see tradeoffs:\n- \"If you go with [A], you get [benefit] but pay [cost]. Aware of that?\"\n- \"What's the alternative to [A]?\"\n- \"Who else has tried [A]? What happened?\"\n\n### 6. Catalog Decisions\n\nAs answers emerge, write them down:\n\n```markdown\n# /grill-me Output — [Plan Name]\n\n## Decisions Made\n\n### D-1: [Decision topic]\n**Question asked**: [original question]\n**Options considered**: [A, B, C]\n**Decision**: [chosen]\n**Rationale**: [why]\n**Tradeoff**: [what you gave up]\n\n### D-2: [Next decision]\n...\n\n## Decisions Deferred\n\n### DD-1: [Topic]\n**Reason deferred**: [why now isn't the right time]\n**Revisit condition**: [when to address]\n**Working assumption**: [what you'll do until resolved]\n\n## Questions You Couldn't Answer\n\n### Q-1: [Topic]\n**Status**: Needs external input (research, data, expert)\n**Action needed**: [what to do to answer]\n```\n\n### 7. When Done\n\nGrilling is done when:\n- Every edge case either has a decision or is explicitly deferred\n- No \"we'll see\" answers remain (unless explicitly deferred)\n- Tradeoffs are surfaced and accepted\n- User is visibly more confident in plan\n\n### 8. Output Summary\n\n```markdown\n# /grill-me Session Complete\n\n## Grilled\n[Plan name]\n\n## Duration\n[time spent interactively]\n\n## Decisions Made: N\n[list of D-N entries]\n\n## Decisions Deferred: M\n[list of DD-N entries]\n\n## Open Questions: P\n[list of Q-N entries requiring external input]\n\n## Confidence Level\n[How sure are you now that the plan will work? 1-5]\n\n## Suggested Next Steps\n- If confidence 5: proceed to `/spec-author` or `/master-plan`\n- If confidence 3-4: address top Q-N questions\n- If confidence 1-2: grill more, different angle\n\n## Artifacts\nDecisions captured at: [path, e.g., `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/grill-YYYY-MM-DD-[plan].md`]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Mindset\n\nAs the griller, your job is NOT to suggest answers. Your job is to surface hidden assumptions and force explicit choices.\n\n\"I don't know\" is a valid answer — it just means the question needs deferral or external input, not avoidance.\n\nBe skeptical. Be thorough. Be kind — this is productive, not adversarial.\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Ask questions you already know the answer to (waste of time)\n- Accept vague answers politely (defeats purpose)\n- Grill when user just wants to ship (wrong timing)\n- Ask 10 questions at once (overwhelming)\n- Skip the StockForge-specific questions (finance domain has real stakes)\n\n**Do**:\n- Ask one question, wait for answer, ask follow-up\n- Push on vague answers\n- Flag when you can't progress further\n- End with concrete artifact (decisions list)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a538eeda-aebe-4555-986f-dffed49e5fa6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Identify Target\n25\t\n26\tRead user's current task. Determine what's about to be written.\n27\t\n28\t### 2. Load Protocol\n29\t\n30\tRead `agent-workspace/constitution/vbw-protocol.md`.\n31\t\n32\t### 3. Execute Appropriate Checkpoint\n33\t\n34\t#### Pre-Spec Checkpoint\n35\t\n36\t```markdown\n37\t# VBW Pre-Spec Checkpoint\n38\t\n39\t**Target**: Writing spec for [feature]\n40\t\n41\t## Source Verification\n42\t- [ ] Read ACTUAL source code for [entity/module]\n43\t  - Files examined:\n44\t  - Methods/dataclasses found:\n45\t- [ ] Listed all methods of [entity] — from code, not memory\n46\t- [ ] Verified factory/constructor signatures — exact params:\n47\t  - Signature: [from code]\n48\t- [ ] Checked if feature already exists\n49\t  - grep result: [exists / does not exist / partially exists]\n50\t\n51\t## Planning\n52\t- [ ] Marking items as CURRENT (exists) vs PROPOSED (new)\n53\t- [ ] Current items: [list]\n54\t- [ ] Proposed items: [list]\n55\t\n56\t## Ready to Write Spec\n57\t- [ ] All terms used exist in glossary\n58\t- [ ] No assumptions about API based on convention\n59\t- [ ] Code references verified\n60\t- [ ] No LLM math planned for B.3 pseudocode\n61\t\n62\tProceed? [Y/N]\n63\t```\n64\t\n65\t#### Pre-Test Checkpoint\n66\t\n67\t```markdown\n68\t# VBW Pre-Test Checkpoint\n69\t\n70\t**Target**: Writing tests for [module]\n71\t\n72\t## Verification\n73\t- [ ] Every method I'm about to call — verified exists\n74\t  - Methods: [list with file:line]\n75\t- [ ] Factory/classmethod signature — exact params verified:\n76\t  - `EntityName.create(...)` takes: [list]\n77\t- [ ] Import paths — verified by file existence check\n78\t  - Imports: [list, each verified]\n79\t- [ ] Base class methods — read base class source\n80\t  - Base methods: [get_events, clear_events, add_domain_event, ...]\n81\t\n82\t## First-File Plan\n83\t- [ ] Writing ONE test file first (test_xxx.py)\n84\t- [ ] Will run mypy + pytest before writing more\n85\t- File to start with: [path]\n86\t\n87\tProceed? [Y/N]\n88\t```\n89\t\n90\t#### Pre-Code Checkpoint\n91\t\n92\t```markdown\n93\t# VBW Pre-Code Checkpoint\n94\t\n95\t**Target**: Implementing [feature/module]\n96\t\n97\t## Verification\n98\t- [ ] Spec loaded and understood\n99\t  - Spec: [path]\n100\t- [ ] Architecture layer identified\n101\t  - Layer: [domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces]\n102\t- [ ] Bounded context identified\n103\t  - BC: [name, e.g. BC-6 Influence Network]\n104\t- [ ] Existing patterns scanned — am I reinventing?\n105\t  - Similar code exists at: [paths or \"no similar pattern\"]\n106\t- [ ] Protocols/ports to implement — verified\n107\t  - Ports: [list]\n108\t\n109\t## Constraints Check\n110\t- [ ] Invariants relevant: [list — esp. I-S1 no LLM math]\n111\t- [ ] Drift signals to avoid: [DR1 domain framework imports, DR6 Any types]\n112\t- [ ] Budget remaining: [estimate]\n113\t- [ ] Domain layer: will use dataclasses only (no Pydantic)\n114\t\n115\tProceed? [Y/N]\n```\n\n#### Pre-Test Checkpoint\n\n```markdown\n# VBW Pre-Test Checkpoint\n\n**Target**: Writing tests for [module]\n\n## Verification\n- [ ] Every method I'm about to call — verified exists\n  - Methods: [list with file:line]\n- [ ] Factory/classmethod signature — exact params verified:\n  - `EntityName.create(...)` takes: [list]\n- [ ] Import paths — verified by file existence check\n  - Imports: [list, each verified]\n- [ ] Base class methods — read base class source\n  - Base methods: [get_events, clear_events, add_domain_event, ...]\n\n## First-File Plan\n- [ ] Writing ONE test file first (test_xxx.py)\n- [ ] Will run mypy + pytest before writing more\n- File to start with: [path]\n\nProceed? [Y/N]\n```\n\n#### Pre-Code Checkpoint\n\n```markdown\n# VBW Pre-Code Checkpoint\n\n**Target**: Implementing [feature/module]\n\n## Verification\n- [ ] Spec loaded and understood\n  - Spec: [path]\n- [ ] Architecture layer identified\n  - Layer: [domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces]\n- [ ] Bounded context identified\n  - BC: [name, e.g. BC-6 Influence Network]\n- [ ] Existing patterns scanned — am I reinventing?\n  - Similar code exists at: [paths or \"no similar pattern\"]\n- [ ] Protocols/ports to implement — verified\n  - Ports: [list]\n\n## Constraints Check\n- [ ] Invariants relevant: [list — esp. Summarize Work Done\n12\t\n13\tReview what happened in this session:\n14\t- What was the goal (from session brief)?\n15\t- What was accomplished?\n16\t- What was blocked or left unresolved?\n17\t- Were there any surprises?\n18\t\n19\t### 2. Write Session Log\n20\t\n21\tCreate: `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n22\t\n23\tTemplate:\n24\t```markdown\n25\t# Session N — YYYY-MM-DD\n26\t\n27\t## Goal\n28\t[One sentence from session brief]\n29\t\n30\t## Session Type\n31\t[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n32\t\n33\t## Context Budget\n34\t- Estimated: X K\n35\t- Actual: Y K (check at end)\n36\t- Efficiency: Z tasks per 100K tokens\n37\t\n38\t## Approach\n39\t[2-3 sentences: what was tried, what strategy was used]\n40\t\n41\t## Accomplished\n42\t- [task with link to commit if applicable]\n43\t- [task with link]\n44\t\n45\t## Blocked / Unresolved\n46\t- [item] — blocked by [reason]\n47\t- [item] — needs decision on [question]\n48\t\n49\t## Learned Rules\n50\t- [if any rule emerged, added to agent-notes.md]\n51\t\n52\t## Patterns Noticed\n53\t- [pattern observed worth tracking, added to patterns-discovered/ if significant]\n54\t\n55\t## Files Modified\n56\t[git diff --name-only]\n57\t\n58\t## Next Session Pickup\n59\t[Specific instruction for next session — what to do first]\n60\t\n61\t## VBW Protocol Adherence\n62\t- Pre-spec checkpoint: [did/did not apply where relevant]\n63\t- Pre-test checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n64\t- Pre-commit checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n65\t\n66\t## Quality Gates Status\n67\t- Deterministic: [pass/fail/not run] (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n68\t- Probabilistic: [scheduled/completed/not needed]\n69\t- Human review: [requested/not needed]\n70\t\n71\t## Thesis Log (if THESIS session)\n72\t- Thesis logged to: [path in agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/]\n73\t- Stock covered: [ticker]\n74\t- Verdict summary: [one line]\n75\t```\n76\t\n77\t### 3. Update project.md\n78\t\n79\tIf any of these happened, update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md`:\n80\t- Architectural decision made\n81\t- Phase boundary reached\n82\t- Major TODO added/completed\n83\t- Known issue surfaced\n84\t- Invariant needs adjustment\n85\t\n86\tOtherwise, only update \"Current Phase\" timestamp if relevant.\n87\t\n88\t### 4. Update current-execution.md\n89\t\n90\tUpdate routing source of truth:\n91\t- If work item was completed → move to Archived section\n92\t- If work item progressed → update Status\n93\t- If work item blocked → add Blocker info\n94\t- If new work item starting → add to Current Work Items\n95\t- Update \"Session N\" number\n96\t\n97\t### 5. Consider Learned Rules\n98\t\n99\tAsk yourself:\n100\t- Did anything go wrong this session that a rule would prevent next time?\n101\t- Did I discover a pattern worth formalizing?\n102\t- Was there an anti-pattern to flag?\n103\t\n104\tIf yes, append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` using the format there.\n105\t\n106\t### 6. Consider Patterns\n107\t\n108\tIf a useful pattern emerged that might be reused:\n109\t- Worth a dedicated file in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/`?\n110\t- Or upgrade to a skill in `.claude/skills/`?\n111\t\n112\tDocument if so.\n113\t\n114\t### 7. Thesis Log (THESIS sessions only)\n115\t\n116\tIf this was a THESIS session:\n117\t- Ensure entry in `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/YYYY-MM-DD-[ticker].md`\n118\t- Format must include: ticker, date, bull case, bear case, catalysts, risks, calibration note\n119\t- No single \"buy/sell\" verdict — output is multi-criteria trade-off matrix\n120\t\n121\t### 8. Run Drift Check (optional but recommended)\n122\t\n123\tIf code was modified, run `/drift-check` to catch issues before next session.\n124\t\n125\t### 9. Run `git commit` when ready, or let me know if you want me to commit.\n164\t```\n165\t\n166\t---\n167\t\n168\t## Error Handling\n169\t\n170\t- If can't write session log (disk/permissions) → CRITICAL, report specifically\n171\t- If project.md conflicts with current-execution.md → flag for resolution\n172\t- If deterministic gates fail → do NOT claim success, report honestly\n173\t\n174\t---\n175\t\n176\t## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n177\t\n178\t- Don't skip this command \"to save time\"\n179\t- Don't write session log without actually reviewing work\n180\t- Don't update project.md automatically if nothing significant happened\n181\t- Don't commit without user approval (unless requested)\n182\t- Don't claim completion if gates failed\n183\t- Don't skip thesis-log update for THESIS sessions (calibration depends on it)\n184\t"}]},"uuid":"28599292-86fd-43f1-a0ad-67fa042c70c8","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:40:45.291Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\session-end.md","content":"# /session-end — Close Work Session\n\n> Persists state, writes session log, prepares handoff for next session.\n\n## When to Use\n\nAt the end of every meaningful work session. **Not optional** — skipping this breaks continuity.\n\n## Steps\n\n### 1. Summarize Work Done\n\nReview what happened in this session:\n- What was the goal (from session brief)?\n- What was accomplished?\n- What was blocked or left unresolved?\n- Were there any surprises?\n\n### 2. Write Session Log\n\nCreate: `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n\nTemplate:\n```markdown\n# Session N — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Goal\n[One sentence from session brief]\n\n## Session Type\n[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n\n## Context Budget\n- Estimated: X K\n- Actual: Y K (check at end)\n- Efficiency: Z tasks per 100K tokens\n\n## Approach\n[2-3 sentences: what was tried, what strategy was used]\n\n## Accomplished\n- [task with link to commit if applicable]\n- [task with link]\n\n## Blocked / Unresolved\n- [item] — blocked by [reason]\n- [item] — needs decision on [question]\n\n## Learned Rules\n- [if any rule emerged, added to agent-notes.md]\n\n## Patterns Noticed\n- [pattern observed worth tracking, added to patterns-discovered/ if significant]\n\n## Files Modified\n[git diff --name-only]\n\n## Next Session Pickup\n[Specific instruction for next session — what to do first]\n\n## VBW Protocol Adherence\n- Pre-spec checkpoint: [did/did not apply where relevant]\n- Pre-test checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n- Pre-commit checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n\n## Quality Gates Status\n- Deterministic: [pass/fail/not run] (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- Probabilistic: [scheduled/completed/not needed]\n- Human review: [requested/not needed]\n\n## Thesis Log (if THESIS session)\n- Thesis logged to: [path in agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/]\n- Stock covered: [ticker]\n- Verdict summary: [one line]\n```\n\n### 3. Update project.md\n\nIf any of these happened, update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md`:\n- Architectural decision made\n- Phase boundary reached\n- Major TODO added/completed\n- Known issue surfaced\n- Invariant needs adjustment\n\nOtherwise, only update \"Current Phase\" timestamp if relevant.\n\n### 4. Update current-execution.md\n\nUpdate routing source of truth:\n- If work item was completed → move to Archived section\n- If work item progressed → update Status\n- If work item blocked → add Blocker info\n- If new work item starting → add to Current Work Items\n- Update \"Session N\" number\n\n### 5. Consider Learned Rules\n\nAsk yourself:\n- Did anything go wrong this session that a rule would prevent next time?\n- Did I discover a pattern worth formalizing?\n- Was there an anti-pattern to flag?\n\nIf yes, append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` using the format there.\n\n### 6. Consider Patterns\n\nIf a useful pattern emerged that might be reused:\n- Worth a dedicated file in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/`?\n- Or upgrade to a skill in `.claude/skills/`?\n\nDocument if so.\n\n### 7. Thesis Log (THESIS sessions only)\n\nIf this was a THESIS session:\n- Ensure entry in `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/YYYY-MM-DD-[ticker].md`\n- Format must include: ticker, date, bull case, bear case, catalysts, risks, calibration note\n- No single \"buy/sell\" verdict — output is multi-criteria trade-off matrix\n\n### 8. Run Drift Check (optional but recommended)\n\nIf code was modified, run `/drift-check` to catch issues before next session.\n\n### 9. Stage Changes\n\n```bash\ngit add -A\ngit status\n```\n\nReport what's staged. **Do NOT commit** unless user explicitly requested.\n\n### 10. Output Session End Summary\n\n```markdown\n# Session N Complete — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Summary\n[2-3 sentence summary]\n\n## Files Changed\n[list]\n\n## Memory Updated\n- project.md: [updated sections or \"no changes\"]\n- current-execution.md: [status updates]\n- Session log: `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md` created\n- agent-notes.md: [rules added or \"none\"]\n- thesis-log: [entry added or \"not a thesis session\"]\n\n## Quality Status\n- Deterministic gates: [status] (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- Test status: [pass count / total]\n- Drift signals: [clean / N warnings]\n\n## Next Session Pickup\n[Specific instruction]\n\n## Staged for Commit\n[git status output]\n\nStaged but not committed. Run `git commit` when ready, or let me know if you want me to commit.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- If can't write session log (disk/permissions) → CRITICAL, report specifically\n- If project.md conflicts with current-execution.md → flag for resolution\n- If deterministic gates fail → do NOT claim success, report honestly\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n- Don't skip this command \"to save time\"\n- Don't write session log without actually reviewing work\n- Don't update project.md automatically if nothing significant happened\n- Don't commit without user approval (unless requested)\n- Don't claim completion if gates failed\n- Don't skip thesis-log update for THESIS sessions (calibration depends on it)\n","numLines":184,"startLine":1,"totalLines":184}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1b8e1148-ece7-4deb-9cb4-767e7695ec20","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory.
