Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Body delegates load-priority discipline to `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol.\n\n## When to Use\n\nAt the end of every meaningful work session. **Not optional** — skipping breaks continuity (session N+1 SessionStart hook reads checkpoints + sessions/).\n\n## Steps\n\n1. **Summarize work done** — review goal (from session brief), what accomplished, what blocked/unresolved, any surprises.\n\n2. **Write session log** at `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md` per the schema below.\n\n3. **Update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md`** if any of: architectural decision made, phase boundary reached, major TODO added/completed, known issue surfaced, invariant needs adjustment. Otherwise no change.\n\n4. **Update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md`** (routing source-of-truth) — work completed → move to Archived; progressed → update Status; blocked → add Blocker info; new starting → add to Current Work Items; bump \"Session N\" number.\n\n5. **Capture learned rules** — did anything go wrong a rule would prevent? Summarize Work Done\n\nReview what happened in this session:\n- What was the goal (from session brief)?\n- What was accomplished?\n- What was blocked or left unresolved?\n- Were there any surprises?\n\n### 2. Write Session Log\n\nCreate: `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n\nTemplate:\n```markdown\n# Session N — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Goal\n[One sentence from session brief]\n\n## Session Type\n[PLAN | FOCUSED_IMPL | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | VERIFY | RECOVERY | THESIS | INGEST | POST-MORTEM]\n\n## Context Budget\n- Estimated: X K\n- Actual: Y K (check at end)\n- Efficiency: Z tasks per 100K tokens\n\n## Approach\n[2-3 sentences: what was tried, what strategy was used]\n\n## Accomplished\n- [task with link to commit if applicable]\n- [task with link]\n\n## Blocked / Unresolved\n- [item] — blocked by [reason]\n- [item] — needs decision on [question]\n\n## Learned Rules\n- [if any rule emerged, added to agent-notes.md]\n\n## Patterns Noticed\n- [pattern observed worth tracking, added to patterns-discovered/ if significant]\n\n## Files Modified\n[git diff --name-only]\n\n## Next Session Pickup\n[Specific instruction for next session — what to do first]\n\n## VBW Protocol Adherence\n- Pre-spec checkpoint: [did/did not apply where relevant]\n- Pre-test checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n- Pre-commit checkpoint: [applied/not applicable]\n\n## Quality Gates Status\n- Deterministic: [pass/fail/not run] (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- Probabilistic: [scheduled/completed/not needed]\n- Human review: [requested/not needed]\n\n## Thesis Log (if THESIS session)\n- Thesis logged to: [path in agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/]\n- Stock covered: [ticker]\n- Verdict summary: [one line]\n```\n\n### 3. Update project.md\n\nIf any of these happened, update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md`:\n- Architectural decision made\n- Phase boundary reached\n- Major TODO added/completed\n- Known issue surfaced\n- Invariant needs adjustment\n\nOtherwise, only update \"Current Phase\" timestamp if relevant.\n\n### 4. Update current-execution.md\n\nUpdate routing source of truth:\n- If work item was completed → move to Archived section\n- If work item progressed → update Status\n- If work item blocked → add Blocker info\n- If new work item starting → add to Current Work Items\n- Update \"Session N\" number\n\n### 5. Consider Learned Rules\n\nAsk yourself:\n- Did anything go wrong this session that a rule would prevent next time?\n- Did I discover a pattern worth formalizing?\n- Was there an anti-pattern to flag?\n\nIf yes, append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` using the format there.\n\n### 6. Consider Patterns\n\nIf a useful pattern emerged that might be reused:\n- Worth a dedicated file in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/`?\n- Or upgrade to a skill in `.claude/skills/`?\n\nDocument if so.\n\n### 7. Thesis Log (THESIS sessions only)\n\nIf this was a THESIS session:\n- Ensure entry in `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/YYYY-MM-DD-[ticker].md`\n- Format must include: ticker, date, bull case, bear case, catalysts, risks, calibration note\n- No single \"buy/sell\" verdict — output is multi-criteria trade-off matrix\n\n### 8. Run Drift Check (optional but recommended)\n\nIf code was modified, run `/drift-check` to catch issues before next session.\n\n### 9. Stage Changes\n\n```bash\ngit add -A\ngit status\n```\n\nReport what's staged. **Do NOT commit** unless user explicitly requested.\n\n### 10. Output Session End Summary\n\n```markdown\n# Session N Complete — YYYY-MM-DD\n\n## Summary\n[2-3 sentence summary]\n\n## Files Changed\n[list]\n\n## Memory Updated\n- project.md: [updated sections or \"no changes\"]\n- current-execution.md: [status updates]\n- Session log: `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md` created\n- agent-notes.md: [rules added or \"none\"]\n- thesis-log: [entry added or \"not a thesis session\"]\n\n## Quality Status\n- Deterministic gates: [status] (mypy --strict, pytest, ruff)\n- Test status: [pass count / total]\n- Drift signals: [clean / N warnings]\n\n## Next Session Pickup\n[Specific instruction]\n\n## Staged for Commit\n[git status output]\n\nStaged but not committed. Run `git commit` when ready, or let me know if you want me to commit.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- If can't write session log (disk/permissions) → CRITICAL, report specifically\n- If project.md conflicts with current-execution.md → flag for resolution\n- If deterministic gates fail → do NOT claim success, report honestly\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n- Don't skip this command \"to save time\"\n- Don't write session log without actually reviewing work\n- Don't update project.md automatically if nothing significant happened\n- Don't commit without user approval (unless requested)\n- Don't claim completion if gates failed\n- Don't skip thesis-log update for THESIS sessions (calibration depends on it)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"054a14f7-2bc4-4bbf-852a-96e6dcc79665","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"e9fad407-da78-447a-8c1a-b3a488dd618a","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"88b3c76d-e873-4fb1-b54a-a4b7b28ce1b4","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:41:20.628Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"afb4d312-d6e3-48cc-af1f-8c1092e727d5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_016zTp9ruDC737xBHECfdZws","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012MzvzxESU5NVBfzFB8Sfhx","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\spec-author.md","content":"# /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n\n> Invokes `spec-author` subagent (Business Analyst + DDD Designer persona) to produce Tier 2 feature spec following `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md`. Body delegates dual-layer discipline to the `spec-dual-layer` skill.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Before implementing any non-trivial feature\n- When converting a requirement into a formal spec\n- When refactoring requires updated spec\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — feature name or brief description (e.g., `KOL recommendation extraction pipeline`, `thesis validation workflow`).\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Pre-flight check** — relevant BC exists in glossary? If new domain terms emerging, suggest `/drill-me` first. Check if a similar spec already exists (avoid duplication).\n\n2. **Gather context** — read `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` (template), relevant `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md` sections, related specs, and constraints from `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` + `architecture.md`.\n\n3. **Dispatch `spec-author` subagent** (run_in_background) with the context bundle. Subagent budget: up to 50K tokens. Persona: BA + DDD Designer. Task: produce dual-layer spec for `$ARGUMENTS`.\n\n4. **Subagent produces three parts** per `spec-dual-layer` skill:\n   - **Part A (Business Specification)** — context narrative; use cases with acceptance scenarios; business rules in ubiquitous language; decisions + tradeoffs (A.6); risks (A.7, including finance-specific); dependencies (A.8). Readable by non-engineer stakeholder.\n   - **Part B (Agent Contract)** — input/output contracts (dataclasses for domain, Pydantic for interfaces only); core logic at algorithm level — **NO LLM math** (numbers come from deterministic code per I-S1); data model changes; affected BCs; domain events; API surface (Phase 2+); NFRs; test requirements (B.9); MUST/MUST-NOT/SHOULD constraints; rollback (B.12); verification checklist (B.13). Output **must be multi-criteria, never single buy/sell score**.\n   - **Part C (Provenance)** — authoring history, review slot (reviewer fills), decision provenance refs.\n\n5. **Subagent writes** to `specs/tier2-feature/NNN-feature-name.md` per template.\n\n6. **Review prompt** — output: spec_id + path / 2-3 sentence summary from Part A / Key Decisions Made (D-N list) / Open Questions for human (Q-N list) / Glossary Status (existing terms used + new terms proposed) / **StockForge compliance check**: no-LLM-math in B.3 ✅; output multi-criteria ✅; source citation in output contract per I-S2 ✅; bear case required if thesis-related per I-S10 ✅ / Next Steps (`/spec-to-wiki [path]` then `/bdd-planner [spec-id]`).\n\n7. **Iteration** — minor edits in place, bump version 1.0 → 1.1; major changes re-run `/spec-author` with refined input.\n\n8. **Sign-off when approved** — add to `current-execution.md` as active spec; schedule `/bdd-planner` for test planning + `/master-plan` for implementation breakdown.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Writing spec without checking glossary first\n- Combining multiple features in one Tier 2 spec (split)\n- Skipping Part C provenance (decision history matters)\n- Writing Part B without reviewing Part A first\n- Spec >500 LOC in Tier 2 → split\n- LLM math in B.3 pseudocode (e.g., `LLM computes P/E ratio` — charter violation per I-S1)\n- Single buy/sell confidence score as output (use trade-off matrix per I-S35)\n\n## Do\n\n- Use dual-layer format religiously (per `spec-dual-layer` skill)\n- Flag ambiguities explicitly in open questions\n- Reference existing patterns from `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/`\n- Keep Tier 2 spec to 200-500 LOC\n- Make Part A readable by non-engineer\n- Ensure all numbers in B.3 trace to deterministic code\n\n## Quality Check\n\nBefore finalizing: every domain term in glossary; Part A narrative + Part B structured; B.13 complete; A.7 risks identified; A.6 decisions documented; A.8 dependencies listed; B.9 tests specified; B.12 rollback present; no LLM math in B.3; multi-criteria output. Full check list: `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` checklist section.\n\n## Related\n\n- `spec-dual-layer` skill — canonical dual-layer discipline (substance)\n- `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` — template + checklist\n- `/drill-me` — pre-spec glossary extraction\n- `/spec-to-wiki` — natural follow-up after sign-off\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 / I-S2 / I-S10 / I-S35 enforced in Part B\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9225,"cache_read_input_tokens":252755,"output_tokens":2259,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9225,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":2259,"cache_read_input_tokens":252755,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9225,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9225},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUVaSUaHaegn1dWG5Rk","type":"assistant","uuid":"3de66ed4-f3ad-4f30-805f-9e160d56b1e5","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:41:57.654Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Full check list: `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` checklist section."," ","-- [ ] Every domain term used appears in glossary.md","-- [ ] Part A is narrative (BA perspective)","-- [ ] Part B is structured (agent contract)","-- [ ] B.13 verification checklist complete","-- [ ] Risks identified in A.7","-- [ ] Decisions documented in A.6","-- [ ] Dependencies listed in A.8","-- [ ] Test requirements specified in B.9","-- [ ] Rollback plan in B.12","-- [ ] No LLM math in B.3","-- [ ] Output is multi-criteria (not single score)","+## Related","+","+- `spec-dual-layer` skill — canonical dual-layer discipline (substance)","+- `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` — template + checklist","+- `/drill-me` — pre-spec glossary extraction","+- `/spec-to-wiki` — natural follow-up after sign-off","+- `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 / I-S2 / I-S10 / I-S35 enforced in Part B"]}],"originalFile":"# /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n\n> Invoke spec-author subagent to produce Tier 2 feature spec following template.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Before implementing any non-trivial feature\n- When converting a requirement into formal spec\n- When refactoring requires updated spec\n\n## Input\n\n`$ARGUMENTS` — feature name or brief description (e.g., \"KOL recommendation extraction pipeline\", \"thesis validation workflow\")\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pre-flight Check\n\nBefore invoking subagent:\n- Ensure relevant bounded context exists in glossary\n- If new domain terms emerging, suggest `/drill-me` first\n- Check if similar spec already exists (avoid duplication)\n\n### 2. Gather Context\n\nPrepare for subagent:\n- Read `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` (template to follow)\n- Read relevant `glossary.md` sections\n- Read related specs if any\n- Note constraints from `invariants.md` and `architecture.md`\n\n### 3. Invoke spec-author Subagent\n\nSpawn subagent via Task tool:\n- Persona: Business Analyst + DDD Designer\n- Context: Template, glossary, related specs, constraints\n- Task: Produce dual-layer spec for `$ARGUMENTS`\n- Budget: Up to 50K tokens\n\n### 4. Subagent Process (what it does)\n\nThe subagent:\n\n**Phase A — Business Specification (Part A)**:\n- Interview user if needed\n- Draft context narrative\n- Identify use cases with acceptance scenarios\n- Define business rules in ubiquitous language\n- List decisions and tradeoffs\n- Identify risks (including finance-specific risks)\n\n**Phase B — Agent Contract (Part B)**:\n- Derive input/output contracts from Part A (dataclasses for domain, Pydantic for interfaces)\n- Specify core logic at algorithm level (no LLM math — numbers come from deterministic code)\n- Define data model changes\n- List affected bounded contexts\n- Specify domain events\n- Define API surface (if Phase 2+ applicable)\n- Document non-functional requirements\n- Design test requirements\n- List constraints (MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD)\n- Ensure multi-criteria output (no single buy/sell score)\n\n**Phase C — Provenance**:\n- Authoring history entry\n- Review slot (to be filled by reviewer)\n- Decision provenance references\n\n### 5. Subagent Output\n\nWrites to `specs/tier2-feature/NNN-feature-name.md` using template from `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md`.\n\n### 6. Review Prompt\n\nAfter subagent completes:\n\n```markdown\n# Spec Created — [spec_id]\n\nPath: `specs/tier2-feature/NNN-feature-name.md`\n\n## Summary\n[2-3 sentences from Part A]\n\n## Key Decisions Made\n- [D-1]: [decision]\n- [D-2]: [decision]\n\n## Open Questions (for human review)\n- [Q1]: [question needing human input]\n- [Q2]: [question needing human input]\n\n## Glossary Status\n- Existing terms used: [list]\n- New terms proposed: [list — may need /drill-me]\n\n## Stock-Specific Compliance\n- No LLM math in B.3: [confirmed / at risk: note]\n- Output includes multi-criteria (not single score): [confirmed / needs revision]\n- Source citation in output contract: [confirmed / missing]\n- Bear case required (if thesis-related): [confirmed / N/A]\n\n## Next Steps\n1. Review Part A (business narrative) — does it capture intent?\n2. Review open questions\n3. Confirm decisions in A.6\n4. If approved: run `/spec-to-wiki [spec-path]` to create Obsidian version\n5. Run `/bdd-planner [spec-id]` to propose test cases\n\nPlease review Part A carefully. Part B derives from A — if A is right, B is usually right.\n```\n\n### 7. Iteration\n\nUser reviews. If changes needed:\n- Minor: edit in place, bump version (1.0 → 1.1)\n- Major: run `/spec-author` again with refined input\n\n### 8. Sign-off\n\nWhen approved:\n- Add to current-execution.md as active spec\n- Schedule `/bdd-planner` for test planning\n- Schedule `/master-plan` for implementation breakdown\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Write spec without checking glossary first\n- Combine multiple features in one Tier 2 spec (split into separate specs)\n- Skip Part C provenance (decision history matters)\n- Write Part B without reviewing Part A first\n- Make spec too detailed (>500 lines in Tier 2 = split)\n- Put LLM math in B.3 pseudocode (e.g., \"LLM computes P/E ratio\" — wrong)\n- Include a single buy/sell confidence score as output (use trade-off matrix)\n\n**Do**:\n- Use dual-layer format religiously\n- Flag ambiguities explicitly in open questions\n- Reference existing patterns from patterns-discovered/\n- Keep spec to 200-500 lines for Tier 2\n- Make Part A readable by non-engineer stakeholder\n- Ensure all numbers in B.3 trace to deterministic code, not LLM output\n\n---\n\n## Quality Check\n\nBefore finalizing spec:\n\n- [ ] Every domain term used appears in glossary.md\n- [ ] Part A is narrative (BA perspective)\n- [ ] Part B is structured (agent contract)\n- [ ] B.13 verification checklist complete\n- [ ] Risks identified in A.7\n- [ ] Decisions documented in A.6\n- [ ] Dependencies listed in A.8\n- [ ] Test requirements specified in B.9\n- [ ] Rollback plan in B.12\n- [ ] No LLM math in B.3\n- [ ] Output is multi-criteria (not single score)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3de66ed4-f3ad-4f30-805f-9e160d56b1e5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

/budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n\n> Report current session context consumption and project against budget.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Every ~30 minutes during long sessions\n- Before starting major new subtask\n- When feeling context might be bloating\n- Before loading large new files\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Estimate Current Consumption\n\nMethod (rough):\n- Sum of all file reads performed\n- Sum of all LLM responses in session\n- Sum of all tool outputs\n- Plus fixed overhead from CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution\n\n(Claude Code doesn't expose exact count, so estimation is practical.)\n\n### 2. Identify Session Type\n\nFrom current session brief:\n- PLAN: budget 80K\n- FOCUSED_IMPL: budget 150K\n- MULTI_TASK_IMPL: budget 250K\n- VERIFY: budget 60K\n- RECOVERY: budget 150K\n- THESIS: budget 100K\n- INGEST: budget 80K\n- POST-MORTEM: budget 50K\n\n### 3. Project Remaining Work\n\nGiven current position in session plan:\n- Tasks remaining\n- Estimated token cost per remaining task\n- Total remaining work\n\n### 4. Compute Status\n\n```\nUsage percent = estimated_used / budget_limit\nProjected total = estimated_used + estimated_remaining\nProjection = projected_total / budget_limit\n```\n\n### 5. Output Status Report\n\n```markdown\n# Budget Check — [time]\n\n## Current Session\n- Type: [FOCUSED_IMPL]\n- Started: [timestamp]\n- Duration so far: [elapsed]\n\n## Estimated Consumption\n- Fixed overhead (CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution): ~12K\n- Files read this session: ~X K  \n- Tool outputs: ~Y K\n- Agent responses: ~Z K\n- **Total estimated**: ~Total K\n\n## Budget Status\n- Session budget: [150K]\n- Used: ~Total K ([percent]%)\n- Remaining: ~Remaining K\n\n## Projection for Remaining Work\n- Tasks still to do: N\n- Avg per task: ~K K\n- Projected additional: ~Additional K\n- **Projected total**: ~Grand K\n\n## Status\n[ GREEN ON TRACK | YELLOW CAUTION | RED AT RISK | OVER BUDGET ]\n\n## Recommendations\n[If green]: Continue as planned.\n[If yellow]: Avoid loading large new files. Consider finishing task before taking new one.\n[If red]: Wrap up current task, prepare for session end. Do not start new major work.\n[If over]: STOP. Emergency handoff. Split to new session.\n```\n\n### 6. Threshold Actions\n\n- **< 50% used**: normal, proceed\n- **50-70% used**: caution message, avoid unnecessary loads\n- **70-85% used**: finalize current task, no new major tasks\n- **> 85% used**: immediate handoff preparation\n- **> 100% / over 250K**: hard stop, emergency session end\n\n### 7. Hard Cap Enforcement\n\nIf projected to exceed 250K (universal hard cap regardless of type):\n\n```markdown\nWARNING: BUDGET BREACH IMMINENT\n\nProjected total: 270K tokens (exceeds 250K universal hard cap)\n\nMeasured evidence: quality degrades sharply past 250K (\"lost in middle\" effect).\nSession 4 in Phase2 project: 300K+ tokens, 0 tasks completed.\n\nAction required:\n1. **Stop current task at safe checkpoint**\n2. **Save state to session log**\n3. **Split remaining work to new session**\n\nI will not continue past 250K without explicit override from you.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Observable Signals of High Usage\n\nEven without exact count, these suggest high context:\n- Difficulty remembering early part of conversation\n- Needing to re-read files already read\n- Agent asking questions that were answered earlier\n- Responses getting shorter / less coherent\n\nIf observed → run `/budget-check` immediately.\n\n---\n\n## Integration\n\n- Automatic check embedded in `/session-verify`\n- Manual check via `/budget-check`\n- Hard stop logic can be added to hook (future)\n\n---\n\n## Cost Awareness\n\nBudget isn't just about quality — it's money.\n- Claude Opus: ~$15 per M tokens input\n- Claude Sonnet: ~$3 per M tokens input\n- 250K session = ~$3.75 (Opus) or ~$0.75 (Sonnet) per input pass\n\nKeep sessions focused → cost stays reasonable.\n","numLines":147,"startLine":1,"totalLines":147}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"339b5a2b-c569-4dfc-bebb-987f924f9110","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"11cf655b-8ddb-4206-bdbc-76c8956e0d31","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"8d266d3c-efb5-4ab5-a09e-0adbfbc6ad16","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:41:58.755Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"8f0b38b1-00b2-4bca-873d-086d9731811d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01Xuwk8fxkxKuqELtjbEfEoj","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017reixhzEbxCXJ8wYkUHjBA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\commands\\budget-check.md","content":"# /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n\n> Report current session context consumption and project against budget. Body delegates budget formulas + thresholds to `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` (canonical).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Every ~30 minutes during long sessions\n- Before starting a major new subtask\n- When feeling context might be bloating\n- Before loading large new files\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Estimate current consumption** — sum of file reads + LLM responses + tool outputs + fixed overhead (CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution). Claude Code doesn't expose exact count, so estimation is practical. Use `.transcript-tokens` if available (per Track 8/9 telemetry).\n\n2. **Identify session type budget** — PLAN 80K / FOCUSED_IMPL 150K / MULTI_TASK_IMPL 250K / VERIFY 60K / RECOVERY 150K / THESIS 100K / INGEST 80K / POST-MORTEM 50K. Universal hard cap: 250K.\n\n3. **Project remaining work** — given current position in session plan: tasks remaining × estimated tokens per task → total remaining.\n\n4. **Compute status** — `usage_pct = estimated_used / budget_limit` ; `projected_total = estimated_used + estimated_remaining` ; `projection_pct = projected_total / budget_limit`.\n\n5. **Output status report** with sections: Current Session (type / started / elapsed) / Estimated Consumption (fixed + files + tool outputs + agent responses → total) / Budget Status (session budget / used / remaining + percent) / Projection (tasks still to do / avg per task / projected additional / projected total) / Status (GREEN / YELLOW / RED / OVER) / Recommendations.\n\n6. **Threshold actions** — `< 50%` normal proceed; `50-70%` caution, avoid unnecessary loads; `70-85%` finalize current task, no new major tasks; `> 85%` immediate handoff prep; `> 100% or > 250K` hard stop, emergency session end.\n\n7. **Hard cap enforcement** — if projected to exceed 250K (universal cap regardless of session type), output WARNING: BUDGET BREACH IMMINENT — projected total / 250K cap / cite Session 4 (300K+ tokens, 0 tasks completed) as measured evidence. Required action: stop at safe checkpoint, save state to session log, split remaining work to new session. Do NOT continue past 250K without explicit user override.\n\n## Observable Signals of High Usage\n\nEven without an exact count, these suggest high context:\n\n- Difficulty remembering early conversation\n- Re-reading files already read\n- Agent asking questions answered earlier\n- Responses getting shorter / less coherent\n\nIf observed → run `/budget-check` immediately.\n\n## Cost Awareness\n\nBudget isn't just quality — it's money. Claude Opus ~$15/M input tokens; Claude Sonnet ~$3/M; 250K session ≈ $3.75 (Opus) or $0.75 (Sonnet) per input pass. Keep sessions focused → cost stays reasonable.\n\n## Integration\n\n- Auto-check embedded in `/session-verify`\n- Manual check via this command\n- Hard-stop logic via `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh` (per CLAUDE.md context-threshold band: 180K wind-down / 220K cliff / 250K hard cap)\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Continuing past 250K because \"I'm almost done\" — quality degrades sharply (\"lost in middle\" effect; Session 4 evidence)\n- Skipping check on long sessions\n- Treating budget as advisory not enforcement\n\n## Do\n\n- Run periodically during long sessions\n- Treat 250K as hard ceiling, not soft\n- Wrap up cleanly when projected over budget — emergency handoff is more expensive than a clean split\n\n## Related\n\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` — canonical budgets per session type + thresholds\n- `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh` — automated wind-down / cliff / hard-cap signals\n- `/session-verify` — pairs with this command\n- `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/sessions-rollup.tsv` — observed token usage per session (per S19 aggregator)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1897,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7106,"cache_read_input_tokens":261980,"output_tokens":1913,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7106,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1897,"output_tokens":1913,"cache_read_input_tokens":261980,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7106,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7106},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUYPfAZRr24CUUqi5E7","type":"assistant","uuid":"945a9b4e-c2e8-4268-b2d0-dc9398989fab","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:42:21.387Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Body delegates budget formulas + thresholds to `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` (canonical).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Every ~30 minutes during long sessions\n- Before starting a major new subtask\n- When feeling context might be bloating\n- Before loading large new files\n\n## Process\n\n1. **Estimate current consumption** — sum of file reads + LLM responses + tool outputs + fixed overhead (CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution). Claude Code doesn't expose exact count, so estimation is practical. Use `.transcript-tokens` if available (per Track 8/9 telemetry).\n\n2. **Identify session type budget** — PLAN 80K / FOCUSED_IMPL 150K / MULTI_TASK_IMPL 250K / VERIFY 60K / RECOVERY 150K / THESIS 100K / INGEST 80K / POST-MORTEM 50K. Universal hard cap: 250K.\n\n3. **Project remaining work** — given current position in session plan: tasks remaining × estimated tokens per task → total remaining.\n\n4. **Compute status** — `usage_pct = estimated_used / budget_limit` ; `projected_total = estimated_used + estimated_remaining` ; `projection_pct = projected_total / budget_limit`.\n\n5. **Output status report** with sections: Current Session (type / started / elapsed) / Estimated Consumption (fixed + files + tool outputs + agent responses → total) / Budget Status (session budget / used / remaining + percent) / Projection (tasks still to do / avg per task / projected additional / projected total) / Status (GREEN / YELLOW / RED / OVER) / Recommendations.\n\n6. **Threshold actions** — `< 50%` normal proceed; `50-70%` caution, avoid unnecessary loads; `70-85%` finalize current task, no new major tasks; `> 85%` immediate handoff prep; `> 100% or > 250K` hard stop, emergency session end.\n\n7. **Hard cap enforcement** — if projected to exceed 250K (universal cap regardless of session type), output WARNING: BUDGET BREACH IMMINENT — projected total / 250K cap / cite Session 4 (300K+ tokens, 0 tasks completed) as measured evidence. Required action: stop at safe checkpoint, save state to session log, split remaining work to new session. Do NOT continue past 250K without explicit user override.\n\n## Observable Signals of High Usage\n\nEven without an exact count, these suggest high context:\n\n- Difficulty remembering early conversation\n- Re-reading files already read\n- Agent asking questions answered earlier\n- Responses getting shorter / less coherent\n\nIf observed → run `/budget-check` immediately.\n\n## Cost Awareness\n\nBudget isn't just quality — it's money. Claude Opus ~$15/M input tokens; Claude Sonnet ~$3/M; 250K session ≈ $3.75 (Opus) or $0.75 (Sonnet) per input pass. Keep sessions focused → cost stays reasonable.\n\n## Integration\n\n- Auto-check embedded in `/session-verify`\n- Manual check via this command\n- Hard-stop logic via `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh` (per CLAUDE.md context-threshold band: 180K wind-down / 220K cliff / 250K hard cap)\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Continuing past 250K because \"I'm almost done\" — quality degrades sharply (\"lost in middle\" effect; Session 4 evidence)\n- Skipping check on long sessions\n- Treating budget as advisory not enforcement\n\n## Do\n\n- Run periodically during long sessions\n- Treat 250K as hard ceiling, not soft\n- Wrap up cleanly when projected over budget — emergency handoff is more expensive than a clean split\n\n## Related\n\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` — canonical budgets per session type + thresholds\n- `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh` — automated wind-down / cliff / hard-cap signals\n- `/session-verify` — pairs with this command\n- `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/sessions-rollup.tsv` — observed token usage per session (per S19 aggregator)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":146,"newStart":1,"newLines":66,"lines":[" # /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status"," ","-> Report current session context consumption and project against budget.","+> Report current session context consumption and project against budget. Estimate Current Consumption\n\nMethod (rough):\n- Sum of all file reads performed\n- Sum of all LLM responses in session\n- Sum of all tool outputs\n- Plus fixed overhead from CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution\n\n(Claude Code doesn't expose exact count, so estimation is practical.)\n\n### 2. Identify Session Type\n\nFrom current session brief:\n- PLAN: budget 80K\n- FOCUSED_IMPL: budget 150K\n- MULTI_TASK_IMPL: budget 250K\n- VERIFY: budget 60K\n- RECOVERY: budget 150K\n- THESIS: budget 100K\n- INGEST: budget 80K\n- POST-MORTEM: budget 50K\n\n### 3. Project Remaining Work\n\nGiven current position in session plan:\n- Tasks remaining\n- Estimated token cost per remaining task\n- Total remaining work\n\n### 4. Compute Status\n\n```\nUsage percent = estimated_used / budget_limit\nProjected total = estimated_used + estimated_remaining\nProjection = projected_total / budget_limit\n```\n\n### 5. Output Status Report\n\n```markdown\n# Budget Check — [time]\n\n## Current Session\n- Type: [FOCUSED_IMPL]\n- Started: [timestamp]\n- Duration so far: [elapsed]\n\n## Estimated Consumption\n- Fixed overhead (CLAUDE.md + skills + constitution): ~12K\n- Files read this session: ~X K  \n- Tool outputs: ~Y K\n- Agent responses: ~Z K\n- **Total estimated**: ~Total K\n\n## Budget Status\n- Session budget: [150K]\n- Used: ~Total K ([percent]%)\n- Remaining: ~Remaining K\n\n## Projection for Remaining Work\n- Tasks still to do: N\n- Avg per task: ~K K\n- Projected additional: ~Additional K\n- **Projected total**: ~Grand K\n\n## Status\n[ GREEN ON TRACK | YELLOW CAUTION | RED AT RISK | OVER BUDGET ]\n\n## Recommendations\n[If green]: Continue as planned.\n[If yellow]: Avoid loading large new files. Consider finishing task before taking new one.\n[If red]: Wrap up current task, prepare for session end. Do not start new major work.\n[If over]: STOP. Emergency handoff. Split to new session.\n```\n\n### 6. Threshold Actions\n\n- **< 50% used**: normal, proceed\n- **50-70% used**: caution message, avoid unnecessary loads\n- **70-85% used**: finalize current task, no new major tasks\n- **> 85% used**: immediate handoff preparation\n- **> 100% / over 250K**: hard stop, emergency session end\n\n### 7. Hard Cap Enforcement\n\nIf projected to exceed 250K (universal hard cap regardless of type):\n\n```markdown\nWARNING: BUDGET BREACH IMMINENT\n\nProjected total: 270K tokens (exceeds 250K universal hard cap)\n\nMeasured evidence: quality degrades sharply past 250K (\"lost in middle\" effect).\nSession 4 in Phase2 project: 300K+ tokens, 0 tasks completed.\n\nAction required:\n1. **Stop current task at safe checkpoint**\n2. **Save state to session log**\n3. **Split remaining work to new session**\n\nI will not continue past 250K without explicit override from you.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Observable Signals of High Usage\n\nEven without exact count, these suggest high context:\n- Difficulty remembering early part of conversation\n- Needing to re-read files already read\n- Agent asking questions that were answered earlier\n- Responses getting shorter / less coherent\n\nIf observed → run `/budget-check` immediately.\n\n---\n\n## Integration\n\n- Automatic check embedded in `/session-verify`\n- Manual check via `/budget-check`\n- Hard stop logic can be added to hook (future)\n\n---\n\n## Cost Awareness\n\nBudget isn't just about quality — it's money.\n- Claude Opus: ~$15 per M tokens input\n- Claude Sonnet: ~$3 per M tokens input\n- 250K session = ~$3.75 (Opus) or ~$0.75 (Sonnet) per input pass\n\nKeep sessions focused → cost stays reasonable.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"945a9b4e-c2e8-4268-b2d0-dc9398989fab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Invoked when suspected drift or periodic audit.\n4\tmodel: sonnet\n5\ttools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\n6\t---\n7\t\n8\t# Subagent: Drift Detector\n9\t\n10\t## Persona\n11\t\n12\tStructural integrity inspector. Looks for slow decay across architectural boundaries.\n13\t\n14\tMindset: \"Code starts clean. Decays session by session. My job: catch decay early, before it's systemic.\"\n15\t\n16\t## Responsibility\n17\t\n18\tExecute full drift signal scan + semantic checks that simple grep can't catch:\n19\t- DR1-DR6: grep-based (also in /drift-check)\n20\t- DR7: UL semantic check\n21\t- DR8-DR10: cross-reference checks\n22\t- DR11: staleness check\n23\t- DR12: semantic anti-pattern detection (this requires LLM inspection)\n24\t\n25\t## Input\n26\t\n27\t- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` (definitions)\n28\t- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` (learned anti-patterns for DR12)\n29\t- Access do\n  grep -rn \"from packages.domain\\.\" packages/domain/$BC/ \\\n    --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"packages.domain.$BC\\.\"\ndone\n```\n\n### Phase 2: Semantic Signals (LLM-inspected)\n\n**DR7**: UL term drift (semantic check)\n\nThis requires understanding synonyms, not just exact match:\n- Does code use \"Report\" where glossary expects \"Thesis\"?\n- Does code use \"Fact\" where glossary expects \"Claim\"?\n- Does code use \"Score\" where glossary expects \"CredibilityScore\"?\n- Any variable name suggesting concept not in glossary?\n\nScan for:\n1. Class names / type names\n2. Variable names in domain code\n3. Event names\n4. Method names\n\nFor each, compare against glossary semantically.\n\n**DR12**: Anti-patterns from agent-notes.md\n\nRead `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`.\nFor each documented anti-pattern, search code:\n- Pattern: [description]\n- Search strategy: [grep pattern or semantic signature]\n- Findings: [file:line with details]\n\n**DR10**: Spec cross-references\n```bash\n# Extract all spec IDs referenced\ngrep -rhoE \"SPEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{3}\" . \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" --include=\"*.md\" 2>/dev/null | sort -u > /tmp/refs.txt\n\n# For each, check if file exists\nwhile read spec_id; do\n  found=$(find specs -name \"*${spec_id}*\" 2>/dev/null | head -1)\n  if [ -z \"$found\" ]; then\n    echo \"MISSING: $spec_id (referenced but not found)\"\n  fi\ndone < /tmp/refs.txt\n```\n\n**DR11**: Staleness\n```bash\n# Last modified of state files\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/project.md 2>/dev/null\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md 2>/dev/null\n\n# Compare with latest session\nLATEST_SESSION=$(ls -t agent-workspace/memory/sessions/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)\n# If project.md older than latest session, likely stale\n```\n\n### Phase 3: Synthesize Findings\n\nGroup by:\n- Severity (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW)\n- Location (file)\n- Drift type (DR number)\n\n### Phase 4: Write Report\n\n```markdown\n# Drift Detector Report — YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM\n\n## Summary\n- Signals run: 12\n- HIGH violations: X\n- MEDIUM violations: Y\n- LOW violations: Z\n\n## Status\n[CLEAN | WARNINGS | HIGH VIOLATIONS BLOCK MERGE]\n\n## HIGH Severity (blocks commit/merge)\n\n### DR1: Domain framework imports (2 violations)\n\n1. `packages/domain/analysis/thesis.py:12`\n   ```python\n   from fastapi import HTTPException  # VIOLATION\n   ```\n   Fix: Move to interfaces layer. Keep domain pure.\n\n2. `packages/domain/fundamental/ratio.py:8`\n   ```python\n   from pydantic import BaseModel  # VIOLATION\n   ```\n   Fix: Use stdlib dataclasses in domain. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. {"parentUuid":"6ec7ae85-a407-4115-aabf-e0ea6d6c4685","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01JzSkYRj8fJqSXuLGWNZ4tM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CsjkYW7KDNR4Aerz9YUBX5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\agents\\drift-detector.md","content":"---\nname: drift-detector\ndescription: Runs drift signals DR1-DR12 with adversarial eye. Deeper than /drift-check command — includes semantic inspection for DR7, DR12. Invoked when suspected drift or periodic audit.\nmodel: sonnet\ntools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\n---\n\n# Subagent: Drift Detector\n\n## Persona\n\nStructural integrity inspector. Looks for slow decay across architectural boundaries.\n\nMindset: *\"Code starts clean. Decays session by session. My job: catch decay early, before it's systemic.\"*\n\n## Responsibility\n\nExecute full drift signal scan + semantic checks that simple grep cannot catch:\n\n- DR1-DR6 — grep/sql-based (already covered by deterministic hook)\n- DR7 — UL semantic check (synonym detection)\n- DR8-DR10 — cross-reference checks (cross-BC imports, claim metadata, spec references)\n- DR11 — staleness check\n- DR12 — semantic anti-pattern detection from `agent-notes.md` (requires LLM inspection)\n\n## Input\n\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` (signal definitions, severity, remediation)\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` (learned anti-patterns for DR12)\n- Codebase access via Read / Glob / Grep / Bash\n\n## Process\n\n### Phase 1 — Run automated signals (DR1-DR6, DR8-DR11)\n\nInvoke `bash scripts/hooks/drift-signals-D1-D9.sh` for the full deterministic suite. The script handles framework imports / citation completeness / LLM-without-budget / hardcoded prompts / claim metadata / `Any` types / cross-BC imports / thesis-without-verifier / learning-data path leaks / staleness / spec cross-references. Capture stdout for inclusion in report.\n\nFor DR10 (spec cross-reference), the agent additionally extracts `SPEC-YYYY-MM-DD-NNN` references via `grep -rhoE` and verifies each lives under `specs/`. Report any missing.\n\nFor DR11 (staleness), compare `mtime` of `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` + `current-execution.md` vs latest `sessions/*.md`. Project.md older than latest session = likely stale.\n\n### Phase 2 — Semantic signals (DR7, DR12)\n\n**DR7 — UL term drift (semantic)** — read `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`. For each term, scan code (class names, type names, variable names in domain code, event names, method names). Use semantic comparison, not just exact match: code uses `Report` where glossary expects `Thesis`? `Fact` where canonical is `Claim`? `Score` where canonical is `CredibilityScore`? Variable name suggesting a concept not in glossary?\n\n**DR12 — Anti-pattern detection** — read `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. For each documented anti-pattern: pattern description / search strategy (grep pattern OR semantic signature) / actual findings (file:line with details).\n\n### Phase 3 — Synthesize findings\n\nGroup by: severity (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW), location (file), drift type (DR number).\n\n### Phase 4 — Write report\n\nSave to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/drift-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md` with sections:\n\n- **Summary** — signals run / HIGH count / MEDIUM count / LOW count\n- **Status** — `CLEAN` | `WARNINGS` | `HIGH VIOLATIONS BLOCK MERGE`\n- **HIGH severity** — per signal, list violations with file:line + code snippet (3-5 lines) + suggested fix\n- **MEDIUM severity** — same shape, \"fix this session or next\"\n- **LOW severity** — same shape, advisory tracking\n- **Trend Analysis** — vs previous report: new violations / resolved since last / persistent (3+ reports)\n- **Recommendations** — split: Block-merge (HIGH) / Fix-this-session (MEDIUM) / Track-for-later (LOW) / Constitutional (should DR-N tighten? add stop-list?)\n\n### Phase 5 — Update drift log\n\nUpdate `agent-workspace/memory/drift-logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with one-line summary linking to full report.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Run ALL 12 signals, not a subset\n- Cite `file:line` for every violation\n- Distinguish severity accurately (HIGH blocks merge, MEDIUM blocks session close, LOW informational)\n- **Do not auto-fix** — report only; remediation requires user explicit approve\n- Semantic checks (DR7, DR12) require actual inspection — not just grep — and are the highest-value findings\n\n## Do NOT\n\n- Auto-fix violations\n- Skip semantic signals because \"harder\"\n- Report false positives (verify each finding before listing)\n- Ignore DR12 (learned rules from agent-notes.md are most valuable)\n\n## Related\n\n- `/drift-check` — user-facing command that may invoke this agent\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` — canonical definitions\n- `scripts/hooks/drift-signals-D1-D9.sh` — deterministic recipes (Phase 1)\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` — DR12 source rules\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":12083,"cache_read_input_tokens":269086,"output_tokens":2262,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":12083,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":2262,"cache_read_input_tokens":269086,"cache_creation_input_tokens":12083,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":12083},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYUa9HXjBdxWXUAvMnxb","type":"assistant","uuid":"0d7a5858-b2e5-44d0-9e3b-d65b058445f5","timestamp":"2026-04-29T17:42:58.408Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

Deeper than /drift-check command — includes semantic inspection for DR7, DR12. Invoked when suspected drift or periodic audit.\nmodel: sonnet\ntools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\n---\n\n# Subagent: Drift Detector\n\n## Persona\n\nStructural integrity inspector. Looks for slow decay across architectural boundaries.\n\nMindset: \"Code starts clean. Decays session by session. My job: catch decay early, before it's systemic.\"\n\n## Responsibility\n\nExecute full drift signal scan + semantic checks that simple grep can't catch:\n- DR1-DR6: grep-based (also in /drift-check)\n- DR7: UL semantic check\n- DR8-DR10: cross-reference checks\n- DR11: staleness check\n- DR12: semantic anti-pattern detection (this requires LLM inspection)\n\n## Input\n\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` (definitions)\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` (learned anti-patterns for DR12)\n- Access to codebase\n\n## Process\n\n### Phase 1: Run Automated Signals\n\nExecute grep/script signals from `drift-signals.md`:\n\n**DR1**: Domain layer framework imports\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"from fastapi\\|import fastapi\\|from pydantic\\|import pydantic\\|from sqlalchemy\\|import sqlalchemy\" \\\n  packages/domain/ --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n```\n\n**DR2**: Evidence without citation (if DB accessible)\n```sql\nSELECT id, text FROM claims WHERE source_url IS NULL OR source_url = '';\n```\n\n**DR3**: LLM call without budget/retry\n```bash\ngrep -rn \"anthropic\\.Anthropic\\|client\\.messages\\.create\\|openai\\.OpenAI\" packages/infrastructure/ \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"with_budget\\|with_retry\"\n```\n\n**DR4**: Large inline prompts outside prompts/\n```bash\n# Heuristic: long triple-quoted strings in Python files outside prompts/\ngrep -rEn '\"\"\"[^\"]{500,}\"\"\"' packages/application/ apps/ \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"prompts/\"\n```\n\n**DR5**: Claim missing required metadata (SQL — if accessible)\n\n**DR6**: `Any` types in domain\n```bash\ngrep -rn \": Any\\|-> Any\\| Any,\" packages/domain/ \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"test_\\|_test\"\n```\n\n**DR8**: Cross-BC direct imports\n```bash\nfor BC in market_data fundamental company_intelligence macro news influence crowd analysis portfolio; do\n  grep -rn \"from packages.domain\\.\" packages/domain/$BC/ \\\n    --include=\"*.py\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v \"packages.domain.$BC\\.\"\ndone\n```\n\n### Phase 2: Semantic Signals (LLM-inspected)\n\n**DR7**: UL term drift (semantic check)\n\nThis requires understanding synonyms, not just exact match:\n- Does code use \"Report\" where glossary expects \"Thesis\"?\n- Does code use \"Fact\" where glossary expects \"Claim\"?\n- Does code use \"Score\" where glossary expects \"CredibilityScore\"?\n- Any variable name suggesting concept not in glossary?\n\nScan for:\n1. Class names / type names\n2. Variable names in domain code\n3. Event names\n4. Method names\n\nFor each, compare against glossary semantically.\n\n**DR12**: Anti-patterns from agent-notes.md\n\nRead `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`.\nFor each documented anti-pattern, search code:\n- Pattern: [description]\n- Search strategy: [grep pattern or semantic signature]\n- Findings: [file:line with details]\n\n**DR10**: Spec cross-references\n```bash\n# Extract all spec IDs referenced\ngrep -rhoE \"SPEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{3}\" . \\\n  --include=\"*.py\" --include=\"*.md\" 2>/dev/null | sort -u > /tmp/refs.txt\n\n# For each, check if file exists\nwhile read spec_id; do\n  found=$(find specs -name \"*${spec_id}*\" 2>/dev/null | head -1)\n  if [ -z \"$found\" ]; then\n    echo \"MISSING: $spec_id (referenced but not found)\"\n  fi\ndone < /tmp/refs.txt\n```\n\n**DR11**: Staleness\n```bash\n# Last modified of state files\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/project.md 2>/dev/null\nstat -c \"%Y %n\" agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md 2>/dev/null\n\n# Compare with latest session\nLATEST_SESSION=$(ls -t agent-workspace/memory/sessions/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)\n# If project.md older than latest session, likely stale\n```\n\n### Phase 3: Synthesize Findings\n\nGroup by:\n- Severity (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW)\n- Location (file)\n- Drift type (DR number)\n\n### Phase 4: Write Report\n\n```markdown\n# Drift Detector Report — YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM\n\n## Summary\n- Signals run: 12\n- HIGH violations: X\n- MEDIUM violations: Y\n- LOW violations: Z\n\n## Status\n[CLEAN | WARNINGS | HIGH VIOLATIONS BLOCK MERGE]\n\n## HIGH Severity (blocks commit/merge)\n\n### DR1: Domain framework imports (2 violations)\n\n1. `packages/domain/analysis/thesis.py:12`\n   ```python\n   from fastapi import HTTPException  # VIOLATION\n   ```\n   Fix: Move to interfaces layer. Keep domain pure.\n\n2. `packages/domain/fundamental/ratio.py:8`\n   ```python\n   from pydantic import BaseModel  # VIOLATION\n   ```\n   Fix: Use stdlib dataclasses in domain. Pydantic only in interfaces/infrastructure.\n\n### DR8: Cross-BC imports (1 violation)\n[...]\n\n## MEDIUM Severity (fix this session or next)\n\n### DR3: LLM calls without budget wrapper (3 violations)\n[...]\n\n### DR7: UL semantic drift (1 violation)\n- `packages/domain/analysis/thesis.py` uses `Report` in method names\n- Canonical term: `Thesis`\n- Impact: future maintenance confusion\n- Fix: Rename methods to use `Thesis`\n\n## LOW Severity (tracked)\n\n### DR11: Staleness (advisory)\n- `project.md` last modified 2026-04-15\n- Latest session: 2026-04-20-session-12.md\n- Project.md may not reflect current state\n\n## Trend Analysis (vs previous report)\n\n[If previous drift report exists]\n- New violations: N\n- Resolved since last: M\n- Persistent (3+ reports): P\n\n## Recommendations\n\n### Block merge until resolved\n- [HIGH violations]\n\n### Fix this session\n- [MEDIUM violations]\n\n### Track for later\n- [LOW violations]\n\n### Constitutional Considerations\n- Should DR3 be tightened to pre-commit hook?\n- Should DR7 have stop-list rule added?\n```\n\n### Phase 5: Save Report\n\nSave to `agent-workspace/quality-reports/drift-reports/drift-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md`.\n\nUpdate `agent-workspace/memory/drift-logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with summary.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Run ALL signals, not just some\n- Cite file:line for every violation\n- Distinguish severity accurately\n- Don't fix violations (report only)\n- Semantic checks (DR7, DR12) require actual inspection, not just grep\n\n## Do NOT\n\n- Auto-fix violations\n- Skip semantic signals because \"harder\"\n- Report false positives (verify each finding)\n- Ignore DR12 (learned rules are most valuable)\n\n## Related\n\n- Command: /drift-check\n- Constitution: drift-signals.md\n- Agent notes: memory/agent-notes.md (DR12 source)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0d7a5858-b2e5-44d0-9e3b-d65b058445f5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"302fc447-cdb8-4e0e-bae6-af6f07ebadcd","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
